# [It's our campaign-iversary!](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=6380051&post_id=195063798&utm_source=post-email-title&utm_campaign=email-post-title&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTk1MDYzNzk4LCJpYXQiOjE3NzY5MDI1MzMsImV4cCI6MTc3OTQ5NDUzMywiaXNzIjoicHViLTYzODAwNTEiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.ZE7WguolZ_5Qnto2DQ8PBQORB-bIBQnb1OPtlgrkVbg)
### One year ago today, I launched my campaign for the U.S. Senate.
| | [Haley Stevens](https://substack.com/@haleyformi)
---
| Apr 23
---
| [](https://substack.com/@haleyformi)
---

---
| | | [](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9vcGVuLnN1YnN0YWNrLmNvbS9wdWIvaGFsZXlmb3JtaS9wL2l0cy1vdXItY2FtcGFpZ24taXZlcnNhcnk_.-oMYocxPUQJGdefWKUkplV6R-dYDmPd5Lj5jrWKkfV8?&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email)
---
| | [READ IN APP](https://open.substack.com/pub/haleyformi/p/its-our-campaign-iversary?utm_source=email&redirect=app-store&utm_campaign=email-read-in-app)
---

Friends,
We've come a long way since launching this campaign one year ago.
Together, we have built more than just a campaign to keep Michigan blue. We've built a movement that is by the people, for the people, focused on all the things that make our state beautiful.
Grit. Hard work. Determination. Our core values of listening to your neighbor, learning from your community, and then leading with the same doggedness that built this state brick by brick.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/2b3df7c0-74b0-47f3-bf50-b14aa9fdb6a6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**[That's what I'm most proud of, friends.](https://substack.com/redirect/9427a5fe-92a2-43d5-b3d4-f45046978560?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Even as I see the polling numbers -- which show that I'm in a statistical tie with Mike Rogers -- it never leaves my mind that all of this is because of folks like you.
The folks who have been with us since Day One. The folks who just came across this campaign and knew straight away that a Hope Agenda is exactly what our state needs. The folks who have believed in me enough to chip in to this campaign, to fill out surveys, to knock on doors, and to talk to friends and family members about this race.
**[We've got a long way to go yet.](https://substack.com/redirect/9427a5fe-92a2-43d5-b3d4-f45046978560?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** The GOP is dead set on taking this seat, and they're throwing everything they've got at us to try to buy this seat.
But since Day One, we've proven that this campaign has what it takes to win. Polls have consistently shown that I'm the candidate who can win for Democrats, keep this seat blue, and help flip the Senate.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/3d96462b-5583-4642-9e37-d3998c5092f7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
From now until November, I'm going to be giving this campaign my all to make sure we keep up this momentum so we can continue building something Michiganders can be proud of.
And bring home the win on Nov. 3.
[Thank you for being in this with me, friends. You're the backbone of this campaign, and I couldn't be more grateful.](https://substack.com/redirect/9427a5fe-92a2-43d5-b3d4-f45046978560?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
With grit and gratitude,
Haley
* * *

A personal note from Haley 👋

I'm a lifelong Michigander and the daughter of small-business owners. I've spent my career fighting for Michigan's working families - and now I'm running for the U.S. Senate to keep standing up for the people I love.

But here's the truth: Senate control could come down to Michigan. And Trump and his megadonors know it. That's why they're gearing up to spend tens of millions to defeat me and hand this seat to a MAGA Republican.

I need your help to fight back. This race will be one of the most competitive - and expensive - in the country, and I'm counting on grassroots support to win.

If you're with me, will you chip in today?
[Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/9427a5fe-92a2-43d5-b3d4-f45046978560?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

Stats like this from California are the canary in the coal mine, Team. Kern County went from 332 uncounted, late ballots in 2024 to 3,303 in 2025. In Riverside County it was almost 6,000 uncounted, late ballots, more than double 2024's total.
Remember: These are from eligible voters, postmarked on time, sent ahead of or on Election Day. They should have counted -- except Trump's changes to the USPS made them arrive too late.
MAGA is trying every trick in the book to end the use of mail-in ballots or make them not count. RUSH $35 or whatever you can to help us reach voters in time to make every voice heard in the midterms and beyond >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?refcode=042226_3&amount=35]
Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
LA Times: California election experts sound alarm as rate of rejected ballots quadruples [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?refcode=042226_3&amount=25]
Here's the deal, Team: Due to USPS changes , a huge number of mail-in ballots arrived too late to be counted in last year's special election in California.
A review by the Los Angeles Times showed that " ballots came in late at an average rate four times higher than that of the 2024 election ." By California law, vote-by-mail ballots are considered late if they do not arrive within seven days of election day, even if they are postmarked on or ahead of election day.
What does this mean? There is now concrete proof that Trump's changes to the U.S. Postal Service are aiding his attacks on mail-in voting . California voters did their job and mailed their ballot in accordance with their laws. Trump's attacks on the Postal Service aren't letting them deliver those ballots on time.
Team, every voter needs to know about this massive problem. Will you pitch in $35 or whatever you can today and help us spread the word about the USPS changes so we can protect mail-in ballots? >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?refcode=042226_3&amount=35]

Election officials warned before that 2025 special election that the Postal Service changes could delay the postmarking of ballots and lead to votes not being counted. Trump's USPS leadership shrugged after reducing the number of post office pickups in a quest for "efficiency".
“ Something changed ,” said Melvin E. Levey, who heads the Merced County Registrar of Voters. “ We don’t like seeing late ballots and if someone has made the effort to vote, we want to count it .” Semi-rural Merced County saw almost a sevenfold increase in late-arriving mail ballots in the November election compared with the year before.
We have to make sure every voter understands this change and how it can impact them -- from vote-by-mail, to bills, taxes, legal replies to companies, so much more. What Americans think is the mailing deadline may not be the deadline anymore and that's a huge deal that's generally being under-reported by the media.
Every vote should count, especially those postmarked and mailed ahead of or on election day. Pitch in $35 to help us make that a reality by informing voters about these USPS changes and holding USPS leadership accountable to Americans who deserve on this vital service >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?refcode=042226_3&amount=35]

I’ll get straight to it.
A new poll shows Zach Wahls trailing Republican Ashley Hinson by just 2 points.
In a statewide Senate race. In Iowa!
If Democrats are going to retake the majority, it will require winning races exactly like this one. That’s why I’m asking you to split a donation between Zach Wahls and Resist Reclaim Rebuild right now. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-wahls]
DONATE NOW TO FLIP IOWA BLUE! >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-wahls]
Here’s the math: Democrats need a net gain to retake the Senate majority. There are only a handful of true pickup opportunities in the entire country this cycle, and this poll shows that Iowa is one of them.
Trump carried the state by double digits in 2024, but now, Wahls has narrowed that lead to 2. That’s why this race matters so much.
As someone who has spent a lot of time campaigning in Iowa, I know Zach has what it takes to win. Zach isn’t some placeholder candidate. He’s a 6th-generation Iowan who has spent his career standing up for working families and taking on powerful interests. He’s built real grassroots support without taking a cent from corporate PACs.
And now he’s within 2 points.
But here’s what I’ve learned over decades in politics: when a Democrat gets this close in a red-leaning state, national Republicans don’t sit back. They flood the zone with money and try to shut it down early.
If Zach has the resources to define this race, expand outreach, and reach persuadable voters before outside money drowns him out, he can win. If he doesn’t, Republicans will try to bury this opportunity before it fully takes shape.
Zach can win this race. But he cannot do it alone.
If you care about Democrats retaking the Senate, I’m asking you to split a contribution between Zach Wahls’ campaign and Resist Reclaim Rebuild today. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-wahls]
CHIP IN TODAY TO HELP DEMS WIN! >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-wahls]
Iowa is in play. Let’s not miss this opportunity.
Howard Dean

body:
I wanted to reach out personally to share something with you today.
# [](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1269?t=1&akid=3151%2E21716%2EQ-Fvbd)
When I think about the work we’re doing in Congress, what inspires me the most is the people. Grassroots supporters like you who are committed to fighting for a Delaware where everyone has a chance to thrive.
That’s why I wanted to reach out personally to share something with you today.
**Right now, our average online donation is just $38.50.**
That number means something to me because it tells a story. Of a teacher in Wilmington pitching in what they can after a long day of educating our kids. A small business owner in Dover who believes we can grow our economy while protecting workers’ rights at the same time. A young community organizer in Newark who wants to see leaders in government with an agenda that’s rooted in dignity, fairness, and care.
**This is what our movement is made of.** We’re sustained by everyday people who believe in what we can do when courage and compassion drive our work.
I don’t answer to big money, I answer to my neighbors in Delaware. Every vote I cast and every bill I sponsor in Congress is grounded in the belief that government should serve everyone, not just the wealthy few at the top.
[**With all that said, will you chip in $38.50 or anything you can spare today to help power my campaign? Meeting our fundraising goals is critical to keep me fighting for Delaware families in Congress.**](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1420?c0=mcb-em-20260422-2.ueV6BN&refcode=em20260422-3151&t=2&akid=3151%2E21716%2EQ-Fvbd)

Thank you for being a part of this movement with me.
With gratitude,
Sarah McBride

| Dear Peter, Did you know even 10 year olds are concerned about the price of gas? At a recent event I noticed a boy in the audience (can’t get them exposed to civic engagement too early - great job, Mom!). I asked him what his biggest concern was in the world today. His answer: the price of gas. I was surprised! He said that his mom and his sister complain everyday about how much it costs them to drive him back and forth to practice. This struck me because even children feel the economic crisis we are facing. When I think about how many of us can’t afford to live where we work, how many hours we spend commuting to work, and all of the stress of traffic, I worry about what this does to our spendable income, mental health, physical health and quality of life. A contract driver I met recently said he’s not even making minimum wage anymore because the price of gas has gone up so much. Transportation and production are immediately impacted which then limits spending overall, hurting our local economies. The high cost of fuel impacts more and more of our daily lives, way beyond the gas station. clean_body: | = = | Dear Peter, Did you know even 10 year olds are concerned about the price of gas? At a recent event I noticed a boy in the audience (can’t get them exposed to civic engagement too early - great job, Mom!). I asked him what his biggest concern was in the world today. His answer: the price of gas. I was surprised! He said that his mom and his sister complain everyday about how much it costs them to drive him back and forth to practice. This struck me because even children feel the economic crisis we are facing. When I think about how many of us can’t afford to live where we work, how many hours we spend commuting to work, and all of the stress of traffic, I worry about what this does to our spendable income, mental health, physical health and quality of life. A contract driver I met recently said he’s not even making minimum wage anymore because the price of gas has gone up so much. Transportation and production are immediately impacted which then limits spending overall, hurting our local economies. The high cost of fuel impacts more and more of our daily lives, way beyond the gas station. I realize times are tough for so many – it is critical that we unite and give of our time, talent and treasure sacrificially. Please=. Every dollar brings us one step closer to a government that truly represents and serves everyone. Thank you for your time, your faith in a just and humane future, and your support. body:
No one should have to second-guess the water coming out of their tap or worry about what their kids are breathing in. Peter,

Earth Day comes around once a year, but Wesley is fighting to protect our environment every single day.

No one should have to second-guess the water coming out of their tap or worry about what their kids are breathing in. And no community should be left dealing with the consequences while polluters walk away without being held accountable.

That's why Wesley has been pushing in Congress for stronger protections for clean air and clean water, real enforcement against polluters, and investments that actually reach the communities that have been ignored for too long. _And it's why his work is getting recognized._

**Wesley is proudly endorsed by the League of Conservation Voters** — a national organization that has spent decades holding polluters and anti-environment politicians accountable, electing climate champions, and fighting for policies that protect clean air, clean water, and public health across the country. **Their endorsement is a testament to their trust in this campaign, because he will always stand up to special interests and deliver real environmental progress.**

But getting things done in Congress takes resources, especially when we're up against deep-pocketed special interests who are willing to sacrifice our environment to further their agenda, no matter the cost. Wesley believes we have the power to take them on and build something better at the same time. Investing in clean energy means creating good-paying union jobs right here at home. It means growing our economy in a way that actually works for people — and for our planet.

Peter, Earth Day comes around once a year, but Wesley is fighting to protect our environment every single day. No one should have to second-guess the water coming out of their tap or worry about what their kids are breathing in. And no community should be left dealing with the consequences while polluters walk away without being held accountable. That's why Wesley has been pushing in Congress for stronger protections for clean air and clean water, real enforcement against polluters, and investments that actually reach the communities that have been ignored for too long. And it's why his work is getting recognized. Wesley is proudly endorsed by the League of Conservation Voters — a national organization that has spent decades holding polluters and anti-environment politicians accountable, electing climate champions, and fighting for policies that protect clean air, clean water, and public health across the country. Their endorsement is a testament to their trust in this campaign, because he will always stand up to special interests and deliver real environmental progress. But getting things done in Congress takes resources, especially when we're up against deep-pocketed special interests who are willing to sacrifice our environment to further their agenda, no matter the cost. Wesley believes we have the power to take them on and build something better at the same time. Investing in clean energy means creating good-paying union jobs right here at home. | | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

clean_body: Right now President Trump has one on the US Secret Service. | | | Don't want to receive our publications? | | | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18] | | | | | Right now President Trump has one on the US Secret Service. Peter, I just stepped off the stage from the first debate of this race for governor, and I want to tell you exactly what I saw up there.
**There were two very different visions for California.**
I’m fighting for working families—people stretched thin by skyrocketing costs, students buried in debt, parents struggling to afford child care.
The other candidates? _They’re fighting for themselves._
Steyer is a self-funding billionaire trying to buy his way into this race. Becerra took tens of thousands from Big Oil. And the two Republicans in this race are trying to bring Trump’s MAGA agenda to California.
_I’ve spent my career calling out exactly this kind of behavior._ When I bring out a whiteboard, it’s not for show—it’s because facts matter. People can see exactly who’s looking out for them and who isn’t.
As governor, I’ll do the same thing. I’m fighting for tuition-free public college, single-payer health care, eliminating state income tax for those earning under $100,000, and universal child care so parents don’t have to choose between a paycheck and their kids.
**The bottom line is I don’t take corporate PAC money, I’m not self-funding my campaign, and I’m not here to protect the status quo. I’m here to change it.**
California’s primary is coming up fast, and only the top two candidates move on to November. If we’re going to win this, we need to make sure we’re one of them.

Our Glenrock Meet & Greet at the Higgins Hotel had a great turnout!

While we were in Douglas, Kelly and I had the opportunity to check out East=
ern Wyoming College Douglas Campus. Really cool to see the Nursing program,=
the Gunsmithing program, and the progress on their new Construction buildi=
ng. Lots of good things happening out there.

ul questions (and fresh off a successful FFA state convention), then we wer=
e off to Guernsey for stops at the VFW and Senior Center, where we had a st=
rong conversation about property tax concerns.

le Kelly met up with a great group and had a well-attended meet and greet i=
n Lusk. It is always appreciate hearing directly from folks across our comm=
unities.

Kelly and I had a great stop at Eastern Wyoming College and had a great tou=
r of Ag Technology and the new trailers they will be sending out to communi=
ties around Wyoming to help teach.

We had a good Meet and Greet at The Old Moose Coffee shop was well attended=
and great questions were asked!

Cheyenne
We were able to stop by for a visit with the leadership, staff and board of=
the Wyoming Association of Municipalities (WAM) in Cheyenne.

We had a great=C2=A0discussion on economic development in the region and th=
e work WAM is doing for collaboration across the state.

A great time with Cheyenne folks this week! The meet & greet at The Hawthor=
n Tree showed a great turnout, and Patron Night at the Old West Museum did =
not disappoint. We ended the night with a local meetup and lots of good con=
versation, hosted by friends Tony and Sandy Ross, with help from Diane Shob=
er.
Thanks to everyone who made our visit great.

Thank you to Denise and Roz as well as Larry Barttelbort who helped with hi=
s wife Susie for gathering friends for a meeting while we were in town.

# **[Want to live to 100? Don't expect Big Pharma to help.](http://trk.libertyledger._c2V5aWQ9In0/TcpJOpdcdfcRHkYPtvV--w)**
---
A few years ago, surgeries and medications helped heal my broken body after a terrible accident. I was grateful for the modern medical system’s capabilities as eight broken ribs, a clavicle that was in five pieces, and a collapsed lung were treated and healed. What would have been miracles of biblical proportions 50 years ago were a process that allowed me to go back to work within months.The pharmaceutical drugs that got my body on the road to healing were a big part of that success. As a chiropractor with almost two decades in the field, I have seen medications, drugs, and related treatments do wonders, especially after an accident, surgery, birth, or some other significant medical event.

subject: “There’s more than one way to skin a cat around here”
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Jamie Davis for U
body:
That is how a Republican senator described stopping a black man from taking his elected seat.
| | | | | [](https://r6msg8hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001kw7OT0eaCSw7cL0AvANY-nkmLExB637EqMyo92XgrRAr0l--EULaMp41YegvhgzYqRQL4jiLcPsg3JlM7GeHAhedt7Pv-7i9oujKohLvVM6uhC-KrHu2_fqQGA1zH9s05HWZhQsliafBkO6kZOCo-0GOkW0THFv1i348sSyOMP2Jp-Elo-ghST9qhjJiwe5dlTC-enpcj24NC7t7imFSnkwdLambFuwe&c=s1zIciOWMcupqhALz61b5RHCjiyuce5D8NSqAy1j1JXQgM9vGnS-gg==&ch=yk9dmTv5mtQ1BAEi8m1Ny2veUiiNoGMqMmewDxb11smV2NK6Xv4FxA==)
---
Peter, In a recent Louisiana State House hearing, Republican State Senator Jay Morris said the quiet part out loud when asked why he introduced multiple bills to remove a Black man from an elected seat before he was even sworn in:
---
| [](https://r6msg8hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001kw7OT0eaCSw7cL0AvANY-nkmLExB637EqMyo92XgrRAr0l--EULaMp41YegvhgzYqRQL4jiLcPsg3JlM7GeHAhedt7Pv-7i9oujKohLvVM6uhC-KrHu2_fqQGA1zH9s05HWZhQsliafBkO6kZOCo-0GOkW0THFv1i348sSyOMP2Jp-Elo-ghST9qhjJiwe5dlTC-enpcj26KhMI_Gcj5ObW-qKwAVQ94&c=s1zIciOWMcupqhALz61b5RHCjiyuce5D8NSqAy1j1JXQgM9vGnS-gg==&ch=yk9dmTv5mtQ1BAEi8m1Ny2veUiiNoGMqMmewDxb11smV2NK6Xv4FxA==)
---
"There's more than one way to skin a cat around here."
What he is actually saying is that there is more than one way to strip a duly elected Black man from the position he was democratically elected to.
This is not new. Louisiana has a long history of blocking Black men (especially those representing the interests of Black people) from taking office, even after they win.
In the New Orleans City Court, there have always been two clerks:
One handles civil cases. One handles criminal cases.
Now a MAGA Senator is doing everything in his power to eliminate the Criminal Clerk of Court seat in New Orleans. This is not about eliminating the Criminal Clerk of Court in New Orleans. This is about stopping Calvin Duncan.
---
| [](https://r6msg8hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001kw7OT0eaCSw7cL0AvANY-nkmLExB637EqMyo92XgrRAr0l--EULaMp41YegvhgzYqRQL4jiLcPsg3JlM7GeHAhedt7Pv-7i9oujKohLvVM6uhC-KrHu2_fqQGA1zH9s05HWZhQsliafBkO6kZOCo-0GOkW0THFv1i348sSyOMP2Jp-Elo-ghST9qhjJiwe5dlTC-enpcj24sscvnuf21MSk2FxeSbkDL&c=s1zIciOWMcupqhALz61b5RHCjiyuce5D8NSqAy1j1JXQgM9vGnS-gg==&ch=yk9dmTv5mtQ1BAEi8m1Ny2veUiiNoGMqMmewDxb11smV2NK6Xv4FxA==)
---
Calvin Duncan is not just anyone. He was wrongfully convicted as a teenager and sentenced to death row. He taught himself law from inside a prison cell. He fought for his freedom, and he won. He then went on to graduate from college and law school.
And then the people of New Orleans elected him, with 68% of the vote, because he promised something simple:
He would work to make sure that what happened to him would never happen to anyone else.
That promise is why these Republican legislators, at the direction of the MAGA movement, are trying to stop him.
An accountable, transparent criminal court system threatens a system that seems to care little about getting it wrong. Louisiana leads the nation in incarceration.
We have a system where prison labor is contracted for pennies - two cents an hour. A system where more people fall through the cracks and are denied justice, the more laborers the state has, the more profit for their "prison enterprises."
Calvin Duncan threatened that racist system. And MAGA is fighting to protect it.
We're going to make damn sure that the good people of Louisiana remember this when it is time to vote in the coming midterms.
[My name is Jamie Davis, and I'm the Democrat running for the United States Senate in Louisiana. If MAGA didn't like Calvin Duncan, then they're going to hate me. Because I believe people who know how broken this system is deserve a seat at the table--not to be shut out of it. Will you join the fight to help me overcome injustice and win this crucial Senate race?](https://r6msg8hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001kw7OT0eaCSw7cL0AvANY-nkmLExB637EqMyo92XgrRAr0l--EULaMp41YegvhgzYIhk-AVZ5hTYl3vimv6Dm5DR_gfEATduGnUamZnjF-JjnaOXEK52VMsU_x2dfu7Vk89BEz18zoyy9Hy2cN6U7E1JlW2G3N1-fBJ4JYGksWXMiiP_w_l_zhXwrSlxLI_XlNKaQAV-F7bfW38rkO5txzO3hGVcGi1oq_OaIJQt9UI4=&c=s1zIciOWMcupqhALz61b5RHCjiyuce5D8NSqAy1j1JXQgM9vGnS-gg==&ch=yk9dmTv5mtQ1BAEi8m1Ny2veUiiNoGMqMmewDxb11smV2NK6Xv4FxA==)

name: Senator Tom Willis
subject: My Opponent Has Lost Her Way
body:

# My Opponent Has Lost Her Way

---
|
---
|
---
| |
Dear Friend,
West Virginians believe in something simple:
* **Faith.**

* **Family.**

* **Freedom.**

But somewhere along the way, **my opponent lost her way** — and it’s not hard to see why.
This isn’t just about votes in Washington.
It’s about **values** — and whether those values still reflect West Virginia.
Take the Second Amendment:
While **she supported red flag gun confiscation funding — putting your rights at risk without due process** **—** **I’ve earned an "A" rating from the NRA — the highest of any U.S. Senate candidate in West Virginia.**
**That’s a big difference.**
And it’s not the only one.
Time and again, she’s taken positions that don’t line up with the people of this state:
* She voted against **traditional marriage — one man and one woman.**

* She’s **flip-flopped on abortion** and backed **taxpayer funding for Planned Parenthood.**

* She failed to stand up for **protecting girls’ sports.**

* She didn’t push for the **SAVE Act — ensuring only American citizens vote in American elections.**

**That’s not where West Virginia stands.**
And it goes beyond policy.
**While you work hard to get ahead, she’s looked out for herself and her circle:**
* **A top insider trader in the U.S. Senate**

* **Helped secure her son’s appointment as U.S. Attorney — then voted for him**

**That’s not putting West Virginia first.**
And some of these decisions have real consequences:
* **Unvetted refugee resettlement.**

* **Attempts to expand government control over online speech.**

**These aren’t isolated votes — they’re a pattern.**
And people here see it.
Because West Virginians still believe:
* **One nation under God.**

* **Strong families.**

* **Parents — not government — raising their children.**

But too often, politicians go to Washington and forget who they represent.
They follow pressure.
They follow politics.
They follow the crowd.
**I won’t.**
I’m a Christian, a husband, and a father raising my family right here in West Virginia.
**I’ve served this state for decades — as a U.S. Army Special Forces Green Beret, in business, and in the State Senate.**
**As a Green Beret, I learned how to make tough decisions under pressure, stand firm in the face of opposition, and see the mission through.**
**Our values don’t change when you get elected.****
They matter even more.**
I’m running to put **West Virginia first again** — not Washington agendas, not special interests, not political convenience.
And you can count on me to fight for:
* **Securing our border**

* **Investing in West Virginia infrastructure**

* **Lowering costs by cutting government overreach**

**This race comes down to a simple choice:**
**Do you want more of the same from a career politician — or a proven conservative with real experience who will stand and fight for West Virginia?**
**If you believe it’s time for a Senator who stands firm — not one who’s lost her way —**
**Vote Tom Willis on May 12.**
**IT’S TIME FOR A CHANGE, WEST VIRGINIA.**
**Tom Willis**

## Iran Seizes Ships as Ceasefire Teeters
Iran's Revolutionary Guard [fired on at least two vessels](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkD1u6zAQhE9DdRTopX6ogsVr1Pm1KYW1uLQ2pkSDosU4pw-UK6QcDDCD7_u4TlfkwNv9P65ks4_TRmUPlDOlaY57jj4h77zd8cHu5ePBjuIECjqpGgl6csjhPTWVs54ISFdkL33fDdoY0NVilQcA9Ma3HerWmbaH2aAejMfW6G6o2J5rqgF9UapXqlboPKLxRpmhwVsrGkWOc0z1Z-QtL-TDOx6U6jmuVbBLzs9d6H8CRgFjKaX28eukOHsBY-CD5JkFjJxwk69dFkzyFuL8QEdyiWl9fUt8Jg4SoErWPQuHwHvXi0bdV-Tw-5X_JOiw8BMAAP__N-l7LQ) in the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday and took custody of both ships, the first such seizures since the war began. Iran's parliament speaker called the U.S. blockade a "flagrant breach" of the ceasefire. President Trump, who extended the ceasefire Tuesday after a planned second round of peace talks in Pakistan fell apart, said Wednesday there is "no time pressure" on a deal and that the blockade "scares them more than bombing." Trump also announced that Iran [agreed to spare eight women protesters](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGS4yAQRL8GMrnwgBEKCC5R5ksvVM2JwZo7BC7A9vrvt7S1f7Bxv-qufn-uyxU5cb79xp18j2XJ9GqJeqe6rKX1Eity43zD_xwesTw5UFlAgR2UGUAvATm9FyODj0RAWpI_j6OdtHOg5eanyWhrVzNNlmwYiS4KnbYQ4-osQJTsjzZlQJ-VGpU6KQwR0UWn3GTw70UYRYF7qad_hXPfKKZ3eVI9rWWXyW-935vQvwTMAua-0cYpHZmAeSs7HYcEzBh2ztx6xc4lC5gvzmjtzMAVM2MeXgc7tDtWCgN90Pr4BmX14f7ilLjZURh125G_BmT_kbGnh88AAAD__0r6gLc) who had been scheduled for execution, with four released immediately and four sentenced to one month in prison. Senate Republicans blocked a [fifth attempt from Democrats](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2OpDAQhJ_GZKCmzfATOLiEbC69EDW4PdO3BiPbM9a8_Yp9hc1KKqlK3_fvvtxJvByPv7SzyS4sB5fkOWeOyxZSDi6SJDke9CX25cJbLIcFAfsauhr1Ykn8Z-kqaxwzsq7YtMPQT3ocUVdPY2_9aoHJtXparaUeB8YbwoSM7TZulZhrDTrULcAA0ABZRzS6Ecapo_WmOmArOcTmf5AjP9n5T3hzbLawV948cz6T0n8UzgrnUkqzremiuHqF8xUVzokPylzn-NrPulCsz1A4ploiHQrnKhp7FvFeUj-oDh47if95yL_S8jb4HQAA__8UHng6) to invoke the War Powers Resolution on the 54th day of the conflict, with the fast-approaching 60-day deadline set to force Congress to formally weigh in on continuing military operations.
## NFL Draft Kicks Off Tonight
The first round of the 2026 NFL Draft kicks off tonight from Pittsburgh, with the Las Vegas Raiders on the clock at No. 1 overall. It's the Steel City's first time hosting the event since 1948. [See the draft order](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFuwyAQgOGnwVssOIjtDAxdvKVrR-sc7pJrCURAbOXtq_QVOv_SN_xf5-WMEiVdP_FOvnFeEu01UmtUlkuuLXNBqZKu-CPhyXmTQHkBDcNBuwPYJaDE1-K64JkIyHbkzTgOJztNYLubN8CWjtbS6uxoLmxoALNOHIw9nlYcO_FvTTuwRutR615jYMSJJz2dHK5H5TQFabn031lSuxHHV96o9Jd876K_tfaoyn4omBXM-773VB_pHRXMiaOCORTkpmAu-ZlC7YoPj11ilDqMyunrHSX-Ye1fBzYPvwEAAP__6_JvzQ). Indiana quarterback Fernando Mendoza is the odds-on favorite to be the Raiders' selection, meaning the draft _really_ starts at pick two. Notre Dame running back Jeremiyah Love is this year's X-factor--if the [Cardinals take him at No. 3](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLFuwyAURb8Gb47wg9h4YOjiLV07Ws_mEb8UQwTUUfr1Vbr0A7pd6V7dI52Py3xBDhyv77iTrT7NkR4lUK2U5zWVmnxGLhyv-Mnuy6eDHaUZJPSt1C2o2SGH56wbZz0RkGrIdsPQj8oYUM1mERajvexw6bTrz7SMi9NeKj_imdZ-adi-3qQG1Uk5SHmS6Dyi8UaaUeNyFlqS45ry6ZY41o18eKaD8mlNexPsVuu9CPUmYBIwYebvFLHcU67ltRAwRR_-mnbF7DhiKAKmG2Xa-YlbG9JBLQiYVN8ZNb5Sk627PzgELv0gtLzuyOEXWv9l6rDwEwAA__8Dh32w), he'd be the highest running back drafted since Saquon Barkley in 2018. The 2026 class is widely considered weaker than usual because there's only _one_ franchise quarterback (Mendoza) and fewer elite prospects at the top. Chiefs general manager Brett Veach [predicted](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLHOmzAURp_GbEbGmOAMHtJWtEMTdajaEd3Y13BbgyNzS8TbV8kr_PunT-ec39fxCpRonW6woOOYxxWfW0JmLKPPG-dYgDZaJ_hL4V_MOwXMo1b6JJWRuh0DUDpGUwUXETW2Fbqm70_n1lrdVrNDE5VvlIUGNETofNc08e6V76Ppz1ZX5F5vyui2UapXqlYQIoCNVtmzgXsnjMJAnEv9J9PKM8Z05B1L7fNSJTczPzbRXoQehB5iznyHlOqCkKbltRF6eFJBhofQQ2eM7YUePs-EcZNfr_JTQWb5C8HP8kfBQJ43-Q1hP-TPAgHlxTPtxIe8sHyL34bv8kuByFVx4fGklGg79cKoaQFKbyz-UMvd6f8BAAD__2ybiHQ) "a lot of trades" as teams jockey for prospects with nearly identical grades. Round 1 wraps up tonight before Rounds 2-3 on Friday and Rounds 4-7 on Saturday. Coverage airs across ESPN, ABC, and the NFL Network, with the full broadcast starting tonight at 8 p.m. ET. ## Cost of Raising a Child Per State
The national average cost of raising a child from birth to age 18 [topped $300,000 for the first time](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLFyszAQhJ9GdDDnQwZRqPgbdf7blMwZncwlAnmQbIa3z5DJG6S6K3Z299uP23gjibI-_tPCtoQ0rrznyKXwNk4plxQ2kizrg77Ev0J6i-c0ImBXg66xHT1JPEZdeRuYkduK7aXvu6E1BttqtpO-kr-jvgzBIAD0xICM2BkkbNFUYk830NheAHqABsgHIhMMmEHT_ao0sJeStuYzyVpmDvFIb96aKS1VtHMpz6zafwqdQrfve_PKVJKn4xQodLmk7VDolrTyec84hQ70-aNCd3LWv5j1NEv09f2oc6HCCp0ZejCgrwC9Qldt1j93iVFy1ysNj4Uk_jQpf5rvbfE7AAD__4TKgJw), reaching $303,418 according to a new analysis that tracked housing, food, daycare, transportation, and health insurance. ## Dells Giving $750 Million for UT Medical Center
Michael and Susan Dell announced a $750 million donation Tuesday to establish an "AI-native" hospital at UT Austin, becoming the first donors to [surpass](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLHOnDAQhJ8GOp9sww-mcJGG7tKmRIu9hk2MjezNcff2EXmFvxtpNKOZ79dzeQJFSttPONDyO-Ql4VUjMmNZdqqcC7mNApPDM0dyHzgwLVrqQche6G7xQPGz9K23q_STatGqcRymXitj2t1-dZNHF5xaDazKdMOowuq-AIJyZgDdkr3LZK87pWQn9SMYb4JRq9Z-dFOYml6iJ87lwTsyvqGG-MkvLA-XjzbanfmsTfej0XOj5-u6HiG_7xe33-iZ0e2Nng9yO2AU9W-FJDzGW5YTahVKrBQj5SR8TsCUUxUruD-UNgEkfKEXJrHnehJDFGfJv9FxW6w_rztYh7Hp5XYAxf-b-HskX1b_CwAA__9USoym) $1 billion in giving to the school. Michael Dell, the founder and CEO of Round Rock-based Dell Technologies, dropped out of UT Austin in the 1980s and has [contributed significantly](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL-OtSAQR58GO25wRMCC4mvs7tduaVDgOgmCwbl_fPuNu4-w3cmc5GTy-7pPd4cJ8-O_24KlTyxTDu8jBaJQpxUPKhWXB0bCJewl4XK6LeQJBCguJIdu8g7TOcnG21n4oW2CbbVWg4TWmGa1vYmd7xejFKi5871WUoPSRkqjBMyiQXvFhISubUUn4BaNN9G0M4DXyxAHJkXwSKXeaA0UPu6I6SyvUG9L2ZpkV6L9YN0_BiODMZZKzxwux2C80gxGIS8GBuOGy-pC4j6kxJ_E3fMgzFz3gm-YEpbMfcmOLph_Dw5r4PuKyWVaa9lPBmNTrd_flz-UZlI8Nofp5x_624ovC98BAAD___NXhfk) to the university over the last two decades. The historic gift will be used to [establish](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0L2unTAQBOCnMZ2RvXD5KVykobtpUyJjrw8r-Qfh5XLO20fkFdKNNNKn0fz5Xr8tRcqv3zah4Xcoa8a7RmTGc92pcjnJvSgwOTxKJPexCfMKCgapegnd6i3Fz9o33mzKz7pBo8dxmHvQ09TsBpTquml2ECDgqDY3wxZmP8Lw9eWshobMg6keOq1Vp6ANk5_CpDcAP7o5zKJX6InL2fKOjG9bQ_yUHzxbV1ITzc58VNH9ErAIWO77bl3e3FMKWB5bwKL6J2sBSyK3W4yyXtVm6TFGebG0V2XK0pdsmUqWCT05G6Wz6bhqu3OKzWn8cVOMVIdR9OqVLMV_E_j_jvsx8DcAAP__O4WCVQ) the UT Dell Medical Center and the UT Dell Campus for Advanced Research, which will employ advanced computing and AI in disease prevention, diagnosis, and treatment. The donation jumpstarts a university [initiative](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2upSAURp8GOwxsPYoFxTR2d9opDcJWd4JgZHt-3n7ieYXbfcXKysr372f6cRQprX_djpbfS54SvkpEZjynjQrnk_xKC5PHI0fyH7djmkBBJ1UroZmCo_iZ2irYWYVBV2h133dDC9qYarOz6Xww-HjMoPUDBhWcDzCgamZtXK8rsrdMtdBorRoF9WKCWYyeAULvh2UQrcJAnM-aN2R8u7LET37iWfu8V9FuzEcRzR8Bo4Dxzq-vL1ZjuASMt17AqNp7awHjTn5zGKVLQZaruCQDxijLdR6uFKnlTDFSTpKSXOlJaZWc5cXSXYUpCRir04bjdVOl60Wr1t1R_Obw7058WvgfAAD__3mchjA) to raise $10 billion for the medical center in the next 10 years, with the aim of ranking among the nation's top 10 hospitals during that time.
## Ten Commandments Law Upheld
A federal appeals court [overturned](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOpTAMRb8mdHlKDCJQUGxDN9tuiUziPCwFgogZhr9f8X5hKru4ukfn_vuavpATb--_uNIgPzFPG10lkQgd08JF8sH-zVHY054T-xtX2iYw0GrTaKingJzuqanCMJvQ24oG61zbN2C7rlqGOLvookUDHmsb2xoctm0_227uA3lX8fCUmQZqa01t4BW70MXOzgDB-T72qjEUWPLxkoWEfrDEdOdvOl4-r1UaFpG9qPqPglHBeF3X6ywoOeD9BBSMj8StYHzMnoPCeVMwPlwFo2me3yoYIwU6MGncd8JUtM_nIfo4ExX9Aev9nBN7XfySc9IeNx247AlvLbRpa7TP64pbWGmTh9X1DpreGmOcgrE6hrBfnBKX1qnGvFfk9LGQ323_PcD_AAAA__-2wZit) an injunction blocking several school districts from implementing a new state law mandating the display of the Ten Commandments in public school classrooms. In a 9-8 ruling, the 5th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals [rejected](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLHOpCAURp9GOwwgO2JBsY3dbLulQbjoTUBcuI4zb79xXuGvv-TkfOfvc35ajLivf2wCQ--Q5x2uGoEIyrxhpVzQrRgIHRw5ovvYBPssuXwwrpjsZ28xfmbVerNwP4oWjBiGx6ik0LrdzC-ng-fKikX1DgQHq5SAAFyphetet2huGFeyF4L3XHZBex20WKT0gxvD2CgOHimXjjYgeNsa4ie_oHQupzaajeioTf-7kVMjp-u6upDf94t7b-R0axO62sgpgIdiI3P5LMTOY8vRV_ZlsmgvVuDfiQX3lRHszOWU7O4T7FTZcS4RHXPR1lpyTrUtxh8Xxoj1MTSKr8li_CrRz0K-jPwfAAD__6dqjK4) the argument that the law violates the First Amendment's establishment clause or the free exercise clause. "_To Plaintiffs, merely exposing children to religious language is enough to make the displays engines of coercive indoctrination. We disagree_ ," Judge Stuart Kyle Duncan [wrote](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2OhCAYAJ8GOw18AkJBcbnEbq-8Kw3yo1-CYoRdd9_-cvsK10w5k8zPbbpZTLgvX3YLpj5jnvZwlRRqDee0Yqn5RLdgrOjCkRO6l93CPgEF2VLeQj95i-k18cabmXrNmmDYMEjNgSnVrMZywSjjSs0xwqD57KQQTA7OU6k0dQ2aPxnl0DNGewpdVF5FxWYAPzgdNeE0eKz57OoaanjaEtMrP8LZubw1yay1HoX0HwRGAuN1XZ2zorsXl-9nLd2SHwTGfOCOeS8ExuM-ExhBvNEKKrVoP79pd_jYnMYfF6aERQ6E02WzmN6Z-r85DwO_AQAA__8YtHbA) for the majority. The ACLU of Texas, which is representing the families who are challenging the statute, [vowed](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkDvOpDAQhE9jMiPbIDCBg03IZtMNkR9taMkP1vYMM7f_xVzhT7urPlXVv8f20Bgw7X91BNXePm8JrhqgNSjbgbXlgnZH39DCmQPaj46QNsHERNlIxbA5jeGzjZ1ThrmFd6D4PE_LKLiU3aGkN0770UhpgQ9sAmbBTG5x3Bq7sKVDdcPYKAbO2cBE76WTXnIjhJvt4hcyMnDYcunbAQ3euvrwyS8ovc2xC-po7axk-EPESsR6XVdvTb1b3H8i1q-FiPU-EbF6cFB0oPo8QYdKbX6WRp_nkYOr9CumQV-0wP8nFkw7bZCozTHq5CKkVikmaoOuteQcb2RXlDsvDAHrNJOR7VFj-KZrv9v0pcRPAAAA__87bZCP) to appeal the ruling to the U.S. Supreme Court, saying the decision threatens the "separation of church and state, and the freedom of families to choose how, when, and if to provide their children with religious instruction." Attorney General Ken Paxton, whose office is defending the mandate, [called](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2OpDAQhJ8GMpDd-PgJHFxCNpdeiDx2e2ipwcjuHYa3X7GvsFlJJVXp-_4_locjpv31z21o5RPTsuNZGEUwLysVSZn8i6KQxyMx-cttuC-goG-UaaBbgiO-FlMH-1Rh0jVaPQz9ZECPY71aDAZ6pUI3mCHoXk9G9S6a6CZvvAq6JnuPKQOd1qpT0MYxjHHUT4Aw-ClOlVEYSFJuZUXBjyuRr_TG3Pq01WxXkaNU3d8K5grm8zzby60p3W0F841TweyykGe8Y8SA2XHjjgMdl8anryyNY05naQT3BsD0-g8Y3a6ycZ1tOE5iptIPlVGvzRH_XMvvhL0tfAcAAP___82AIA) the decision a "major victory for Texas and our moral values."

| Friend
Since 1982, Pennsylvania's Medicaid recipients have been denied abortion coverage -- for over four decades, low-income women have been shut out of reproductive care.
Yesterday, that changed.
Pennsylvania's Commonwealth Court struck down the ban, ruling it unconstitutional. More than that, the Commonwealth Court found that the right to abortion is fundamental. This is HUGE--and YOU helped make it happen.

| [](https://zzejj9hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001SsRaOWU63o5NRKaghI_-d1w8EFZgyk7XwK1hUauAXxAH9Vh-h0HAA9Ynhe3ZjJfAyU_m5Xm4_DZh25D0ul13WiV03BffFenTfaFU51YZVM2qbcsdmbA4zm0ChQ1rQOHEm_To2USlZOHCRJq7V72v2nVox4RuIFQRPURtsxnrVaS5ectUfvme7z4_IfT1B5sAKlw7ziUU__XBFVhnQjkqkmcbppKNuYrxAtDREP8sUqisQxcKHsnUnuQlveAYMYrlJ7FPdW2jmVY=&c=bHgwOnZcVYQvoUTj-mZqo7pb8ot2by0m_hwL85_0Ov0-yi9yPwFfag==&ch=cj8221vZMq_wOSKOq4PcBMsdGyN7ryLwTcxxrpATn5oLRJpwo1FMGw==)

Because you stepped up, women across Pennsylvania will finally get the care they deserve. Because of you, the rights of women in PA have been expanded. On their behalf--thank you.
But this didn't happen by chance.
In 2025, Defend Our Courts built a full-scale electoral program targeting 750,000 low-propensity Democratic voters. We doubled turnout from 30% to 60%--driving hundreds of thousands of additional votes in a judicial election most people ignore.
Those voters didn't just retain Supreme Court Justices Donohue, Dougherty, and Wecht.They also helped retain Judge Wojcik and elect Judge Stella Tsai to the Commonwealth Court.
Those are the judges who made yesterday's ruling possible. That's your impact.
And when opponents appeal this decision to the Pennsylvania Supreme Court, as they will, the pro-rights majority you helped protect will be there to uphold it.
But we don't get to stop here. Because while Pennsylvania women are gaining rights-- Women in Georgia are still losing them.
---

| Georgia's abortion ban is still in effect. Women are still being denied care. Women are still dying unnecessarily. And the Georgia Supreme Court is directly responsible.

name: James O'Keefe
subject: The White House responded to our hidden-camera election fraud footage.
body:
A man handed a homeless person a post-it note and a dollar bill on a sidewalk in Los Angeles. On the note was a name, an address, and a date of birth

| | | [](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2z6alvqtul3adtg4tfcpmidi10s093ni00g8tdui0_rp22sh2s8i6epr3cjim1oj1c1h2bs "https://secure.anedot.com/okeefemediagroup/omg-doesnt-happen-mb-popa?utm_source=omg-doesnt-happen&utm_medium=popa&utm_campaign=20260423&utm_content=aan&amount=25")

---
| Dear Patriot,
A man handed a homeless person a post-it note and a dollar bill on a sidewalk in Los Angeles. On the note was a name, an address, and a date of birth — **a real voter's identity.** “Sign his name,” the man said. “Just write what I tell you to write.”**[**We filmed the whole thing.**](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2z4u2anu7lvg4tc7nov8m5lbg5alr1j0444frbjto_rp22sh2s8i6epr3cjim1oj1c1h2bs)

**[****](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2z32tnfpjsj75m2r064m9avq3t1ih05mdmrse6e3o_rp22sh2s8i6epr3cjim1oj1c1h2bs)What you're about to see is the most explosive hidden-camera footage my team has ever captured. Not speculation. Not anonymous sources.**Actual election crimes committed on camera — in broad daylight — on the streets of Los Angeles.** Over the course of several days, my undercover journalists documented petition circulators handing post-it notes with real voters' names and addresses to homeless individuals, paying them cash — one to three dollars per signature — and instructing them to forge those voters' signatures on official petitions and voter registration forms.We captured it **twenty-eight times.** That's twenty-eight documented instances in just a few days of filming. Which means across Los Angeles County, this is happening **tens of thousands of times.**[****](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2za6ot3ilgt0rig7jfliskmhvohn9fmg3uro4s8k8_rp22sh2s8i6epr3cjim1oj1c1h2bs "https://secure.anedot.com/okeefemediagroup/omg-doesnt-happen-mb-popa?utm_source=omg-doesnt-happen&utm_medium=popa&utm_campaign=20260423&utm_content=aan&amount=25")****| [▶ WATCH THE HIDDEN-CAMERA FOOTAGE AND CHIP IN $35](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2zu1fd1q4isg3bb2dm3duvjsusfgj4do89uh82l6o_rp22sh2s8i6epr3cjim1oj1c1h2bs "https://secure.anedot.com/okeefemediagroup/omg-doesnt-happen-mb-popa?utm_source=omg-doesnt-happen&utm_medium=popa&utm_campaign=20260423&utm_content=aan&amount=25")
---
Let me walk you through what our cameras caught.
A voter named Vicky Walker. A voter named Paulson. A voter named Joseph Albright. Real people. Real identities. In each case, a petition coordinator handed a homeless person a sticky note bearing that voter's information and told them to sign as if they were that person.
One coordinator was caught on camera admitting they get paid seven to ten dollars per signature. They're turning around and paying homeless people a fraction of that — a dollar, sometimes three — to commit federal crimes on their behalf.
Let me be clear about what we're talking about: **it is a federal crime to provide false information on a voter registration form. It is a federal crime to offer payment for voter registration.** What we documented is not a gray area. It is multiple felonies, exposed on hidden camera, happening systematically.
The New York Times told America this doesn't happen. Their Sunday edition dismissed election fraud concerns. **We just proved them wrong twenty-eight times on tape.**
And here's what happened next: we brought our footage to the White House. Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt called it “astounding.” NBC News covered it. The story is breaking through.
**But investigations like this are not free.**
Every dollar you give goes directly to fieldwork: $35 covers a day of undercover equipment costs. $50 covers the background research we do to identify real voters whose identities are being stolen. $100 funds a full day of field operations. $250 helps cover the legal costs of protecting our journalists when powerful people try to shut us down.
[****](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2z1ujtrjiracrp56kkbb8buvksnu3hb42qeqe51b0_rp22sh2s8i6epr3cjim1oj1c1h2bs "https://secure.anedot.com/okeefemediagroup/omg-doesnt-happen-mb-popa?utm_source=omg-doesnt-happen&utm_medium=popa&utm_campaign=20260423&utm_content=aan&amount=25")****
[▶ CHIP IN $50 TO KEEP OUR CAMERAS ROLLING](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2zaq7vtlkduh75ihol43ptkfnrl1voa10bpb0eoro_rp22sh2s8i6epr3cjim1oj1c1h2bs "https://secure.anedot.com/okeefemediagroup/omg-doesnt-happen-mb-popa?utm_source=omg-doesnt-happen&utm_medium=popa&utm_campaign=20260423&utm_content=aan&amount=25")
---
Think about what's at stake. If petition circulators can forge voter signatures by the tens of thousands in broad daylight — paying homeless people with cash and cigarettes to impersonate real voters — and the system does nothing about it, then your vote is being diluted. Your voice is being stolen.
The only reason we know about this is because my team was there with hidden cameras. **No one else was going to expose this.** Not the Times. Not local officials. Not the people getting paid seven dollars a signature to look the other way.
We did it. And we need your help to keep doing it.
Can I count on you today?
[****](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2z44h4k1v9kg2nui2l019ovs8r2p35juha56qakgg_rp22sh2s8i6epr3cjim1oj1c1h2bs "https://secure.anedot.com/okeefemediagroup/omg-doesnt-happen-mb-popa?utm_source=omg-doesnt-happen&utm_medium=popa&utm_campaign=20260423&utm_content=aan&amount=25")****
[▶ YES — RUSH $100 TO FUND THE NEXT INVESTIGATION](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2zbh1116tb4jtpcnjpjuqi4p84b9kc8jbbef7a5e0_rp22sh2s8i6epr3cjim1oj1c1h2bs "https://secure.anedot.com/okeefemediagroup/omg-doesnt-happen-mb-popa?utm_source=omg-doesnt-happen&utm_medium=popa&utm_campaign=20260423&utm_content=aan&amount=25")
---

In Truth,
James O'Keefe
Founder and CEO
O'Keefe Media Group

**P.S.** They said election fraud doesn't happen. We filmed it twenty-eight times in a matter of days — real voters' identities, forged by strangers for a dollar a signature. The White House has seen it. NBC has covered it. But the investigation isn't over. **Your gift of $35, $50, or $100 today puts our cameras back on the street tomorrow.**

body:
Property Tax Update From Rep. Chamberlin

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/repryanchamberlin/newsletter-from-rep-ryan-chamberlin-kqs1grv7ud-12933547?e=d1c1b9864f)
---
| | | | |
---
| |
# Property Tax Update From Rep. Chamberlin
---
| | Friends and Neighbors,

In 2023, after my 1st election, **I filed a bill proposing the elimination of Property Taxes.** Then in 2024, 2025, and 2026, I filed major relief bills and my **Freedom 1,2,3 plan** to TOTALLY eliminate and replace the current property tax system.
The strategy laid out will **COMPLETELY** fund our Police, Fire, and Schools all while allowing **FLORIDA** to become the first state in the United States where you can actually own your property.
Now, after fighting for Florida citizens property tax relief, on April 1st, I released a plan that will ensure our success. _(Click the link below watch the full 10 minute press conference (and Follow me on Facebook for ongoing updates)_
---
[|
---](https://ryanchamberlin.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=ec15c6093052c02efbd22b6cd&id=bf64e16dd0&e=d1c1b9864f)
| | Since the Press Conference, a series of articles and interviews are starting to pop.
Here is an article by The Florida Roundup titled:**Why Rep. Ryan Chamberlin wants to eliminate and replace Florida's property taxes**
_A Republican state representative wants to shake up Florida's entire property tax system by eliminating and replacing it._
_The effort to cut or eliminate property taxes in the state has been a top priority for Gov. Ron DeSantis, but so far, there's no official plan._
_Supporters believe cutting these taxes will help with affordability. WUSF's Douglas Soule previously reported how_[ _**critics warn**_](https://ryanchamberlin.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=ec15c6093052c02efbd22b6cd&id=53b599248d&e=d1c1b9864f) _it would affect local services and require fees to be raised elsewhere._
_Lawmakers have wanted to put a measure on the November ballot to reduce property taxes. But during the session, the Florida House passed a sweeping plan that the Senate did not support._
[_**The session ended without a budget,**_](https://ryanchamberlin.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=ec15c6093052c02efbd22b6cd&id=ae4e8a938c&e=d1c1b9864f)_so lawmakers will have to come back to hash it out. The budget has to be approved by July 1 to avoid a partial government shutdown._
_Since the likelihood that the two chambers will pass a constitutional amendment this year is on shaky ground, state Rep. Ryan Chamberlin (R-Marion County) has a backup plan._
_He wants to launch a campaign to collect enough signatures on a petition that would eliminate all property taxes on all properties in Florida. If he gets enough signatures, it could be on the ballot in 2028._
_On "The Florida Roundup," Chamberlin said he'd have a replacement plan following elimination, why he doesn't support the current system, and more._
_I think we should come to a place in this state — be the first state in the United States where people can actually own their property rather than rent it from the government._**Do you support doing away with all property taxes in Florida?**_Absolutely. I support doing away with the system of property taxes that also involves a replacement plan, which I have unveiled this past year. At least a first draft of one.__I do believe that we can eliminate and replace. I'm a believer that the government should not have a lien on anybody's property._**Would you include eliminating property taxes for school districts?**_I would propose eliminating — eventually — all property taxes.__Initially, homestead is where it seems like we're going to start.__But again, if I believe that the government having a lien on a personal home property is wrong, I also don't like the fact that we would have liens in school districts or liens on properties in any district.__"We don't need to cut. We just need to figure out a different way to generate that revenue."__I think with a $1.8 trillion economy, we can figure out a better way to generate the revenue to absolutely not cut any funding when it comes to fire departments, our safety, our schools.__We don't need to cut. We just need to figure out a different way to generate that revenue._**Eliminate the property taxes — all property taxes on all property: Residential vacation homes, commercial condominiums, school taxes, public safety taxes, all taxes, that's eventually what you'd like to get to. Is that accurate?**_Absolutely.__I think we should come to a place in this state — be the first state in the United States where people can actually own their property rather than rent it from the government.__I don't like the current system. I think it was designed in a time when our state was a different size, a different place. I wouldn't have agreed with it back then either, but it's gotten out of control._**How would you propose local governments and school districts, police and fire pay for existing services and personnel?**_I think there are several ways we can do it. I have presented a few ways based on transactions. One, we would put a one-time sales fee on property.__Rather than taxing people $3,000 to $5,000 a year for the rest of their lives on one purchase, we could figure out a reasonable fee where they buy their property to put some money into the system.__I know we have 140-plus million travelers in and out of the state of Florida. They're not helping cover any of the safety fees that are on the backs of the homeowners paying for the whole state right now.__Yet, when they come here, if they're in trouble, our police take care of them, our fire takes care of them. And there's nothing that's being contributed to relieve the burden of property taxes when it comes to that.__[If] someone says, "Ryan, are you open to raising the sales tax at all?" If I have to make a choice between property tax and raising the sales tax one cent or two cents.__Every one cent in the state of Florida generates billions of dollars. We can get to the number fairly rapidly if we look at these creative transactional ways.__"I don't like the current system. I think it was designed in a time when our state was a different size, a different place."__One reason why I would lean toward a sales tax increase if we had to — I don't know that we have to.__But if we had to is because again, the 140 million people that travel to our state, then they're spending so much of that money there, it's actually relieving if we move it off the backs of the homeowners.__It would be one of the biggest tax cuts for the citizens of Florida in history. So I think we look at the numbers and figure it out._
---

clean_body: Property Tax Update From Rep. Chamberlin | | | | | | | | | | | | | | Property Tax Update From Rep. Chamberlin | | Friends and Neighbors, In 2023, after my 1st election, I filed a bill proposing the elimination of Property Taxes. Then in 2024, 2025, and 2026, I filed major relief bills and my Freedom 1,2,3 plan to TOTALLY eliminate and replace the current property tax system. The strategy laid out will COMPLETELY fund our Police, Fire, and Schools all while allowing FLORIDA to become the first state in the United States where you can actually own your property. Now, after fighting for Florida citizens property tax relief, on April 1st, I released a plan that will ensure our success. (Click the link below watch the full 10 minute press conference (and Follow me on Facebook for ongoing updates) | | Since the Press Conference, a series of articles and interviews are starting to pop. Here is an article by The Florida Roundup titled:Why Rep. Ryan Chamberlin wants to eliminate and replace Florida's property taxes A Republican state representative wants to shake up Florida's entire property tax system by eliminating and replacing it. The effort to cut or eliminate property taxes in the state has been a top priority for Gov. Ron DeSantis, but so far, there's no official plan. Supporters believe cutting these taxes will help with affordability. WUSF's Douglas Soule previously reported how it would affect local services and require fees to be raised elsewhere. Lawmakers have wanted to put a measure on the November ballot to reduce property taxes. But during the session, the Florida House passed a sweeping plan that the Senate did not support. lawmakers will have to come back to hash it out. The budget has to be approved by July 1 to avoid a partial government shutdown. Since the likelihood that the two chambers will pass a constitutional amendment this year is on shaky ground, state Rep. Ryan Chamberlin (R-Marion County) has a backup plan. He wants to launch a campaign to collect enough signatures on a petition that would eliminate all property taxes on all properties in Florida. If he gets enough signatures, it could be on the ballot in 2028. On "The Florida Roundup," Chamberlin said he'd have a replacement plan following elimination, why he doesn't support the current system, and more. I think we should come to a place in this state — be the first state in the United States where people can actually own their property rather than rent it from the government.Do you support doing away with all property taxes in Florida?Absolutely. I support doing away with the system of property taxes that also involves a replacement plan, which I have unveiled this past year. At least a first draft of one.I do believe that we can eliminate and replace. I'm a believer that the government should not have a lien on anybody's property.Would you include eliminating property taxes for school districts?I would propose eliminating — eventually — all property taxes.Initially, homestead is where it seems like we're going to start.But again, if I believe that the government having a lien on a personal home property is wrong, I also don't like the fact that we would have liens in school districts or liens on properties in any district."We don't need to cut. We just need to figure out a different way to generate that revenue."I think with a $1.8 trillion economy, we can figure out a better way to generate the revenue to absolutely not cut any funding when it comes to fire departments, our safety, our schools.We don't need to cut. We just need to figure out a different way to generate that revenue.Eliminate the property taxes — all property taxes on all property: Residential vacation homes, commercial condominiums, school taxes, public safety taxes, all taxes, that's eventually what you'd like to get to. Is that accurate?Absolutely.I think we should come to a place in this state — be the first state in the United States where people can actually own their property rather than rent it from the government.I don't like the current system. I think it was designed in a time when our state was a different size, a different place. I wouldn't have agreed with it back then either, but it's gotten out of control.How would you propose local governments and school districts, police and fire pay for existing services and personnel?I think there are several ways we can do it. I have presented a few ways based on transactions. One, we would put a one-time sales fee on property.Rather than taxing people $3,000 to $5,000 a year for the rest of their lives on one purchase, we could figure out a reasonable fee where they buy their property to put some money into the system.I know we have 140-plus million travelers in and out of the state of Florida. They're not helping cover any of the safety fees that are on the backs of the homeowners paying for the whole state right now.Yet, when they come here, if they're in trouble, our police take care of them, our fire takes care of them. And there's nothing that's being contributed to relieve the burden of property taxes when it comes to that.[If] someone says, "Ryan, are you open to raising the sales tax at all?" If I have to make a choice between property tax and raising the sales tax one cent or two cents.Every one cent in the state of Florida generates billions of dollars. We can get to the number fairly rapidly if we look at these creative transactional ways."I don't like the current system. I think it was designed in a time when our state was a different size, a different place."One reason why I would lean toward a sales tax increase if we had to — I don't know that we have to.But if we had to is because again, the 140 million people that travel to our state, then they're spending so much of that money there, it's actually relieving if we move it off the backs of the homeowners.It would be one of the biggest tax cuts for the citizens of Florida in history. So I think we look at the numbers and figure it out. | | | You can read and listen to the full interview by This story was compiled from interviews conducted by Tom Hudson for "The Florida Roundup." | | HERE IS ALSO SOME ADDITIONAL COVERAGE ON THIS ISSUE: | | | STAY CONNECTED FOR UPDATES: For continued updates and future announcements on property tax reform, I encourage you to follow along on Facebook: Staying informed is important as this conversation continues, and your input will help shape what comes next. Ashli was a proud American patriot and veteran who loved God and her family and was passionate about defending our Constitution. That’s why, on January 6, 2021, Ashli went to Washington to exercise her constitutional rights in protest of the certification of the 2020 election results. But on that day, a Capitol Hill Police officer shot Ashli in cold blood in a crowded hallway inside the Capitol. People have told me it’s time to move on, that the forces I am up against are just too big to fight, and that I will never get justice for Ashli. BUT I WILL NEVER STOP FIGHTING! However, there is one very special organization that wasn’t afraid to fight back. In fact, they are still fighting for justice for January 6th victims and former defendants. That organization is Stand in the Gap. I’m so thankful for President Trump’s pardons, but so many lives have been ruined... Former January 6th defendants lost years of their lives while they rotted in jail. Their families lost homes as they paid crushing legal expenses. Some January 6th defendants lost all hope and ended their lives, leaving their families with nothing but a memory. And my daughter Ashli paid the ultimate sacrifice. There’s nothing that can be done for my Ashli, but there is work to be done to make things right for other J6ers. Now that President Trump has issued pardons for these victims of political persecution, Stand in the Gap is on a mission to help them navigate the challenging process of re-entry into society after being incarcerated. These men and women need help and healing — physically, mentally, emotionally, and financially. We must let them know that they are not forgotten. This begins by helping to ensure they have the resources they need to rebuild their lives and reclaim their dignity. Peter,
Donald Trump has launched a full-scale war against free and fair elections in his second term.
With his job approval collapsing and MAGA's House majority on the line heading into the midterms, he is pulling every lever he can to rig the outcome before voters get their say.
MAGA's election rigging strategy has two main fronts:
First, gerrymandering red states to manufacture more Republican seats in Congress.
Second, attacking elections directly -- attempting to seize voter data in key states, calling for the federalization of elections, and laying the groundwork to challenge results at the state level.
But Democrats are fighting back, and winning:

* After California redistricted, Virginia just voted to do the same. Democrats have now completely countered MAGA's gerrymandering and head into the midterms with an edge on the map.

* In 2025, we successfully defended the Wisconsin and Pennsylvania Supreme Courts from MAGA takeover attempts.

* Earlier this year, we won again in Wisconsin -- securing a pro-democracy majority on that court through 2030 at the earliest.

* We have now built a judicial firewall in two of the most critical swing states in the country for the remainder of Trump's presidency.

But the war isn't over.
In less than 26 days, another critical battle arrives. On May 19, Georgia holds a state Supreme Court election -- and Democrats have a chance to knock two MAGA judges off the bench.

Control of GA's state Supreme Court is the firewall that stops these schemes.

But we have to be able to go toe to toe with the war chests my opponents will use to attack me and derail our movement's chances of success.
The more we raise _now,_ the better the chance we'll have** to combat those attacks, talk to more undecided voters across Colorado with our vision for the future and get more folks on our team. **
So while your $5 may not sound like much, friend, trust me – it makes all the difference. _Because every cent you give gets us closer to winning. _
**_[But that's not the only reason I'm asking you to chip in $5 this morning.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/129996484/616284055/-1487442751?amounts=5,25,50,100,250&amount=5&refcode=jtk1364-fr-nd&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjgvMS83NDc5MSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIyOWQ0MjcxMi0xNTNmLWYxMTEtOGVmMi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=cyIHbvmEvgfd0cBbLjXJdbvdvmp-FJRw6Rj3_T9yEpM=)_**

Reaching this goal will determine whether we have the funds to make it out to each of Colorado's 64 counties. **And we've got to reach it by 11:59 p.m. MT next Wednesday.**
So before we get on with the day, friend,** _[will you please rush $5, $25 or anything now to help us reach our $100,00 end-of-quarter goal by next Wednesday evening to help us win this race in November and make Colorado the best state to live in and raise a family?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/129996489/616284064/-1487442751?amounts=5,25,50,100,250&refcode=jtk1364-fr-nd&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjgvMS83NDc5MSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIyOWQ0MjcxMi0xNTNmLWYxMTEtOGVmMi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=cyIHbvmEvgfd0cBbLjXJdbvdvmp-FJRw6Rj3_T9yEpM=)_**

subject: Team Tabitha is showing up everywhere
body:
We’ve been out in the community, building support, and getting ready for our Elmore County campaign kick-off.

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/d3809470e890/im-running-for-alabamas-most-flippable-state-senate-seat-in-15-years-13693703?e=62156fa6a8)
---
[|
---](https://tabithaisner.us20.list-manage.com/track/click?u=800028f57ad91543dbbdd90f2&id=d72975ed8a&e=62156fa6a8)
|
---
| | | | | |
# Team Tabitha Hits the Streets
---
|
---
| | From 5Ks benefiting local organizations to neighborhood meetings and community events, Team Tabitha has been hitting the streets all across Montgomery these last few weeks.
Tabitha joined the 5K benefiting The Grove MGM, then rolled up her sleeves for a community cleanup with the Newtown and Charlestown neighborhoods.
---
| | | | | | | | | | |
---
| |
---
| | She also stopped by the Chisholm Community Resource Fair and dropped in on Herb Day, continuing to connect with people and communities across the city.
Everywhere we go, we are reminded that Montgomery is full of people doing the work to build stronger neighborhoods and a stronger future.
That is what this campaign is about: showing up, staying connected, and being present in the communities we hope to serve.
---
| [Help Team Tabitha Continue to Hit the Streets of District 26!](https://tabithaisner.us20.list-manage.com/track/click?u=800028f57ad91543dbbdd90f2&id=31cebff3e5&e=62156fa6a8)
---
|
---
| |
# D.C. Fundraiser Recap
---
|
---
| | Recently, we gathered with supporters in Washington, D.C. for a fundraiser at Circa at Navy Yard as our campaign continues to build momentum.
It was an encouraging evening filled with conversation about the future of District 26, the importance of this race, and the work it will take to bring new energy and stronger leadership to Alabama.
I am incredibly thankful to everyone who hosted, attended, and supported the event. This campaign is growing because people believe more is possible, and that support is helping us build the kind of movement it will take to win.
---
|
---
| |
# Save the Date:
# Elmore County Kick-Off on May 16th!
---
|
---
| | We’re excited to officially kick off our campaign efforts in Elmore County with a Campaign Kick-Off at Gold Star Park (300 Ready St.) in Wetumpka on Saturday, May 16th, from 1–3 p.m.
Join us as we gather with supporters, build momentum for the months ahead, and continue growing this movement across Elmore County.
If you’re ready to be part of the team, we hope you’ll come out and sign up to volunteer with the campaign.
---

clean_body: | | | Friend — I’m running for Congress because Washington isn’t working for working people.
