Peter, It's spreading like the plague. Quite literally.
The anti-vaccine wing of the MAGA movement -- led by RFK Jr. and his dangerous "Make America Healthy Again" crusade -- is now trying to buy Louisiana's Senate seat to seize more power to enact their deadly ideology.
Let us be clear about what's at stake here.
Louisiana is now among eight states where not a single parish meets the herd immunity threshold for measles vaccinations among kindergarteners.[ ](https://r6msg8hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001yM7asCVMZsWpLj3dC5tstGui_tetv_X4JKG46XcRPciY1WJJT0X24ddZsjufCpC1J833YBdMlRPvcF4YukaMsfWpl5E4ozqlSpCKPn_yFMzQWelhAROExV29dc6oEDWnNFQe5iHmAW7LW58ey72ve_75MlKSoPGMHIpYqTa5gysDZDx2lh1wC_PmKiznhtZgeNZ6vPJ9CyY1DTl2M-PiNeSMO24eYapUShvpsZ7VAab03LdCSRAL_3sBvydspgv_CZ5EWI8chkeLsEtI8vg2pg==&c=d1GgHCxAtd6wcutoqfaePaWn4FmTVvOsOKunIhcsvlIF277TVka7PQ==&ch=xpP8MCM4QJ3vQA8IjHjBc0D2FOAFvutc9SqYvLtpLNJMgqawumK48Q==)In the last 15 years, Louisiana kindergarten MMR rates dropped from 98% down to 92%[ ](https://r6msg8hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001yM7asCVMZsWpLj3dC5tstGui_tetv_X4JKG46XcRPciY1WJJT0X24ddZsjufCpC1J833YBdMlRPvcF4YukaMsfWpl5E4ozqlSpCKPn_yFMzQWelhAROExV29dc6oEDWnNFQe5iHmAW7LW58ey72ve_75MlKSoPGMHIpYqTa5gysDZDx2lh1wC_PmKiznhtZgeNZ6vPJ9CyY1DTl2M-PiNeSMO24eYapUShvpsZ7VAab03LdCSRAL_3sBvydspgv_zu1zJZtfCwpSQS96OrzVfA==&c=d1GgHCxAtd6wcutoqfaePaWn4FmTVvOsOKunIhcsvlIF277TVka7PQ==&ch=xpP8MCM4QJ3vQA8IjHjBc0D2FOAFvutc9SqYvLtpLNJMgqawumK48Q==)-- below the 95% needed to protect our communities.
And what's the MAHA movement's response? Pour money into Louisiana's Senate race to elect someone who will help them finish the job of dismantling our vaccine programs.
Jamie Davis grew up in rural Louisiana. He watched his grandfather -- a sharecropper -- break his body doing manual labor because he didn't have access to basic healthcare. He watched his father build a farm from nothing, always worried about how the family would afford a doctor's visit when someone got sick.
For working families in Louisiana -- then and now -- healthcare has never been a luxury they could take for granted. Vaccines represented hope. A chance for their children to avoid the diseases that had devastated previous generations.
And now we're watching the MAHA movement try to drag us back to those dark days.
RFK Jr. fired all 17 members of the CDC's Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices and replaced them with vaccine skeptics.[ ](https://r6msg8hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001yM7asCVMZsWpLj3dC5tstGui_tetv_X4JKG46XcRPciY1WJJT0X24ddZsjufCpC1GuVg56R_M7T8-qNYhuFC2xa83kXnBTn3zIX7RTmYb28kb5rX_Z-xpfkW4QCfZoectCdGUAmVaExkr08rDJKxSkiI7DbdTgJNcIQSgYtu_59dwE9OiTm00flaw21L0lLXk6UQXkmoT4SdvS6orsNb3q-rhphulf5ynID8iUM3JNKvJPxE1YfYSO-E97lT8GKcPwAGguJc4NseU6bEAHlIauIs2nIF1jv_&c=d1GgHCxAtd6wcutoqfaePaWn4FmTVvOsOKunIhcsvlIF277TVka7PQ==&ch=xpP8MCM4QJ3vQA8IjHjBc0D2FOAFvutc9SqYvLtpLNJMgqawumK48Q==)He went on national television and claimed the measles vaccine kills people. He said natural measles infection prevents cancer -- a statement so medically reckless it's hard to comprehend.
This isn't fringe conspiracy theory stuff happening in some dark corner of the internet anymore. This is the Secretary of Health and Human Services.
And now his movement wants more power in the Senate to continue this madness.
Jamie Davis is the only Democrat in this race with a real shot at flipping this seat and stopping this madness.
We won't stand by while the MAHA movement tries to bring those days back -- not just through lack of access, but through active campaigns to convince parents that vaccines are dangerous.
Louisiana's children deserve better. The state deserves better. And Louisianans need a senator who will stand up to this anti-science extremism instead of enabling it.

Read my trial update:
| Dear Peter,
---
I spent a lot of time over the Easter weekend reflecting on the big picture of what my trial in Arizona is really all about.
---

Maj. Gen. # **Virginia judge blocks Democrat redistricting referendum one day after it passed, citing constitutional violations**
Virginia Circuit Court Judge Jack Hurley **[ruled Wednesday](https://substack.com/redirect/a094c2e9-1c66-4af1-a005-c2158c49efa9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** that all votes for or against the Democrat redistricting amendment approved by voters Tuesday were unconstitutional, entering an injunction blocking certification and citing requirements the referendum didn't meet. Former Republican AG Ken Cuccinelli explained that over 1 million people voted before the General Assembly's "first passage" on Halloween due to Democrats' 45-day early voting period starting September 19, 2025--violating rules requiring an "intervening election" between the first and second passage of constitutional amendments.
* **Democrats immediately appeal, call judge "activist"**: Virginia Attorney General Jay Jones announced his office would "immediately file an appeal," arguing "an activist judge should not have veto power over the People's vote." Democrat strategist Adam Parkhomenko claimed "a rogue Republican judge is trying to override the will of the people because they didn't like the outcome," adding he has "full confidence a higher court will overturn this nonsense quickly."
* **What 's at stake**: The approved referendum could give Democrats a 10-1 advantage in Virginia's congressional delegation (up from their current 6-5 advantage) despite the state being essentially evenly split--Harris won with less than 52% in 2024. Cuccinelli said there are four constitutional challenges moving through Virginia courts, three challenging the amendment process itself, with a final ruling expected by May.

* * *

Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis **[fired back at House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries](https://substack.com/redirect/b2a0c547-3c5b-4969-a232-06798b0b103d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** after he threatened Florida's redistricting plans following Virginia's narrow referendum approval (51.5%-48.5%) of a constitutional amendment allowing Democrats to bypass a bipartisan commission and redraw maps for a 10-1 advantage. What 's at stake: The approved referendum could give Democrats a 10-1 advantage in Virginia's congressional delegation (up from their current 6-5 advantage) despite the state being essentially evenly split--Harris won with less than 52% in 2024. Cuccinelli said there are four constitutional challenges moving through Virginia courts, three challenging the amendment process itself, with a final ruling expected by May. DeSantis challenges Hakeem Jeffries after Dem leader threatens Florida redistricting: "Please be my guest" Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis after he threatened Florida's redistricting plans following Virginia's narrow referendum approval (51.5%-48.5%) of a constitutional amendment allowing Democrats to bypass a bipartisan commission and redraw maps for a 10-1 advantage. Jeffries warned Florida Republicans to "F around and find out" and vowed to "crush" the "DeSantis Dummymander." DeSantis offers to host Jeffries, calls him political liability : DeSantis told reporters "There's nothing that could be better for Republicans in Florida than to see Hakeem Jeffries everywhere around this state. Voters will not like what they see," offering to pay for Jeffries' travel, put him up in the Governor's Mansion, and "take you fishing." DeSantis mocked Jeffries for being "more liberal than Pelosi" while his far-Left base remains unimpressed, calling him "dollar-store Obama" and "AIPAC Shakur." What 's next in Florida: DeSantis called a special session for late April to address Florida's "massive population-driven malapportionment," noting the state has seen "ten years of population growth in just three" making current districts unfair. body:
Mark Kelly has successfully landed on an aircraft carrier 375 times. That's not easy.
#

Mark Kelly has successfully landed on an aircraft carrier 375 times.
[](https://act.markkelly.com/go/1389?c0=mek-em-apr26.E0ZGh8&refcode=em260423-1-180-90&t=1&akid=6428%2E6688874%2EzZ0zZD)
That's not easy.
First off, the landing area of an aircraft carrier is only a few hundred feet in length. That’s about 1/40th the length of a runway at a military airbase. But what makes this even more complicated is that your runway is moving through the water.
It moves to the right because of the angled deck, and bobs up and down like a cork, and rocks left and right in the ocean. It’s challenging during the day and often feels impossible at night.
Naval aviators have to do this in all kinds of conditions — rain, snow, fog, and during combat when the ship is often blacked out so it can’t be found by the enemy.
Mark did that 375 times, and every time any naval aviator does this, he or she is risking their life for their country. And then, he launched into space four times on a space shuttle that is more complicated and more difficult to operate than any other machine ever built by humans.
But never — EVER — did Mark do that alone. Not in the Navy, not at NASA, and not now. At every step of the way Mark has been lucky to have a team behind him. Strong, committed, dependable people who had his back no matter what.
And that’s what Mark needs again today.

But what makes this even more complicated is that your runway is moving through the water. It moves to the right because of the angled deck, and bobs up and down like a cork, and rocks left and right in the ocean. It’s challenging during the day and often feels impossible at night. Mark did that 375 times, and every time any naval aviator does this, he or she is risking their life for their country. But never — EVER — did Mark do that alone. Not in the Navy, not at NASA, and not now. At every step of the way Mark has been lucky to have a team behind him. body:
Our first speaker drop + a look at Poudre School District’s role in student ICE walkouts
| | | | [](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
---
**PRESENTED BY[ROCKYMOUNTAINVOICE.COM](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
| | Hi friends!
**🚨 BIG ANNOUNCEMENT 🚨** We’re doing something different today. Instead of the usual news breakdown, we’re announcing something big:
**👉[Freedom Festival 2026 is officially live — and tickets are on sale now.](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
And we’re kicking it off with our first confirmed speaker... **🎤 Nick Shirley — Keynote Speaker at the Mountain Majesty Gala**
---
[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
Nick Shirley is one of the fastest-growing independent journalists in the country—known for documenting unfiltered truth from the ground, especially in places most media outlets avoid. His investigations into fraud, government accountability, and policy failures have driven national conversations—and we believe Colorado deserves that same level of scrutiny.
Nick will headline the **Mountain Majesty Gala on Saturday evening** , a featured event of the weekend.
Like Rocky Mountain Voice, he represents the future of journalism:
**independent, fearless, and committed to uncovering the truth.**
This is a two-day event bringing together thousands of freedom-loving Coloradans just days before the primary.
**June 26–27 in Castle Rock, we’re hosting:** 🎤 National & regional speakers
📚 Hands-on workshops to educate, activate, and mobilize
👮 The Back the Blue Bash
🎪 A family-friendly carnival & rodeo
🎆 The Mountain Majesty Gala + fireworks finale
This is more than an event — it’s where the movement comes together.
👉 **[Get your tickets now!](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
Want your full news breakdown? Listen to the Mountain Minute podcast [here](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), or watch on [YouTube](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) or [Rumble](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.). Also, don't miss our deep dive video of the day, a look at a new murder sentencing bill [going directly against the wish of voters.](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
This is your Mountain Minute for Thursday, April 23, 2026.
– Team RMV
|
---
**TODAY'S TOP STORIES**
**[What records show about Poudre School District’s role in student ICE walkouts](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY RMV STAFF, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
Nearly half of Lesher Middle School’s 766 students walked out of class on Feb. 2 to protest Immigration and Customs Enforcement, part of a wave of student demonstrations that Poudre School District says it neither encouraged nor discouraged. PSD is among the 10 largest school systems in Colorado.
Emails and internal records reviewed by RMV suggest the situation may not have been as hands-off as described.
Over the following week, other district schools followed Lesher Middle School’s (LMS) lead, as nearly 900 6th–8th graders from over half of the district’s neighborhood middle schools and approximately 1,000 high school students walked out of class to protest ICE.
**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
**Be part of history at Freedom Festival 2026.**
Celebrate America’s 250th and Colorado’s 150th with with 2000+ patriots: two unforgettable days of speakers, action, community, and FUN for the whole family at the Douglas County Fairgrounds.
_America only turns 250 once. Colorado only turns 150 once._
Secure your tickets now and be part of it.
[GET YOUR TICKETS NOW!](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
|
---
**[One Board, One Council, One Legislator at a Time](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY MICHAEL J BADAGLIACCO "MJB", [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* **Nonpartisan elections criticized for reducing transparency:** The commentary argues that removing party labels from local ballots has made it harder for voters to understand candidates’ true positions and affiliations.
* **Shift traced to Progressive Era reforms:** Beginning in the early 1900s, cities and states—including Colorado—adopted nonpartisan elections to curb political machines, but the practice has since become widespread across local governments and school boards.
* **Concerns over gradual political influence at the local level:** The piece contends that local offices like school boards and city councils play a key role in shaping policy, emphasizing the importance of voter awareness and engagement in these races.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
The Rocky Mountain Voice is a 501(c)(3) that exists to promote informed civic engagement and the principles of self-governance through enterprise reporting on public policy, politics, government, and culture throughout the state of Colorado. The only way we can continue to spread truth is with your support!
[DONATE TO ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
|
---
**[The Bell Colorado Voters Refuse to Hear](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY C. J. GARBO, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* **Budget shortfall framed as result of long-term policy choices:** The commentary argues Colorado’s $1.2 billion deficit reflects years of voter support for expanding government programs without sustainable funding, rather than a sudden crisis.
* **TABOR pressures and fiscal practices under scrutiny:** Ongoing efforts to weaken or bypass TABOR are cited as contributing to reduced fiscal discipline, with the piece emphasizing the law’s role in requiring voter approval for tax increases.
* **Economic and revenue concerns tied to policy environment:** The article points to business relocations, rising obligations, and reliance on strong economic growth as risks to long-term stability, warning that declining revenue could shift more financial burden onto taxpayers.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|

**ONLY ON ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE ⤵️ **
**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)****[Patriots Day: Remembering the Courage That Built America](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)****BY REP. SCOTT BOTTOMS | COMMENTARY | APRIL 20** _Every year in April, Americans observe Patriots’ Day to remember the opening battles of the American Revolution at Lexington and Concord in 1775. It is a day that commemorates the courage of ordinary citizens who stood their ground against the most powerful empire in the world. Farmers, tradesmen, pastors, and fathers answered the call of liberty because they believed that freedom was worth defending._
**[Colorado murder bill advances: Sentencing cuts collide with voter mandate](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)****BY SHAINA COLE | STATE | APRIL 20** _Colorado voters approved Proposition 128 in November 2024 with 62 percent support, requiring those convicted of second-degree murder and several other violent felonies to serve at least 85 percent of their sentence before becoming eligible for parole._
____
**[The Trust Weapon: Up the Hill Without the Spill](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** **BY DRAKE HUNTER | COMMENTARY | APRIL 20** _Jack and Jill went up the hill to fetch a pail of water. Jack fell down and broke his crown, and Jill came tumbling after. We’ve all heard this simple nursery rhyme—it’s such a charming and memorable little song. It’s one of my favorites, especially because I recently shared it with my grandchild. That special moment truly highlighted for me how this lovely rhyme reflects a kind of leadership—a wonderful kind at that—The Art of War, Jesus Style._**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**__

**Feel like you have a unique story, commentary or tip to share?** Email [submit@rockymountainvoice.com](mailto:submit@rockymountainvoice.com).
|

|
---
🎤**DID YOU KNOW?** **A little about Nick Shirley:** He is a **23-year-old** independent journalist and viral sensation who has taken the digital world by storm. Nick first made waves on YouTube at just 16 years old with high-stakes undercover stunts, including famously sneaking into influencer Jake Paul’s wedding.

Since then, his work has evolved into hard-hitting investigative reporting, with his recent exposé on state-funded fraud garnering **over 135 million views in a single week**. Having traveled to more than 15 countries to film in high-risk environments—from the favelas of Rio de Janeiro to maximum-security prisons in El Salvador.

Politico: Trump targets states that voted for Harris in shutdown fight [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-end-electoral-college?refcode=042326_1&amount=25]
There's never been a more clear reason to get rid of the Electoral College, friend. We're watching in real time as those in control of the federal government are using it to exact revenge on states that didn't go their way in the last election. Straight from Politico:
“ The White House is targeting Democratic states with its first wave of cuts to federal projects following the government shutdown, impacting billions of dollars in funding for energy and infrastructure ”. Russ Vought, author of Project 2025 and director of the Office of Management and Budget, has gone after billions in federal spending in so-called "blue states" but not publicly announced cuts that affected any state that backed Trump in 2024.

A voter named Vicky Walker. A voter named Paulson. A voter named Joseph Albright. Real people. Real identities. In each case, a petition coordinator handed a homeless person a sticky note bearing that voter's information and told them to sign as if they were that person.
One coordinator was caught on camera admitting they get paid seven to ten dollars per signature. They're turning around and paying homeless people a fraction of that — a dollar, sometimes three — to commit federal crimes on their behalf.

subject: No State Has Fought Back Harder
body:
For every Marylander feeling frustrated at this moment
---
| | | | | [](https://links-1.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fgovernor.maryland.gov%2FPages%2Fhome.aspx/1/0100019dbaf4c26f-20328421-388c-439e-9b21-35aa0271eba7-000000/SmjzeeFklOK56jLRkblsrTo4R8DyaFpMlbYq2YOV5ds=452)
---
| No state has faced more pressure from Washington than Maryland,
and no state has done more to fight back. Here's what we've accomplished,
and why I believe our best days are still ahead. _— Governor Wes Moore_ |
* * *
---
[](https://links-1.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fgovernor.maryland.gov%2FPages%2Fhome.aspx/2/0100019dbaf4c26f-20328421-388c-439e-9b21-35aa0271eba7-000000/4770_UEIdYlW45davScAzXKxrdHQeeOIdZaEjIAnBC8=452)
**No state has been under greater assault from the Trump-Vance administration than Maryland.**
Since January 2025, Maryland's federal workforce has declined by 31,100 jobs — the most of any state — and over 40,000 jobs when federal actions are included. Maryland’s public universities have lost at least $100 million in grants, and Johns Hopkins alone lost nearly $800 million from the dismantling of USAID. NIH cuts jeopardize $5.3 billion in economic activity. And Donald Trump rejected the state’s application and my personal appeal for FEMA assistance after historic floods devastated Western Maryland.
Going into this legislative session, we were squarely focused on **making life more affordable** for the people of Maryland, **protecting the people of Maryland** from the ravages of Washington, and **making Maryland more economically competitive**. Those were our three goals, and we were determined to do all of that while passing a balanced budget without raising taxes or fees on the people of Maryland. Every bill our administration introduced was focused on those priorities, and over the past 90 days, we remained laser-focused on delivering on them with bipartisan support.
**We started with a focus on finances and affordability.** And we focused on where families are seeing it most: the cost of energy, the cost of housing, the cost of child care, and the cost of groceries.
Too many households are being crushed by rising utility bills because of the Trump-Vance administration’s actions and the failures of regional energy operators like PJM. That is why we passed the bipartisan Utility RELIEF Act: to keep more money in Marylanders’ pockets and hold big companies accountable.
Maryland families will save hundreds of dollars on their utility bills. This bipartisan law tackles the problem at its source. It speeds up new energy generation, invests in local clean energy, and stops big corporations from shifting their costs onto ratepayers. Under the bipartisan Utility RELIEF Act, data centers will pay for the grid upgrades they require instead of sticking Maryland families with the bill. Utility companies also cannot come back later and pile on surprise charges.
**We also took aim at unfair utility giveaways.** For too long, ratepayers have been paying for utility executives' enormous salaries, and this law puts a cap on that. They were getting paid extra for doing what they had to do anyway, while Marylanders picked up the tab. This law finally closes that loophole.
And because housing continues to be too expensive for families, **we opened up more than 300 acres of land near major rail stations to help build at least 7,000 homes and generate $1.4 billion in tax revenue.** Building more housing means building more opportunities for people to become homeowners, and building more supply means we can bring down costs. Marylanders should be able to live near where they work, where they grew up, and where they aspire to be.
As parents struggle to afford the skyrocketing cost of quality child care, **Maryland is maintaining record funding — among the largest in the nation — for child care scholarships.** No parent should have to choose between “Are my kids going to be okay?” and “Can I go to work?” Those shouldn't be mutually exclusive choices.
To address grocery prices, the bipartisan Protection from Predatory Pricing Act ensures technology can’t manipulate the price of groceries. Our people shouldn’t be price-gouged in the supermarket checkout line.
Neither a governor nor a state can control how prices continue to rise in supermarkets because of bad federal policy. Neither can control what’s happening because of illegal tariffs. Neither can control the fact that fertilizer has gone up by 37%. Neither can control the fact that gas prices have gone up because of the president’s war of choice, which hasn’t been clearly articulated to the American people. But we’re going to control the things we can control. **We’re going to put money back in your pocket on utility bills and take on big companies. We’re going to make homeownership more attainable and child care more affordable.**
Yet, lowering costs is only part of the solution. We also have to protect our people.
**Public safety remains my highest priority.** Since we took office, statewide homicides have fallen nearly 50%. In Baltimore, which was averaging nearly one homicide a day in the year before I took office, the homicide rate is now lower than at any point in my lifetime. That progress is the result of a comprehensive approach to public safety and record investment in local law enforcement, including a record $124 million this year. We’re seeing the impact in the numbers and in our communities. Recently, that collaboration helped 13 agencies dismantle a drug trafficking ring in Wicomico County, seizing 93 pounds of cocaine, confiscating firearms, and arresting violent criminals.
**Protecting our people also means protecting their health.** When Washington replaced data-driven vaccine research with a choose-your-own-adventure approach, Maryland decoupled its vaccine authority from the federal government. In our state, policy will follow science, not conspiracy theories.
Breaking our reliance on Washington also requires driving economic growth and investing in the foundation of our competitiveness: public education. At a time when the President is tearing apart the Department of Education, Maryland is delivering a record $10.1 billion to uphold our promise of having the best public schools in the country. And we’re already seeing results: o**ver the past two years, math and reading scores have increased in virtually every grade in Maryland, and third-grade reading scores have jumped 20 spots.**
To build on that progress, under State Superintendent Carey Wright’s leadership, we’re adding more literacy coaches to support teachers and help more children read by third grade. That’s what results-based governing looks like.
If we're serious about competing, education must be inextricably linked to economic development. Our schools produce talent, but that means little without more pathways to work, wages, and wealth. **The General Assembly passed the most business-forward legislative package Maryland has seen in years, including the bipartisan DECADE Act.** It strengthens proven programs, removes barriers to investment, and doubles down on lighthouse industries where Maryland can win: information technology, life sciences, and aerospace and defense.
Samsung Biologics recently opened its first American manufacturing facility in Rockville. AstraZeneca committed $2 billion — the largest private capital investment in Maryland in a decade — creating 2,600 jobs in Frederick and Montgomery counties. And National Harbor will become just the third location in the world for a new Sphere, generating more than $1 billion in economic activity each year.
**Each of these bills was passed with bipartisan support.** In fact, 97% of the bills we’ve introduced since our administration came on board have passed with bipartisan support.
Many will say this was a successful session for our administration because we accomplished the objectives we laid out with General Assembly partners. But I want to be clear: this wasn’t a successful session for our administration. This was a successful session for the people of Maryland.
And we’re not done.

| | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. We did it, Peter. **This week****, Virginia voters approved the redistricting referendum that pushes back against a President who believes he’s “entitled” to more Republican seats in Congress.** While other states gave in to those demands without letting voters decide, Virginians refused to let that stand. This victory matters — not just here in the Commonwealth, but across the country. Virginia will play a central role in shaping control of the House of Representatives this November, and I look forward to campaigning with candidates as they earn Virginians’ trust — and their votes. Now, it’s time to build on that momentum — to support candidates up and down the ballot who will now get to work in the districts the voters approved last night. To do that, we need your support. name: Texas Organizing Project
subject: Showing up for our communities. Showing up for Texas.
body:
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/PNG%202023%20TOP%20Newsletter%20Header.png]
Lea el boletín en español abajo [#Español]
FIGHTING BACK:
Calling out Abbott and Paxton's threats to our cities
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/Houston%20speaker%20at%20City%20Hall.jpg]
TOP members in Houston and Dallas showed up and spoke out in solidarity with immigration allies this week, to push back on Greg Abbott and Ken Paxton's attempt to coerce the cities into collaborating with ICE by withholding state funds for public safety.
Read more about their latest disgusting move here. [https://www.texastribune.org/2026/04/16/texas-greg-abbott-ice-houston-dallas-austin-ice-immigration/]
It's textbook MAGA political theater, where actual public safety gets tossed aside because our state "leaders" choose to push Trump's unpopular agenda. Not only is this a direct attack on local governance in our state, the livelihoods of community members is at stake, as ICE continues to act as a rogue agency, disregarding due process and violating people's basic rights. While Abbott and Paxton try to use our cities as political punching bags, we’re stepping up with allies to fight back.
For more information on TOP's work to oppose these threats and how you can plug in, contact Dr. Doshie Piper at dpiper@organizetexas.org [dpiper@organizetexas.org] .
CAST YOUR BALLOT:
Early voting is underway for May 2nd local elections
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/Early%20voting%20sign.jpg]
Just as every vote matters, so does every election for every government level — city, county, state, and federal. Early voting started Monday for a handful of local elections taking place across Texas, and it runs through Tuesday, April 28. Election Day is Saturday, May 2.
Check a list of localities having elections here, and see what's on your ballot. [https://www.texastribune.org/2026/04/10/texas-2026-local-elections-guide-arlington-school-board-dallas-isd/]
Looking for polling places and times near you? Visit GoVoteTexas.org . [https://govotetexas.org/]
Join Team Teal and join the movement
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/2025%20Galveston%20group%20pic.jpg]
TOP is hiring! If you or someone you know is a talented team player and a purpose-driven fighter for justice in our communities, we want to hear from you!
Come work with Team Teal, and help us build the Texas each and every one of us deserves.
Check out our latest job openings. [https://organizetexas.org/about-top/employment/]
Have hiring questions? Reach out to recruit@organizetexas.org [recruit@organizetexas.org] .
TOP Tips: Celebrate Earth Day with family fun
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/Earth%20Day%202025%20kids.png]
It's never too soon to instill in your kids an appreciation for our environment. As we marked Earth Day yesterday, think about commemorating the occasion this week with some at-home educational activities. Check out these quick family-friendly ideas. [https://parade.com/1014585/marynliles/earth-day-activities-adults-kids/]
Español
RESISTIENDO:
Denunciando las amenazas de Abbott y Paxton contra nuestras ciudades
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/Houston%20speaker%20at%20City%20Hall.jpg]
Esta semana, miembros destacados de TOP en Houston y Dallas se hicieron presentes y alzaron la voz en solidaridad con los aliados de la causa inmigrante, con el fin de hacer frente al intento de Greg Abbott y Ken Paxton de coaccionar a las ciudades para que colaboren con ICE, reteniendo para ello los fondos estatales destinados a la seguridad pública.
Lea más sobre esta última y repugnante maniobra aquí. [https://www.texastribune.org/2026/04/16/texas-greg-abbott-ice-houston-dallas-austin-ice-immigration/]
Se trata de un ejemplo clásico del teatro político al estilo MAGA, en el que la seguridad pública real se deja de lado porque nuestros "líderes" estatales optan por impulsar la impopular agenda de Trump. Esto no solo constituye un ataque directo a la gobernanza local en nuestro estado, sino que también pone en riesgo el sustento de los miembros de la comunidad, dado que ICE continúa actuando como una agencia fuera de control, ignorando el debido proceso y violando los derechos básicos de las personas. Mientras Abbott y Paxton intentan utilizar a nuestras ciudades como meros sacos de boxeo político, nosotros damos un paso al frente, junto a nuestros aliados, para contraatacar.
Para obtener más información sobre la labor de TOP para oponerse a estas amenazas y sobre cómo puede usted involucrarse, comuníquese con la Dra. Doshie Piper en dpiper@organizetexas.org [dpiper@organizetexas.org] .
EMITA SU VOTO:
Ya está en marcha la votación anticipada para las elecciones locales del 2 de mayo
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/Early%20voting%20sign.jpg]
Así como cada voto cuenta, también lo hace cada elección en todos los niveles de gobierno: municipal, condal, estatal y federal. La votación anticipada comenzó el lunes para un grupo de elecciones locales que se celebran en todo Texas, y se extenderá hasta el martes 28 de abril. El día de las elecciones es el sábado 2 de mayo.
Consulte aquí la lista de localidades donde se celebran elecciones y vea qué aparece en su boleta electoral. [https://www.texastribune.org/2026/04/10/texas-2026-local-elections-guide-arlington-school-board-dallas-isd/]
¿Busca centros de votación y horarios cerca de usted? Visite GoVoteTexas.org. [https://govotetexas.org/]
Únete al Equipo Teal y súmate al movimiento
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/2025%20Galveston%20group%20pic.jpg]
¡TOP está contratando! Si tú, o alguien que conoces, es una persona talentosa, con espíritu de equipo y un luchador decidido por la justicia en nuestras comunidades, ¡queremos saber de ti!
Únete al Equipo Teal y ayúdanos a construir el Texas que todos y cada uno de nosotros merece.
Consulta nuestras últimas vacantes. [https://organizetexas.org/about-top/employment/]
¿Tienes preguntas sobre el proceso de contratación? Escríbenos a recruit@organizetexas.org [recruit@organizetexas.org] .

[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/Earth%20Day%202025%20kids.png]
Nunca es demasiado pronto para inculcar a tus hijos el aprecio por nuestro medio ambiente. Al conmemorar el Día de la Tierra, considera celebrar la ocasión con algunas actividades educativas en casa. Echa un vistazo a estas ideas rápidas y aptas para toda la familia. [https://parade.com/1014585/marynliles/earth-day-activities-adults-kids/]

clean_body: [] Lea el boletín en español abajo [#Español] FIGHTING BACK: Calling out Abbott and Paxton's threats to our cities [] TOP members in Houston and Dallas showed up and spoke out in solidarity with immigration allies this week, to push back on Greg Abbott and Ken Paxton's attempt to coerce the cities into collaborating with ICE by withholding state funds for public safety. Read more about their latest disgusting move here. [] It's textbook MAGA political theater, where actual public safety gets tossed aside because our state "leaders" choose to push Trump's unpopular agenda. Not only is this a direct attack on local governance in our state, the livelihoods of community members is at stake, as ICE continues to act as a rogue agency, disregarding due process and violating people's basic rights. While Abbott and Paxton try to use our cities as political punching bags, we’re stepping up with allies to fight back. For more information on TOP's work to oppose these threats and how you can plug in, contact Dr. Doshie Piper at dpiper@organizetexas.org [dpiper@organizetexas.org] . CAST YOUR BALLOT: Early voting is underway for May 2nd local elections [] Just as every vote matters, so does every election for every government level — city, county, state, and federal. Early voting started Monday for a handful of local elections taking place across Texas, and it runs through Tuesday, April 28. Election Day is Saturday, May 2. Check a list of localities having elections here, and see what's on your ballot. [] Looking for polling places and times near you? Visit GoVoteTexas.org . [] Join Team Teal and join the movement [] TOP is hiring! If you or someone you know is a talented team player and a purpose-driven fighter for justice in our communities, we want to hear from you! Come work with Team Teal, and help us build the Texas each and every one of us deserves. Check out our latest job openings. [] Have hiring questions? Reach out to recruit@organizetexas.org [recruit@organizetexas.org] . TOP Tips: Celebrate Earth Day with family fun [] It's never too soon to instill in your kids an appreciation for our environment. As we marked Earth Day yesterday, think about commemorating the occasion this week with some at-home educational activities. Check out these quick family-friendly ideas. [] Español RESISTIENDO: Denunciando las amenazas de Abbott y Paxton contra nuestras ciudades [] Esta semana, miembros destacados de TOP en Houston y Dallas se hicieron presentes y alzaron la voz en solidaridad con los aliados de la causa inmigrante, con el fin de hacer frente al intento de Greg Abbott y Ken Paxton de coaccionar a las ciudades para que colaboren con ICE, reteniendo para ello los fondos estatales destinados a la seguridad pública. Lea más sobre esta última y repugnante maniobra aquí. [] Se trata de un ejemplo clásico del teatro político al estilo MAGA, en el que la seguridad pública real se deja de lado porque nuestros "líderes" estatales optan por impulsar la impopular agenda de Trump. Esto no solo constituye un ataque directo a la gobernanza local en nuestro estado, sino que también pone en riesgo el sustento de los miembros de la comunidad, dado que ICE continúa actuando como una agencia fuera de control, ignorando el debido proceso y violando los derechos básicos de las personas. Mientras Abbott y Paxton intentan utilizar a nuestras ciudades como meros sacos de boxeo político, nosotros damos un paso al frente, junto a nuestros aliados, para contraatacar. Para obtener más información sobre la labor de TOP para oponerse a estas amenazas y sobre cómo puede usted involucrarse, comuníquese con la Dra. Doshie Piper en dpiper@organizetexas.org [dpiper@organizetexas.org] . EMITA SU VOTO: Ya está en marcha la votación anticipada para las elecciones locales del 2 de mayo [] Así como cada voto cuenta, también lo hace cada elección en todos los niveles de gobierno: municipal, condal, estatal y federal. La votación anticipada comenzó el lunes para un grupo de elecciones locales que se celebran en todo Texas, y se extenderá hasta el martes 28 de abril. El día de las elecciones es el sábado 2 de mayo. Consulte aquí la lista de localidades donde se celebran elecciones y vea qué aparece en su boleta electoral. [] ¿Busca centros de votación y horarios cerca de usted? Visite GoVoteTexas.org. [] Únete al Equipo Teal y súmate al movimiento [] ¡TOP está contratando! Si tú, o alguien que conoces, es una persona talentosa, con espíritu de equipo y un luchador decidido por la justicia en nuestras comunidades, ¡queremos saber de ti! Únete al Equipo Teal y ayúdanos a construir el Texas que todos y cada uno de nosotros merece. Consulta nuestras últimas vacantes. [] ¿Tienes preguntas sobre el proceso de contratación? Escríbenos a recruit@organizetexas.org [recruit@organizetexas.org] . Consejos de TOP: Celebra el Día de la Tierra con diversión en familia [] Nunca es demasiado pronto para inculcar a tus hijos el aprecio por nuestro medio ambiente. # [What keeps you up at night](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=6380051&post_id=194927793&utm_source=post-email-title&utm_campaign=email-post-title&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTk0OTI3NzkzLCJpYXQiOjE3NzY5NjA0MjAsImV4cCI6MTc3OTU1MjQyMCwiaXNzIjoicHViLTYzODAwNTEiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.X1tEEIjTgLGv98cTkJPoaIiot3S7STJLWv-zuGgRl8Q)
### I want to know what you think.
| | [Haley Stevens](https://substack.com/@haleyformi)

---
| | | [](https://substack..4RxJOFA5XB4llYHlC9Jg_FJpWApWZf731b6VEp4KsII?&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email)

---

Hi friends,
I love talking to people, especially Michiganders. I crack open a pop and chat until the cows come home.
But here's a little secret to being an effective politician: _Stop talking._
Truly. Michiganders know what Michigan needs better than anyone. I learned a long time ago that the first step to getting stuff done is always the same: **listen.**
That's why I'm reaching out with a simple request: **[Will you take one minute to fill out my 2026 Priorities Survey? We're collecting 1,000 responses before midnight tomorrow, and I'd be honored to hear from you directly.](https://substack.com/redirect/1a6e3910-e2d6-4d02-a20e-022749081cee?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[Take the Survey](https://substack.com/redirect/1a6e3910-e2d6-4d02-a20e-022749081cee?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
**Here 's why it matters:**
This is shaping up to be one of the most competitive Senate races in the country. Poll after poll shows I'm neck and neck with MAGA Republican Mike Rogers, and _The New York Times_ even recently named Michigan a key battleground in the fight for Senate control.
The stakes are high. That's why GOP billionaire megadonors are lining up behind Rogers, trying to buy this seat so they can rubber-stamp Trump's chaos agenda in the Senate.
So how do we fight back? **By building a grassroots campaign that listens, learns, and leads - in that order.**
We've already made so much progress:
✅ I introduced the **Stop Trump 's Abuse of Power Act** after Donald Trump abused his power and deployed the military against U.S. citizens.
✅ I led the charge to bring **semiconductor manufacturing back** to Michigan, creating good-paying jobs for our communities.
✅ I introduced the **No Tariffs on Groceries Act** to stop Trump's chaotic price hikes at the checkout line.
✅ I filed articles of impeachment against **RFK Jr.** for putting public health at risk and lying to Congress.
I'm proud of this work. Because it all came from listening to the _real_ concerns of _real_ people - and then taking action to fight for them.
So as we build a winning strategy for what will be a generation-defining election in Michigan, I want to make sure this campaign reflects _your_ priorities.
What's keeping you up at night? What change do you want to see? What matters most to you and your family? How can the government actually help you?
**[Will you please take a minute and let me know? It's a short survey, but it truly helps a ton.](https://substack.com/redirect/1a6e3910-e2d6-4d02-a20e-022749081cee?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[Take the Survey](https://substack.com/redirect/1a6e3910-e2d6-4d02-a20e-022749081cee?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
This is your campaign just as much as it's mine. And together, we're going to make history.
I'm so glad you're here.
With grit and gratitude,
Haley
* * *

A personal note from Haley 👋

I'm a lifelong Michigander and the daughter of small-business owners. I've spent my career fighting for Michigan's working families - and now I'm running for the U.S. Senate to keep standing up for the people I love.

But here's the truth: Senate control could come down to Michigan. And Trump and his megadonors know it. That's why they're gearing up to spend tens of millions to defeat me and hand this seat to a MAGA Republican.

I need your help to fight back. This race will be one of the most competitive - and expensive - in the country, and I'm counting on grassroots support to win.

If you're with me, will you chip in today?

body:
Tim joined Jimmy Kimmel last night to talk about what’s next.
#
Peter,
In case you missed it, **Tim was on _Jimmy Kimmel Live!_** last night to talk about the difficult year that Minnesota has had and what’s next for him: Small Town PAC.
[](https://act.timwalz.com/go/73?c0=stp-ms-em-20206423.19QaaG&amount=5&refcode=em20260423-512&t=1&akid=512%2E34582%2EHjyW6n)
Like Tim announced on Monday, he’s ready to get on the road and find teachers, nurses, small business owners, and other good people out there who aren’t just qualified, but who really care, and give them the tools to run for office.
As Tim told Jimmy, **“I know I can go find people who are better than the clowns and fools we have doing this right now and help them** ... Donald Trump sucks up so much oxygen, we need to fill every single lane with good people who want to make sure that people are fed, that we have healthcare, and we don’t fight stupid wars.”
As long as we continue to come together the way Minnesotans did this past winter — when tens of thousands of people braved 40-below zero weather to deliver food to their neighbors and blow whistles to protect kids from ICE while getting on the school bus — _we’ll get through this_.
That’s what the heart of this country is, and there’s more of us than them.
[**If you’re ready to help Tim recruit and support good people to run for office who truly care about making life better for their neighbors, pitch in $5, $10, or whatever you can right now to directly fuel our work →**](https://act.timwalz.com/go/73?c0=stp-ms-em-20206423.19QaaG&amount=5&refcode=em20260423-512&t=2&akid=512%2E34582%2EHjyW6n)

Tim Walz started Small Town PAC to build a Democratic Party that invests in small towns and delivers a message that resonates with rural America.
Together, we're finding and recruiting thoughtful, hardworking people to run for office, and supporting a new generation of leaders who truly reflect and understand their communities.

subject: Just $1
body:
[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/126?t=1001&akid=6273%2E582294%2EWtVtpu ]Chris Pappas for Senate[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/126?t=1002&akid=6273%2E582294%2EWtVtpu ]Chris Pappas for Senate

We wanted
to share a quick, candid update with you.

Grassroots fundraising has been slower than we expected this month. We
don’t want to panic or sound alarmist, but we do need to be clear about
what that means for our race.

National Republicans are already spending money to flip this Senate seat
red — and they’ve already committed to spend an additional $17 million. It
is clear they’re not holding back.

At the same time, taking back the Senate majority hinges on winning here
in New Hampshire.

The only way we win is by staying competitive every step of the way — and
we’ve seen our fundraising lose steam at a critical moment.

That’s why today we’re lowering our ask to just $1.
[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260423_1.qeuF-T&refcode=em20260423-1&t=1003&akid=6273%2E582294%2EWtVtpu ]Will
you spare $1 to help us win in New Hampshire and flip the Senate majority
blue?

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260423_1.qeuF-T&amount=1&refcode=em20260423-1&t=1004&akid=6273%2E582294%2EWtVtpu ]Donate $1 »

It may not seem like much, but even $1 can make an impact.

That’s because there are hundreds of thousands of people reading this
email, including you.

If even a fraction of folks chip in, we’ll get our fundraising back on
track.

It’s the collective effort of this grassroots team that makes all of this
possible. Together we can build the people-powered campaign it takes to
win.

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260423_1.qeuF-T&refcode=em20260423-1&t=1005&akid=6273%2E582294%2EWtVtpu ]So we’re asking one more time: Can we count on you to contribute $1 or
more today?

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260423_1.qeuF-T&amount=1&refcode=em20260423-1&t=1024&akid=6273%2E582294%2EWtVtpu ]Donate $1 »

Chris’s campaign has always been powered by people like you — Granite
Staters and supporters across the country who believe in commonsense
leadership, protecting fundamental rights, and creating more opportunities
for working families.

If we’re going to win this race and take back the Senate majority, we have
to do it together.

Thank you for being part of this.

Team Pappas

body:

I’ll be the first to admit, I'm not your typical candidate.
You might actually recognize me from TV — and no, not from a campaign ad.
In December 2023, I walked onto the Jeopardy! Champions Wildcard stage as a Marine Corps Intelligence Officer stationed in Stuttgart, Germany. Heading into Final Jeopardy, I had a lead, a category I liked, and a decision to make.
I bet everything...
... and I was right.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-vandenberg [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-vandenberg]
That's how I approach most things in life. You do your homework, you back your judgment, and you don't flinch when the stakes are high.
Right now, the stakes couldn't be higher — and I'm asking you to back me as I take on my next challenge: Running for Congress.
My name is Tyler Vandenberg, and I'm a Democrat running for Congress in California's 6th District. I'm a Harvard Kennedy School graduate, a former Marine officer, and a proud Californian who has spent his career serving this country and our democracy. Now, I’m coming home to fight for it.
Will you chip in $25, $50, or even $100 today to my campaign and Resist Reclaim Rebuild to help us WIN? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-vandenberg]
DONATE TODAY TO HELP WIN THIS RACE! [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-vandenberg]
I didn't come to this decision lightly. After the 2024 election, I watched MAGA Extremists launch attack after attack on everything I love about this state and this country. Cuts to wildland firefighters. Slashing Medicaid. Threatening to sell off our National Forests. Gutting the agencies that keep our communities safe and our air and water clean.
And then there's Kevin Kiley — my opponent, the man currently occupying this seat.
Kiley has recently tried to rebrand himself as an "independent."
Don't believe it for a second.
Kevin Kiley votes with Donald Trump virtually every single time. The independent label is a costume he's trying on because he knows his record is a liability. He's not independent. He's MAGA with crafty branding.
California's 6th deserves better. And I intend to deliver it.
Here's what I'm going to fight for when I get to Congress:
I'm going to fight to make California affordable again. Housing costs are crushing working families across this district. I'll push for real solutions — more housing supply, stronger tenant protections, and federal investment in the infrastructure that makes communities livable. The cost of living isn't a talking point to me. I worked two restaurant jobs just to make rent when I was starting out. I know what it means to hustle just to get by.
I'm going to fight to protect our public lands and our environment. The GOP wants to sell off our National Forests. I want to protect them, fund them, and keep them accessible to every Californian — not just the wealthy few who can afford what comes after privatization. California's wilderness is not for sale.
I'm going to fight to defend Social Security and Medicare. These aren't government handouts — they're promises this country made to working people. I'll oppose any effort to cut, privatize, or undermine them, full stop.
I'm going to fight to protect our neighbors. Immigrants, women, and LGBTQ+ Californians are under assault from this administration. That ends when we flip this seat.
And I'm going to hold MAGA accountable. Not just with speeches — with votes, with investigations, with every tool available to a Member of Congress. The era of consequence-free MAGA corruption has to end somewhere. It can end here.
I spent years in the Marine Corps learning that servant leadership isn't a slogan — it's a discipline. It means showing up, doing the hard work, and putting the people you serve ahead of yourself. That's the kind of congressman I intend to be.
I'm not coming to Washington to build a brand or further my own career.
I'm coming to do the job.
But I need your help to get there. Races like this one don't flip themselves. They flip because people like you decide early that it's worth fighting for — and put their money where their values are.
So, can I count on you to chip in to my campaign TODAY? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-vandenberg]
CHIP IN TO HELP DEMS RETAKE THE HOUSE! [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-vandenberg]
Every dollar goes directly toward building the campaign that beats Kevin Kiley and sends California's 6th a representative who actually works for them.
Let's get to work.
— Tyler Vandenberg

| | Yesterday in the Senate, Republicans kicked off the first step of their budget reconciliation process — a marathon "vote-a-rama" where senators offer amendment after amendment before passing a budget resolution. This is only step one. First, they pass a budget resolution. Then comes step two: a massive, partisan bill that can pass with a simple majority vote and reshape the country. **And what are Republicans prioritizing in that process?** **Not lowering costs for families. Not tackling the price of groceries or gas. Not protecting Social Security or Medicare.** Instead, they are pushing billions more in funding for Trump's secret police at ICE and CBP. During the vote-a-rama, Democrats made it crystal clear what we stand for. **Again and again, we offered amendments to lower costs — to bring down prices on everyday essentials, to support working families, to invest in health care and housing, including an amendment I offered to kick hedge funds out of the single-family housing market.** _And again and again, Republicans voted them down._ They had the chance to stand with families struggling to make ends meet, and they chose to double down on Trump's agenda instead. That's what this budget fight is all about. **It's the same story we've seen over and over: families lose, billionaires win.** I'm fighting back as Ranking Member of the Senate Budget Committee to expose what Trump and Republicans are doing and stop this dangerous agenda from becoming law, but I can't do it alone. clean_body: Yesterday in the Senate, Republicans kicked off the first step of their budget reconciliation process. | | | | Yesterday in the Senate, Republicans kicked off the first step of their budget reconciliation process — a marathon "vote-a-rama" where senators offer amendment after amendment before passing a budget resolution. This is only step one. First, they pass a budget resolution. Then comes step two: a massive, partisan bill that can pass with a simple majority vote and reshape the country. And what are Republicans prioritizing in that process? Not lowering costs for families. Not tackling the price of groceries or gas. Not protecting Social Security or Medicare. Instead, they are pushing billions more in funding for Trump's secret police at ICE and CBP. During the vote-a-rama, Democrats made it crystal clear what we stand for. Again and again, we offered amendments to lower costs — to bring down prices on everyday essentials, to support working families, to invest in health care and housing, including an amendment I offered to kick hedge funds out of the single-family housing market. And again and again, Republicans voted them down. They had the chance to stand with families struggling to make ends meet, and they chose to double down on Trump's agenda instead. That's what this budget fight is all about. It's the same story we've seen over and over: families lose, billionaires win. For years the story was familiar, Californians, tired of sky-high housing costs, crushing taxes, and endless regulations, were packing up and heading for cheaper, redder pastures. It was easy to dismiss as individual choice. A family here, a retiree there. Nothing systemic. Just people voting with their feet.
**That narrative is now CONCLUSIVELY out of date.**
The migration from the "Left Coast" -- California, Oregon, and Washington -- has entered a new, more serious phase. It is no longer just individuals fleeing. Major companies are now doing the same. And the consequences for the Blue states they are leaving behind are becoming impossible to ignore and now there are numbers to back it up!
**[A recent study by the California Policy Lab tracked Californians who moved](https://substack.com/redirect/d0465ad8-085f-48fa-b189-3e290b2f9cb0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** between 2016 and 2025. The financial upside was clear. On average, movers saved roughly $672 per month on housing alone. After seven years, they were 48 percent more likely to own a home than those who stayed. Groceries cost 11 percent more, gas 40 percent more, and utilities 61 percent more in California than the national average. The data is unambiguous: for many families, leaving the state was not just a lifestyle choice -- it was a sound financial decision.
But the real story today is what is happening at the corporate level.

Starbucks, one of Seattle's most iconic companies,[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/5db87765-68b1-4007-b8f8-a3055b15fdf6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[just announced a $100 million investment to build a new Southeastern corporate office in Nashville, Tennessee.](https://substack.com/redirect/5db87765-68b1-4007-b8f8-a3055b15fdf6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** The move is expected to create up to 2,000 jobs. Seattle could lose hundreds of millions in tax revenue as a result. Washington's business tax climate has plummeted from 6th in the nation in 2014 to 45th today. The state recently passed a "millionaires tax" -- a 9.9 percent levy on income above $1 million -- and local progressive politics have grown increasingly hostile to business. Starbucks is not alone in noticing.
Meanwhile, Miami has become a full-blown mecca for the ultra-wealthy. Tech titans like Mark Zuckerberg, Sergey Brin, and Larry Page have led a billion-dollar exodus from high-tax blue states to South Florida. Luxury condo sales in Miami are up 17 percent in the first quarter, and sales of homes above $5 million have risen nearly 10 percent. **[Corcoran Group CEO Pamela Liebman called it a"permanent structural shift,"](https://substack.com/redirect/4e7ba2c0-2b7c-4394-8a55-b4cd049c953c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** no longer a boom-and-bust cycle. Miami is now a "true luxury lifestyle home" and a global city that is pulling capital away from traditional coastal hubs.
This is no longer scattered personal decisions. It is a structural movement. Companies and high-net-worth individuals are deliberately choosing red states with lower taxes, fewer regulations, and more business-friendly environments. Blue states like California, Oregon, and Washington are watching both people and revenue walk out the door.
The pattern is clear and repeating. Progressive policies -- steep income taxes, heavy regulation, and an increasingly hostile attitude toward business -- have created an environment where staying is simply no longer worth the cost. When even Starbucks, a company long associated with progressive values, decides Tennessee makes more sense than Seattle, the message should be impossible to miss.
The financial consequences for the states being left behind are significant. Lost corporate headquarters and high earners mean lost tax revenue, lost jobs, and a shrinking base to fund the very services progressives claim to champion. (As Mamdani in New York is discovering rapidly!) Seattle's potential loss of hundreds of millions in tax revenue from the Starbucks move is just one example of a much larger trend.
Red states, by contrast, are reaping the benefits. Tennessee is gaining jobs and investment. Florida and Texas continue to draw both companies and wealthy individuals. The migration is not random -- it is rational economic behavior in response to very different policy environments.

This should not be surprising. When the cost of living, doing business, and simply existing becomes punitive, people and companies eventually find the exit. What began as a trickle of individuals has become a steady flow that now includes major corporations. The Left Coast is not just losing residents. It is losing the economic engines that pay the bills.
The data and the corporate moves tell the same story. High costs, high taxes, and heavy-handed progressive governance are driving a genuine exodus. And unlike the individual families who quietly packed their bags, companies leaving make headlines and create measurable economic pain for the states they abandon.
The migration from California, Oregon, and Washington is no longer just a personal story. It has become a structural one. Companies are now voting with their headquarters the same way individuals have been voting with their feet for years. The consequences are already showing up in tax revenue projections and corporate relocation announcements.
Blue-state leaders can continue to pretend this is temporary or partisan spin. Or they can look at the data, the corporate moves, and the people leaving -- and finally admit that their policies have consequences.
The Left Coast is emptying out. The question now is how much more it will lose before anyone in power decides it is time to change course.
Given Tom Steyer's comment last night at the California Governor debate, it seems that the lessons are still falling on deaf ears at the moment.

The consequences are already showing up in tax revenue projections and corporate relocation announcements. Blue-state leaders can continue to pretend this is temporary or partisan spin. Or they can look at the data, the corporate moves, and the people leaving -- and finally admit that their policies have consequences. The Left Coast is emptying out. The question now is how much more it will lose before anyone in power decides it is time to change course. Given Tom Steyer's comment last night at the California Governor debate, it seems that the lessons are still falling on deaf ears at the moment. **Coach Tuberville was born in Camden, Arkansas, the third of three children of Olive and Charles Tuberville. College Football’s 2004 Coach of the Year and two-time SEC Coach of the Year, Tommy Tuberville is most often recognized for his success on the field. But it is the legacy of his father, a highly decorated WWII veteran and Purple Heart recipient, that motivates Coach Tuberville to give back to the brave men and women of the United States Armed Forces.

In 1989 Coach Tuberville met his future wife, Suzanne Fette, at the Sugar Bowl in New Orleans. They were married in 1991 and have two boys, Tucker and Troy, who continue to make their dad proud.

In his career as a College Football Coach, Tommy started a long and successful career at the University of Miami, starting as a graduate assistant and rising to the Hurricanes' defensive coordinator. He led the Canes to three AP national championships and coached future Hall of Famers Ray Lewis and Warren Sapp, as well as Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson.

| | | It happened again. Kevin Warsh, Trump's nominee for Fed Chair, [wouldn't answer a simple question](https://default.salsalabs.org/Tbefb5d37-0b05-48f2-b209-9581cce46c94/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9) from Senator Warren — did Trump lose in 2020? Lots of hemming and hawing and word salads but no actual answer. The question should have been easy. Biden beat him. But Trump has spent so much time denying it, and spinning yarns made of complete bullcrap, that nearly every one of his nominees has been afraid to say the truth. This isn't just normal jackassery, it's jackassery that has already done great damage to our democracy and our trust in our most sacred institutions. And given morons across the nation license to believe really stupid shit, and to do terrible things. This dangerous BS needs to end, and it needs to end now. None of the people should ever serve in a government job. You don't hire someone to do work on your house, when they're using a jackhammer to tear apart its foundation. And those already in government jobs — including Congress — should lose them immediately. Peter,

A lot of people leave Montana and don't look back.

I couldn't do it.

I grew up all over this state. Great Falls. Dillon. Victor. Helena. Miles City. As my dad’s career took him from teacher in Great Falls to principal at Pine Hills in Miles City. By the time I graduated high school, I had lived in more Montana towns than most people visit in a lifetime.

Then I went to college in Colorado, then to Harvard Law School, and when I walked across that stage with my law degree, I had offers and opportunities in a lot of places.

I came home to Montana.

I clerked for Ronald Reagan appointed Judge Charles Lovell in Helena then moved to Billings and built a legal career here. My wife Sandra and I have built our life together here for 31 years. We raised our kids here, volunteered here, and put down roots as deep as this state would allow.

I am proud to have served Montana for decades. As Director of the Montana Department of Revenue, I helped spearhead the largest income tax rate cut in state history. I was nominated by President Trump and confirmed by the Senate, as U.S. Attorney, not once but twice. We targeted violent crime, meth trafficking, and the cartels that were flooding our communities with deadly drugs. In my most recent term, our office prosecuted more criminals than any year in the last two decades.

I am now running for United States Senate to stand with President Trump, make life more affordable for Montana families, keep our communities safe, and protect our Montana way of life.

name: Roy Cooper
subject: I knew I had to do something
body:
I felt this responsibility deeply.
Peter,
At the end of this message, I’m going to ask you to **[make a donation to my campaign for U.S. Senate in North Carolina.](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260423-1.pEhhCa&refcode=em-20260423-1&t=1&akid=1313%2E1086043%2EpXq8BK)** But first, will you let me explain why your support is so important?
Frankly, running for Senate wasn’t part of the plan. I wanted to serve North Carolina from right here at home.
Seeing all of the chaos and horrors coming out of Washington, DC, I knew I had to do something. Folks had placed their trust in me throughout my career as a public servant to fight for them – and **I felt that responsibility deeply.**
This is a race I simply could not walk away from. It’s also one I know we can win.
Since launching our campaign, tens of thousands of people have joined our grassroots movement. I’m so grateful to count you as one of them, Peter.
**With a recent poll showing this race statistically tied, and far-right Republicans spending millions to defeat me, I need your help to keep up our momentum.**
**[Your contribution of $5 split between our campaign and Wes Moore will be put to work immediately to help us win in North Carolina and take back the Senate. Will you chip in?](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260423-1.pEhhCa&refcode=em-20260423-1&t=2&akid=1313%2E1086043%2EpXq8BK)**

Despite all of the hate and division in our country right now, I will always believe in the basic goodness of people – and I will always have hope. Thanks for being by my side.
Roy Cooper

Friend, The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) has spent about a billion dollars in the past few months to buy warehouses across the country. It’s begun converting them into ICE detention centers that could each cage up to 10,000 people. We cannot allow this rapid expansion of immigrant detention. Already, at least 17 people have died or been killed in ICE detention facilities so far in 2026. That’s one death per week on average, putting our country on a path to far exceed last year’s horrific record high. Communities in my district and across the country are pushing back against these warehouses, fighting for our neighbors and our shared humanity.**** Some have successfully blocked these detention centers. **Today, I introduced a new piece of legislation: the**** _Ban Warehouse Detention Act_** , which would prohibit DHS from converting or operating any warehouse for the purpose of detaining people. [**Please add your name as a grassroots co-sponsor of the**** _Ban Warehouse Detention Act_****and demand Congress act now to pass it.**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm38h9nrsCCiMen3CGd5zila9m5TwvEQAd8qR-4Y3cFoX07ifYRidlKF1j1X7UPnVwB8-pjMqObs8QVUBt5e3zfgkjH1HvNNzgtyxFIic_Sr6GcJkgEVAS738bAKrosUP7kks7AcR--mAZfhanspSJ5ROMQqs7Vh5slec0vPfIeGxJX1KmD8Z6g2A2sUtDF_aCpIDeFsOm5wczp8htpFWwNVCSw7j07Z8-XiizlxopFKBAHzL23kPjTjJvTjnyPjvBwBtj3ReuKuZ1WBUbxRvx4DEVxJw0u93lcfHTSemvXxO5EehUilIu0n_ew7WYEjVgVnUD6ooxyLxwVluxuHXXCgZ3K2uNXa5AAK9qXIDb8vs0ZB5Ds1UX99WKcZyNFBV37s/4q1/ScdjpBODRlyISOV8mlLjow/h1/h001.Iws7eXT21k6jG-DvAINZAalfzVPBjL7TFX3SSvpHshs) | [SIGN ON](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm38h9nrsCCiMen3CGd5zila9m5TwvEQAd8qR-4Y3cFoX07ifYRidlKF1j1X7UPnVwB8-pjMqObs8QVUBt5e3zfgkjH1HvNNzgtyxFIic_Sr6GTAHzHRZt8HFSMnsvU9_55NG9X6EGserncROzw1HF4tDK2JJwThE07IaB8wZjXtSGd-zqhhc6qeo7X1g9hTIPrpqqLb2iG0LlPnNEmpaDiVN9m5KR_RfLFJVa65P3bZJbML480_4G-vJNiGBcwp0MYN1jC8_FnBQ695haBSU2SuL80_ZfUqaul-MzpnEfj9MXcCaf132V-u_ziv61KtRpcQIkbhK58xlEGDU8YZ_eTJBTiQ84U3C9DPE6Bfm4ZyOtpc-4x9mCZj_Z5URnDp5LUY/4q1/ScdjpBODRlyISOV8mlLjow/h2/h001.SBTE9FCNaHLFnqr3BdNLGnDfj8c2DrNCa8kqWcowmnw)
