The Trump administration’s focus on buying up warehouses has benefitted Trump’s donors, advisors, and business partners. This new model of immigrant detention is tied to Trump’s own grift, profits, and corruption.
Most ICE detention centers are for-profit. They get paid based on how many people they’ve locked up, so they have quotas of the numbers of beds they want to fill in order to make more money.
They already fail to provide necessary medical care, clean drinking water, sanitation, calls to lawyers and families, and other basic rights owed to the immigrants they’ve caged.
These warehouse detention centers will likely be privately-run, as well.
Warehouses are meant to hold objects, not humans. And these will not be temporary holding spaces. **They’re industrial-scale operations designed to process human beings like cargo, stripping them of dignity and due process.**
That’s why I’ve introduced the _Ban Warehouse Detention Act_ with Detention Watch Network, a grassroots organization working to end immigration detention—the unjust and inhumane practice of jailing immigrants while they await a determination of their immigration status or potential deportation.
**This Saturday, Detention Watch Network is coordinating a National Day of Action to Stop ICE Warehouse Detention** , with hundreds of actions planned across the country.1
[**Please help build momentum to end immigrant detention by adding your name as a grassroots co-sponsor of the**** _Ban Warehouse Detention Act_****and demand Congress act now**** _._**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm38h9nrsCCiMen3CGd5zila9m5TwvEQAd8qR-4Y3cFoX07ifYRidlKF1j1X7UPnVwB8-pjMqObs8QVUBt5e3zfgkjH1HvNNzgtyxFIic_Sr6GXBqVS3cwaMgoNi-5Zvaly--U0ndIaZBZCoux--ZhILiWTk6vU7zCDh8aTWxq6brNeETTUEH8lpzQ0llF3YmnyKjcKVKhCoXRXIgueFNjOm0O2zBZqQs2rgyF0w2xWbry65u0FcTHuSNQcHq9XoRL9SSNo3-F9FX1-Gw6sJoVt-93RVmvjjtyE0wabc3T7T79TSn-GtNQA5cqOeCdzWVkED4LRKpw6Z-polAuedOLOuhkDRs05xkkTLIbILyFlPGlH_H5fadwNPJMDv6KYKt1I4/4q1/ScdjpBODRlyISOV8mlLjow/h3/h001.Aay_70De6Mgqp2cb_irQQXyNkiClMLSkUh2hYK43E7Y)
Thank you for taking action.
We will continue building the movement demanding our government abolish ICE, end the criminalization of migration, protect immigrants’ rights, and finally enact a humane immigration system in this country.
I just hosted another Know Your Rights Training with ACLU Michigan and Michigan Immigrant Rights Center (MIRC) to protect people from ICE. More trainings will come, and we will keep showing up for each other.
With you in the fight for our rights and our shared humanity,
Rashida

How many times have you heard the phrase "where there is smoke, there is fire"? Recently, I read [an article](https://clicksp.mariaforstlouis.com/f/a/O91nw8_YS6Mih4Aj6_0akA~~/AAPPABA~/uHFLvFvAK7Phnyz1W9VvViCobz9G7hQNuQbTAPnrScV-QVa_SkvYtrzIKM-nFmbP7G81E_apiwVZDlQQNPvpFXWHkSnUKT3PSlit7FCEBmGzR2AxKQJ2DUfKMtWPuqlvIy-TGIKbYoQv_-5VWC5bu1K0K68E-Dl6w3A0ygVJ8KRfZ4AI98Cck6PbUCqHtijo4G2A2zEHSx0xr0NxT3dljxUMUh1Frh18grSEGeYBDG20syqroBKnRp2_mDxBGshvvnPgPxjv-5VJIGA2zF0Yd3DMh9YFITciRB1_J8NuChkbVHaTUpnLabSeOP-_jbKWZvwgZyrsGslEmDgd8Jk8aKoONQ-xUE6u4ORHulakPrI~) written by Nassim Benchaabane of the Post-Dispatch calling out the soil moved from the Olive Market project to the Ruth Park golf course in University City. At first glance, and after skimming key words and non-responses in the article, I was alarmed the soil was not tested before it was moved. Certainly there would be a follow up article in the paper. For now, no such luck. Here's why I'm concerned about something that may seem trivial to those not paying attention. For the last 16 years, I've tracked the movement of soil. It's not something that was planned, but rather a result of my research investigating radioactive waste and dioxin contamination in St. Louis and how it impacts the health of residential and non-residential communities. One thing an evolving city can count on is migrating soil - natural and manmade. No matter where soil originates, it should always be tested. As St. Louis grew in population, housing and business development became important to sustaining the region. However, knowing and unknowing haulers, concrete makers and citizens participated in the movement of contaminated soil. Whether it was a new housing development built after the early 1940's or a grandmother transporting "soil" to her in-ground garden in Berkeley or workers using soil or "rough gravel" for cement or concrete to lay in basements, sidewalks or playgrounds in Ferguson, everyone is at risk. St. Louis' history of soil migration should not go unrecognized, as it is a reason for many of our illnesses. Today, the movement of soil should still be a concern. Municipalities, County and City governments have praised development, as many of us have, but have ignored the risk factors to workers and families. When soil is not tested almost anything can occur. By way of example, as a young child, I enjoyed making mud pies with soil at my home built in 1940. While original soil may have not been contaminated, a series of floods throughout time may have transported contamination into the soil in areas where I played and where children play now. My environmental research has taken me to the City of St. Louis, Ballwin, Pike County, Kansas City, Chesterfield and other places in Missouri. But I always focused on the St. Louis County senate district I once represented and hoped the elected representatives in the other areas would do their own due diligence to follow up on my work. But, as of now, they haven't. Here are some examples why every local elected leader should care. The homes off of St. Louis Avenue, between Greer and Norwood sit on an out-of-use and unregulated landfill. No one in St. Louis City has followed up on the subsidence, the fact homes are sinking and people have gotten ill with rare diseases. African American doctors and lawyers moved to that neighborhood in the 1960s as it was sold as a place for the up-and-coming. What did the developers know? Why wasn't anything done to warn the residents back then or now? There are three locations in Clayton that have been of concern to some residents. It took the son of a former physicist at Washington University to tell me about two of the locations, alongside Jojo, someone I once babysat when I was a student at Clayton High School. As an adult, Jojo informed me that several young ladies in her neighborhood were impacted by thyroid cancer in their early 20s, an indication early exposure may have occurred. The specific neighborhood is one location mentioned by the physicist's son and also a location where there was a reported truck spill decades ago. No elected official did anything about it. If you drive down Skinker Boulevard now, you may notice the construction next to a church and the Forsyth School, where I once attended. It's frightening to think of the number of people, especially children, who were and are impacted by radioactive waste in that neighborhood. If you're familiar with the previous St. Louis County Board of Elections (BOE) in Maplewood, it too sits on an out-of-use and unregulated landfill where dioxin and radioactive waste were reportedly dispensed with. I obtained a list of nine BOE workers, mostly women, who had cancer at some point while working at that facility. Their cancers are generally associated with radioactive waste exposure. I raised issues about this as a state senator and was ignored by St. Louis County, OSHA and the US Department of Energy, the Maplewood City Council and the Missouri Department of Natural Resources. The Maplewood landfill often had smoke emanating from its pits.

There are other locations of makeshift landfills in places you'd never expect in St. Louis City and County. It has been my personal and professional mission to find each one. Another Post-Dispatch writer wrote a magnificent and detailed article - some years ago - about one of Paul McKee's failed projects and bankruptcy. It is this example in particular that caused me to track the movement of soil even closer. The evidentiary documentation was over 500 pages in the bankruptcy lawsuit McKee once faced. At this old landfill near the airport, Mckee basically allowed for the contents to be spread out to level the ground. The contents had an assortment of chemicals including radioactive waste, dioxin, arsenic, asbestos, PCBs, organic and inorganic matter. Monsanto, Wagner Electric, Mallinckrodt and McDonnell Douglas dumped at the out-of-use and unregulated landfill. 80% of the people who lived in the area became ill with cancer or an auto-immune disease. The list of dumping companies and haulers visiting this site is long. This area was part of the district I represented while serving in the Missouri senate. Many of the surviving families live in the St. Louis County Council seat that I am running for now. Only the memories survive as the illnesses persist, plaguing these families and future generations. In 2017, I videotaped a construction site in the same area. It was obvious workers were never told about the landfill contamination. I brought it up on the senate floor multiple times. No one paid any attention then either. In this case, official documents prove the state and St. Louis County failed adequate oversight and the correct remediation process.
---
In North St. Louis County, there are multiple sites that I have found over the years that are rippled with contamination in and around homes, in school yards and places of employment. One place is a neighborhood along Lindbergh. The businesses mandate their employees to only drink bottled water. However, our local, state and federal governments allow residents in the same neighborhood to drink water from the tap without any warning at all. As your next County Councilwoman, I will change these inconsistancies. St. Louis County has failed to alert residents of the dangers that exist for decades. That's why I am running for the St. Louis County Council - to rip off the scab of silence. It's past time residents know the truth! Citizens deserve to know the truth about the water they drink, the soil their children play in and the toxic air they breathe. It takes just one particulate to change a person's DNA over time, which may lead to cancer or an autoimmune disease. It didn't take a Harvard study to tell me children exposed to radioactive waste get sicker quicker. I already knew this by the stories I've collected for 16 years. My research is quite expansive, unmatched and sought after by both WashU and Josh Hawley. And I can define erasure and environmental racism in 50 different ways. Both the corporate developers (that fund one opponent) and the County executive (who is headed to court for two felonies and supporting the other opponent) want to keep this swept under the carpet for decades to come. St. Louis County deserves leaders who will not bend to corporate interests and their profits, but rather fight for the well-being of workers and families who deserve better than the stale service they are getting now. The out-of-date policies of the past are getting us nowhere fast, regardless of what the issue may be. Finally, the second world war was over 75+ years ago. It's time to uncover the secrets. It is time to be proactive. The clock is ticking. We all deserve clean water, clean air, safe homes and places of employment. #EarthDay2026 Please consider joining my campaign efforts. We need a councilwoman that cares about the health and well-being of every St. Louisan regardless of where they live in the region. Thank You.

Hi – Chrissy here.

Did you know my parents inspired me to become the person I am today, a member of Congress who fights for working families, here in Pennsylvania and across the country?
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/130038052/616406733/685235109?amounts=5,25,50,100,250&refcode=jtk1249-fr-nd&recurring=0&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDIvMS82NDkxMyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI5NWNiNTdhYi00NjNmLWYxMTEtOGVmMi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=hr7V0YF3oMO9lSHC58oErEKKynopofjWGCQ3wPrl6_M=)
It was my dad's experience in the military that led me to want to serve, to join the military myself, to give back to my community in other ways, and to join the House Armed Services Committee. It was my mother's active fight for the Equal Rights Amendment and commitment to her local chapter of the League of Women Voters that led me to my work advocating for women's rights in Congress.
**Just like my parents, I believe there's work to be done. **

And as a longtime resident of Southeast Pennsylvania, I am dedicated to solving the real challenges we face – fighting for everything from greater opportunities for workers and increased savings for families to making high-quality health care more affordable and accessible.
I stepped up for this role to fight for Pennsylvanians during Donald Trump’s first term – and this work has never been more important, as he and his GOP allies in Congress continue to attack our communities, undo progress, and threaten our democracy. President Trump’s policies have made life more expensive, our communities less healthy, and our country less safe.

**I'm committed to continuing the fight to stop MAGA Republicans from threatening our most vulnerable and selling out the middle class, but I can't do it without you. **
**That's why I'm reaching out personally, Derek:** **_[Will you chip in whatever you can spare so I can win my reelection and deliver progress for working families in PA-06 and across the country? Peter,

Today marks one week until our next end-of-month fundraising deadline. Before I ask you to **[chip in just $1](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/130038102/616407010/-349382464?refcode=em-4.23.26-all-b&amount=1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzAvMS85MDE1MyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJiNGNiNTdhYi00NjNmLWYxMTEtOGVmMi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=OoRQoRP4LvLk3gdNLJqlJwnpFUA4j3C4fWj9M5Lkd00=)** to hit our goal, let me explain the rising stakes.

California’s primary election is nearly a month away, and ballots are sent out in less than two weeks. June 2nd is our first opportunity of the midterm election cycle to show our strength at the ballot box – and the national GOP will be watching closely.

**I flipped CA-27 from red to blue in 2024. It was a race that went down to the wire – just 2.6% of the vote, less than 8,000 votes, separated me and the Trump Republican incumbent.**

While it was a close battle with millions in outside spending used against me, it’s not the only reason why this race matters in 2026. Now, I’m in Congress fighting to bring results back to the Santa Clarita, Antelope, and San Fernando Valleys.

The Secretary of State Project (SoSP), launched in 2006, was a formal, targeted initiative founded by progressive activists with significant backing from George Soros and the Democracy Alliance. It operated as a 527 political action committee explicitly aimed at electing Democratic secretaries of state in battleground states to influence election administration and prevent perceived Republican biases, as seen after the 2000 Florida recount. The project focused on a handful of swing states, pouring funds into low-visibility races where secretaries oversee voter rolls, ballot certification, and dispute resolution.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9oZWFydGxhbmRqb3VybmFsLnN1YnN0YWNrLmNvbS9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.U7RXUk99940fPQTafO_PucCOrIieYlRKiOtLfWaCuOo?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=195273473)
In contrast, Soros' involvement in district attorney (DA) races lacks a single, named "District Attorney Project." Instead, it has been a decentralized, multi-year effort starting around 2015-2016, channeled through super PACs like Safety and Justice committees, Justice and Public Safety PACs, and state-specific groups. These often receive direct or indirect funding from Soros' Open Society Foundations or his personal contributions. Reports estimate Soros has spent over $40-50 million (some sources claim up to $117 million including family funds) electing 75 or more progressive prosecutors across dozens of jurisdictions, representing over 70 million Americans--far exceeding SoSP's scale in both dollars and geographic reach.

Both efforts exploit low-profile offices: SoSP targeted election overseers, while DA funding focuses on chief local prosecutors who wield enormous discretion in charging, plea deals, and enforcement priorities.

SoSP's funding was concentrated, with Soros contributing hundreds of thousands directly, amplified by allied donors. It ran coordinated campaigns in specific cycles (2006-2010), achieving successes like electing Mark Ritchie in Minnesota and Jennifer Brunner in Ohio.

DA efforts are more sustained and opportunistic. Soros often becomes the dominant donor in primaries, sometimes providing 90% of a candidate's funds. Examples include $4.7 million for George Gascon in Los Angeles, over $1 million each for Larry Krasner (Philadelphia) and Kim Foxx (Chicago), and millions more across states like Virginia, Texas, and Illinois. Tactics mirror SoSP: overwhelming underfunded opponents in overlooked races, using independent expenditures for ads, and leveraging networks like the ACLU or Fair and Just Prosecution for training and support.

A key similarity is the use of proxy organizations to obscure direct ties, allowing unlimited dark money flows.

Both projects stem from progressive critiques of the status quo. SoSP framed its work as protecting democracy from partisan interference, promoting "fair elections" through expanded access and challenging restrictive rules.

Soros-backed DAs pursue "criminal justice reform": reducing incarceration, eliminating cash bail, declining to prosecute low-level offenses, addressing police misconduct, and prioritizing equity over traditional law-and-order approaches. Proponents argue this corrects systemic biases, especially racial disparities.
Critics view both as partisan power grabs. SoSP was accused of embedding bias to favor Democrats in close races (e.g., aiding Al Franken's 2008 Senate win via recount oversight). Similarly, DA funding is lambasted for installing "rogue prosecutors" who selectively enforce laws, contributing to crime spikes in cities like Philadelphia, San Francisco, and Los Angeles--where homicides and shootings rose dramatically under Krasner and Gascon.

SoSP dissolved around 2010 after mixed results but left a legacy: alumni influenced rules in key states, fueling allegations of enabling irregularities in later elections. Detractors called it corrupt for turning neutral administrators into ideological actors.

The DA initiative has been more enduring and controversial. Many funded prosecutors implemented sweeping policies--downgrading felonies, firing experienced staff, and releasing suspects without bail--correlating with crime surges in their jurisdictions. Backlash led to recalls (e.g., Chesa Boudin in San Francisco) and defeats in some reelections, but dozens remain in office. Conservative groups like the Law Enforcement Legal Defense Fund and Foundation for Government Accountability accuse Soros of buying influence to undermine public safety and even election integrity, noting DAs' power to prosecute (or ignore) voter fraud cases.

Both face claims of corruption: billionaire money distorting democracy by capturing key levers of power--elections for SoSP, justice enforcement for DAs. However, SoSP's impact was narrower (election processes), while DA funding affects daily life more viscerally through crime policy.

Key Differences and Broader Implications
Aspect
Secretary of State Project (SoSP)
Soros-Funded DA Campaigns
Timeframe
2006-2010 (short-lived)
2015-present (ongoing)
Scale
~6-10 states, millions in funding
30+ states, $40-117M+, 75+ prosecutors
Formal Structure
Explicit project with website and founders
Informal network of PACs, no central "project"
Primary Goal
Influence election oversight and rules
Reform prosecution (reduce incarceration, equity)
Criticisms
Partisan election manipulation
Rising crime, selective prosecution
Legacy
Influenced 2008-2020 election debates
Ongoing crime waves, policy shifts in major cities
In essence, both represent Soros-backed strategies to reshape American institutions from the bottom up by targeting obscure but powerful offices. SoSP was a prototype--focused on elections as democracy's gatekeepers--while the DA efforts are an evolution: broader, longer-lasting, and tied to social justice movements. Critics argue they erode impartiality, whether in certifying votes or enforcing laws, prioritizing ideology over neutrality. Proponents see them as necessary corrections to entrenched inequities.

As of late 2025, with crime and election trust remaining flashpoints, these parallel campaigns highlight how concentrated wealth can profoundly influence governance, sparking debates over donor influence in democracy.

body:
Every kid deserves a strong start, great schools, and a bright future.
# [](https://act.mcmorrowformichigan.com/go/685?refcode=&t=1&akid=4538%2E898137%2EXW7nZZ)
It's hard to believe this girl — yes, that’s my Little Orphan Annie hair — is running for the U.S. Senate.
[](https://act.mcmorrowformichigan.com/go/4?c0=mam-em-april2026.vCnu4h&refcode=AU_MAM_FR_GEN_GEN_AC_20260423_PM1_V1_S1&t=2&akid=4538%2E898137%2EXW7nZZ)
_Blowing out the candles on my 7th birthday._
That girl wasn't planning to be in politics. Even after college, even after building a career I was proud of, it wasn't something I was considering.
_And then in 2016, Trump won, and I had to do something about it._
I firmly believe that every kid deserves a strong start at a great school. I’ve spent my time in Lansing fighting to expand educational opportunities and make sure every student in Michigan has what they need to succeed.
Now, I'm in this fight for every kid because they all deserve to have dreams and to have the support they need to fulfill them — including my daughter, Noa.
I want Noa and her friends to grow up in a Michigan where she isn't fighting the same battles for basic rights and economic security that we're fighting right now.
[](https://act.mcmorrowformichigan.com/go/4?c0=mam-em-april2026.vCnu4h&refcode=AU_MAM_FR_GEN_GEN_AC_20260423_PM1_V1_S1&t=3&akid=4538%2E898137%2EXW7nZZ)

I'm going to be blunt with you.

We are closer to losing this country than most people are willing to admit.

Not someday. Not "if things keep going this way."

Right now.

And the scariest part?

It's not happening in Washington. It's happening in classrooms.

High schools. Colleges.

Places where the next generation is being shaped -- or more accurately... reshaped.

If you've ever looked at what's coming out of our schools and thought: _" What happened to this country?" _

You're not wrong. You're seeing it clearly.

Because while most people are arguing online... while they're hoping things will turn around... while they're waiting for the next election to fix everything...

The other side is doing something far more dangerous.

They're raising the next generation.

Earlier. Faster. And with zero resistance in most places.

That's how countries are lost.

Slowly. Then all at once.

But here's the thing that should give a patriot like you hope...

There is one place where that trend is actually being challenged.

_And it shouldn 't even exist. _

**Just one year ago, Turning Point USA 's high school program -- which is now called "Club America" -- was in about 1,200 schools.**
That alone felt like a miracle.

Because starting even ONE chapter today takes courage most adults don't have.

Conservative students get mocked. Targeted. Threatened. Shut down.

And yet...

_They stepped up anyway. _

About that time, Charlie called me.

He didn't sound optimistic... He sounded urgent.

"Andrew, we've got to move faster."

I told him we were. He stopped me.

"No. You're not thinking what I'm thinking. I want to be in 35,000 high schools."

I actually laughed.

"Charlie... there aren't even 35,000 high schools in America."

"Okay," he said. "How many are there?"

"About 27,000."

And without hesitation: "Good. Let's do 27,000."

I remember sitting there thinking to myself... we're barely in 1,200 schools.

We didn't have the staff. We didn't have the infrastructure. We didn't even have the roadmap yet.

But Charlie wasn't fazed.

_" We'll figure it out." _

That was him.

He didn't wait for perfect conditions.

Because he knew something most people don't want to face: If we wait... _we lose everything. _

And now?

Less than a year later...

**We 're in 3,300 schools. **

**Thirteen percent of all high schools in America. **

**Eight states are now backing this effort to put a Club America chapter in every high school statewide. **

_That shouldn 't be possible. _

Not in this environment. Not with the level of hostility these students face every single day.

And yet... it's still happening.

_But Patriot, here 's the part you need to understand: _

This is not a victory. It's a foothold.

_Because in the other 87% of schools? _

There is no resistance. None.

Just one-sided propaganda from the Left.

One-sided pressure on kids who are too young to even realize what's happening to them.

That's the reality.

The question isn't whether we're fighting. We are.

The question is whether it's enough.

Because right now, the students stepping up through Club America...

They're not the majority. _They 're the exception. _

They're the ones willing to take the heat.

The ones willing to stand alone.

The ones willing to risk being targeted just to say: _" I love this country." _

Back them. _Or leave them on their own. _

Everything they need to actually stand their ground.

Not symbolically. For real.

They've already made the decision to lead.

All they're waiting on... is you and me.

**Each activism kit costs $25. That 's it. **

$25 to make sure one student doesn't have to stand alone against the Left in a hostile school.

$25 to put real tools in their hands.

Not "if things keep going this way." Right now. And the scariest part? It's not happening in Washington. It's happening in classrooms. High schools. Colleges. Places where the next generation is being shaped -- or more accurately... reshaped. If you've ever looked at what's coming out of our schools and thought: " What happened to this country?" You're not wrong. You're seeing it clearly. Because while most people are arguing online... while they're hoping things will turn around... while they're waiting for the next election to fix everything... The other side is doing something far more dangerous. They're raising the next generation. Earlier. Faster. And with zero resistance in most places. That's how countries are lost. Slowly. Then all at once. But here's the thing that should give a patriot like you hope... There is one place where that trend is actually being challenged. And it shouldn 't even exist. Just one year ago, Turning Point USA 's high school program -- which is now called "Club America" -- was in about 1,200 schools. That alone felt like a miracle. Because starting even ONE chapter today takes courage most adults don't have. Conservative students get mocked. Targeted. Threatened. Shut down. And yet... They stepped up anyway. About that time, Charlie called me. He didn't sound optimistic... He sounded urgent. "Andrew, we've got to move faster." I told him we were. He stopped me. "No. You're not thinking what I'm thinking. I want to be in 35,000 high schools." I actually laughed. "Charlie... there aren't even 35,000 high schools in America." "Okay," he said. "How many are there?" "About 27,000." And without hesitation: "Good. Let's do 27,000." I remember sitting there thinking to myself... we're barely in 1,200 schools. We didn't have the staff. We didn't have the infrastructure. We didn't even have the roadmap yet. But Charlie wasn't fazed. " We'll figure it out." That was him. He didn't wait for perfect conditions. Because he knew something most people don't want to face: If we wait... we lose everything. And now? Less than a year later... We 're in 3,300 schools. Thirteen percent of all high schools in America. Eight states are now backing this effort to put a Club America chapter in every high school statewide. That shouldn 't be possible. Not in this environment. Not with the level of hostility these students face every single day. And yet... it's still happening. But Patriot, here 's the part you need to understand: This is not a victory. It's a foothold. Because in the other 87% of schools? There is no resistance. None. Just one-sided propaganda from the Left. One-sided pressure on kids who are too young to even realize what's happening to them. That's the reality. The question isn't whether we're fighting. We are. **By Wendy M. Yurgo**
Most parents believe their children are safe at home. That belief is wrong, and it is costing children dearly.
Children are being approached, groomed, manipulated, and threatened through the devices sitting in their hands while parents are in the next room believing everything is fine. This is not a distant threat or something confined to hidden corners of the internet. It is happening in the exact spaces our children use every day, inside games, private messages, and conversations we do not see unless we choose to look.
This is the reality of the 764 network, and it is not theoretical. It is already being prosecuted.
FBI Director Kash Patel provided the following statement:
"The 764 network is real, and it is targeting children right now. These predators use secrecy, fear, and manipulation to reach kids through their own devices. Parents must stay involved, monitor online activity, and report any threats immediately to NCMEC or the FBI. Fast reporting can protect your child and help us stop these criminals."

* * *
_**Piece continues below:**_
Director Patel is not warning parents about an abstract threat. This is already being prosecuted. In March 2026, a confirmed member of the 764 network pleaded guilty in federal court to sexually exploiting multiple minor victims and cyberstalking after targeting at least ten girls online and coercing them into abuse and self harm. Federal cases like this are not isolated. They are part of a growing pipeline of prosecutions moving through the system right now. This is not rumor. This is federal court.
Former FBI Deputy Director Dan Bongino described 764 as "a heinous child exploitation ring that often targets children online and coerces them into acts of violence, self harm, animal abuse, suicide, and sexual abuse." That is not dramatic language. It is an accurate description of what is being done to children.
The process is deliberate and effective. A child is contacted and made to feel seen. Attention turns into trust, and trust turns into secrecy. The relationship is built carefully until the moment the line is crossed. Once that happens, everything changes. The child is no longer participating. They are being controlled. Threats replace conversation, and fear replaces choice.
What parents are not prepared for is the speed. This is not unfolding over weeks. It often happens in hours. A child believes they are talking to someone real, and by the time the truth surfaces, the damage is already done.
These predators do not need proximity. They do not need access to your neighborhood, your school, or your community. They only need access to your child's screen and the belief that the person on the other side is who they claim to be.

**[Support The Capitalist, become a paid subscriber today](https://substack.com/redirect/1451a6a5-6721-49ed-ae64-80de990b2fc6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).**

Parents continue to rely on one dangerous assumption, that their child would tell them. Many do not. Not because they do not love or trust their parents, but because they are afraid. Shame is used against them. Fear is used against them. They are manipulated into silence and convinced that speaking up will only make the situation worse.
At the same time, we have normalized giving children devices that allow direct, private communication with strangers. We have accepted disappearing messages, private accounts, and conversations we cannot see as a normal part of growing up. It is not normal. It is exposure.
This is where parents need to be honest. Privacy is not a right on a child's device. Safety is. Those two ideas are not in conflict. They are the same responsibility.
I delayed a smartphone for my own daughter, and I take criticism for it regularly because she is often the only one in her circle without one. I have not changed my position. A phone for communication is reasonable. A smartphone that allows private messaging, disappearing content, and direct access from unknown individuals is something entirely different. That is not independence. That is access granted to people you would never allow through your front door.
Too many parents are trying to be liked. Too many are giving in because the pressure is constant and the pushback is exhausting. But we are not raising peers. We are raising children, and the cost of giving in is not small. It is exposure to people who understand exactly how to exploit it.
If your child is being threatened, extorted, or exploited online, this is not something to handle quietly. It needs to be reported immediately. The National Center for Missing and Exploited Children CyberTipline and the FBI Internet Crime Complaint Center exist for this reason. If there is immediate danger, call 911. Do not negotiate. Do not wait. Time matters, and evidence disappears quickly.
If this makes you uncomfortable, it should. The appropriate response is not dismissal. It is action. This is happening right now, inside homes, to children who believed they were speaking to someone just like them.
The 764 network is real. The cases are real. The victims are real.
Parents are not powerless, but we cannot protect what we refuse to see, and right now too many are choosing not to look.

He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

She organized doctors, nurses, and activists and stopped the ban in its tracks. Now, she's running for the U.S. House in Nebraska's 2nd Congressional District — and we're going all in to help her win. = | = This race is about so much more than one seat. Here's what's at stake: If state Senator John Cavanaugh wins this Democratic primary, Republican Gov. Jim Pillen gets to handpick his replacement — and we know he'll hand that seat to a MAGA crony with one goal: ban abortion in Nebraska, no exceptions. That's not a hypothetical. That's their plan. And it gets worse. Whoever controls that seat could help Republicans eliminate Nebraska's "Blue Dot," gerrymander the state's competitive congressional district, and lock in an extreme agenda for years to come. The good news? Denise is in the lead. New polling shows that once voters hear her story, she leads Cavanaugh 41%–34%. body:
Will you please give me just a moment to tell you about it?
#
Hey Peter, it’s Emma from Heartland Patriots.
I’m reaching out to share more about the critical mission of Heartland Patriots this cycle. **Will you please give me just a moment to tell you about it?**
_It would be an understatement to say that our country is facing some serious challenges right now._ Control-obsessed politicians are relentlessly attacking our fundamental rights and freedoms. Corruption is at an all-time high. And the cost of living crisis is getting worse and worse, forcing working families to struggle to afford essentials like groceries, housing, gas, healthcare, and so much more.
**Too many of our elected leaders — at all levels of government — have been willing to sit back and watch it all happen. Or worse, willing to add fuel to the fire.** We’re seeing that on full display where I live in Missouri, as many state legislators continue trying to divide us while everyday people work harder than ever simply to make ends meet.
It’s absolutely out of control — and I bet it might feel that way where you live too.
It has never been more important to unite behind candidates across the Heartland who are dedicated to holding the line and fighting back. And that’s why I’m reaching out to tell you more about Heartland Patriots today.
**Heartland Patriots is committed to supporting candidates who will boldly stand up to the spineless politicians + corrupt elites wreaking havoc on and robbing our country.** These are candidates who are working tirelessly to protect our fundamental rights, restore our hard-fought freedoms, and actually make lives better for real working people in communities like mine and yours.
That’s where _you_ come in, Peter. With your help, we can leverage our record-setting grassroots movement to help candidates compete and win tough races across the country.
**That’s why I’m asking:[Will you chip in $10, $25, or just whatever you can to Heartland Patriots today? We’ve already started supporting candidates across the country — and we’ll share more about them in the weeks ahead — but with unprecedented spending by corporate PACs and GOP billionaires this cycle, we need all the grassroots support we can get.](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/102857?refcode=em20260423-10343&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1&akid=10343%2E614464%2EH0C6uJ)**

| | | | High school dropout. Waffle House waitress. First woman to graduate from The Citadel. Single mom. Fighter.

Nancy Mace wasn’t born into power. She worked for every inch of ground she’s gained.

At 17, she dropped out of high school and took a job slinging hash browns at Waffle House to survive. No silver spoon. No Ivy League connections. Just grit, grace, and a whole lot of graveyard shifts.

Nancy is fighting to:

* Prosecute violent criminals and pedophiles with zero leniency

* Crack down on sanctuary sheriffs who let illegal aliens roam free

* Defund radical public universities that indoctrinate, not educate

* Reform education so students learn how to think—not what to think

* Work hand-in-hand with President Trump to put South Carolina FIRST

Through every hardship, Nancy never gave up. And now she’s ready to do what she’s always done: roll up her sleeves, take the heat, and lead from the front.

South Carolina is worth fighting for. And Nancy Mace is just getting started.

I wanted to share this big news with you: I’m endorsing Chris Rabb for Pennsylvania’s third congressional district!
Chris Rabb is the kind of progressive fighter I need alongside me in Congress. He has dedicated his career to challenging corporate power, advancing social justice, and standing up for his community in Philadelphia. He has taken on the establishment before, refused corporate PAC money, and never been quiet about what he believes.
[**Will you consider splitting a contribution between Chris’ campaign and mine to make sure both our people-powered campaigns have the resources needed to win?**](https://act.ilhanomar.com/go/7?c0=io-em-rabb.UN_zjd&refcode=em260423-1-180&t=2&akid=2185%2E791427%2E9eJlUF)

Plus, he’s built a real grassroots movement. In just the first three months of this year, Chris raised as much as his opponents combined, thanks to nearly 1,900 small-dollar donors.

When I was born, my parents had just moved out of a trailer and into a small apartment in Woodlawn, New York. My dad worked long shifts at the steel mill. I watched my mother — who raised six kids — stretch every dollar by buying used clothes and serving fried spam sandwiches for dinner. Witnessing the struggles and pain of those left behind inspired me to run for office, to be a voice for communities that had fallen on hard times, because I had lived that experience. I refuse to sit back and watch as these same struggling families are abandoned by Donald Trump, Bruce Blakeman, and their D.C. Republican allies. But Republican special interest donors could rush millions to my opponent, Bruce Blakeman, to buy control of New York. = = Peter, my childhood inspired me to fight for New York families with everything I’ve got. As Governor, I’ve... ...provided over $100 million in state funding for emergency food assistance ...distributed inflation refund checks for more than 8 million New Yorkers ...and delivered universal free school meals for every New York child But as you’re reading this, Bruce Blakeman is growing his warchest to take me down, turn New York red, and bring Trump’s agenda to our state. We can’t let that happen. = If you’ve saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your payment will go through immediately: | = | = ---|--- = | = ---|--- = | = ---|--- Ever upward, Kathy Hochul Josh Harder for Congress PO Box 4220 Manteca, CA 95337 United States

Peter, Louisiana Republicans just advanced one of the cruelest anti-homeless bills in the country.
Under this bill, homeless people would be forced to choose between jail and involuntary treatment. They'd be billed for that treatment. And if they can't pay, they'd be forced to perform unpaid labor to work it off.

| Peter,

There’s something special about the people here in NY-21.

It’s not something you can always put into words, but you can feel it.

It’s in the early mornings and long days. It’s in the way families stick together and support each other. It’s in the pride people take in their work and in their communities.

##### **APRIL 23, 2026 | THE WAR ROOM | DISPATCH #5**
### **My fellow patriots of District 11, my fellow Floridians, my fellow Americans --**
Lay the bills out across the kitchen table. Add the income, subtract the costs. The number left over represents hope--enough for a down payment, enough to build a future.
For too many in our district, that number is zero. The dream of homeownership has become a cruel equation engineered by a government that has turned from protector to barrier.
* * *
### **The Conflict: Washington Has Declared War on Homeownership**
That zero is not bad luck. It is policy. Even housing advocates pleading for more subsidies admit the scale of the disaster. Their own numbers prove it: in Florida, 576,381 renter households are "extremely low income." For them, there is a shortage of 424,819 affordable and available rental homes. For every 100 of these families, only 26 have a feasible place to live. Of those households, eighty-two percent are severely cost-burdened, spending more than half their income just to keep a roof overhead.
The politicians diagnose "skyrocketing costs" and promise to "reform burdensome regulations." Their solution is always the same: more management. More subsidies to help you pay the rent they made unaffordable. More programs to treat the poverty they engineered.
Tallahassee provided the proof. Faced with a clear choice--to empower you or to manage you--they chose management. Senate Bill 48, which would have let you build a "granny flat" for family or income, they killed. Senate Bill 594, which manages subsidies to pay rent, they passed. The verdict is unambiguous: They will manage your poverty. They will never grant you the freedom to build your way out of it.
This is not a market failure. It is the systematic substitution of managerial surrender for constitutional governance.
The administrative state seized this power through a silent coup of delegation. Congress passes vague, aspirational laws. Then, agencies like the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) and the Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) fill thousands of pages with binding rules. An EPA "Waters of the United States" rule can turn a dry ditch on your property into a federal wetland, forbidding you from building. A HUD rule can withhold federal funds from your town unless it overrides local voters to rezone neighborhoods. They don't just regulate; they zone.
Meanwhile, the Federal Housing Finance Agency (FHFA) dictates who is "creditworthy." It sets the rules for mortgages backed by Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac. If FHFA decides a 20% down payment is the standard, that is now the law for most home loans. They don't just guide the market; they are the credit committee.
This engineered scarcity creates an inescapable trap. Each page of their rulebook adds a cost, a delay, or a prohibition. The nurse priced out of a starter home doesn't vanish--she becomes another bidder in the overstressed rental market, competing with the firefighter and the senior. By blocking the path to ownership, the same rules guarantee a more desperate, expensive fight for every available rental. The result isn't an accident; it's the output of the machine. They don't just regulate the market. They are the market, dictating what you can build, where you can live, and what you must pay.
**This is not governance by consent. It is rule by decree --and it is unconstitutional.**
The first sentence of our Constitution is clear: "All legislative Powers herein granted shall be vested in a Congress of the United States." Law-making does not belong to unelected persons. It cannot. A free society cannot survive when the rules that govern your property and your pursuits are written by those you cannot replace. What they call "expert administration," our Founders would have recognized as tyranny.
The establishment's response, epitomized by Daniel Webster's 15-year record, is managerial surrender. He diagnoses the root cause--declaring that "Congress has slowly delegated its responsibility to unaccountable Washington bureaucrats"--and even cosponsors the solution, the REINS Act. But then, nothing. He will not force a vote. He will not wield his power. He identifies the tree consumed by root rot but refuses to swing the axe.
This is the pattern: diagnose the failure, propose the fix, and surrender to the status quo. He manages the visible dysfunction while acquiescing to its unconstitutional foundation. He manages your decline while surrendering your sovereignty.
This is a direct assault on your **Economic Security** --your ability to own, to build equity, to stand firm. It is enabled by the collapse of your **Political Security** , as power is ceded to a bureaucracy you did not elect and cannot remove.
Washington does not have a housing problem. It has a consent problem. Their method is regulation without representation.
* * *
### **The Impact: The Arithmetic of Despair on Your Kitchen Table**
At your table, this is the monthly calculation: pay the rent, or buy the groceries. Here is the brutal arithmetic of their failure: in Florida, for every 100 families struggling at the very bottom, there are only 26 homes they can possibly afford. In our Orlando metro, it plummets to 13. After rent, a family of four has $62 _less_ than the USDA's "thrifty" weekly food budget.
This is the nurse driving an hour each way on I-4 because she can't afford to live where she works. This is the firefighter, his dream of a fixer-upper crushed by a $20,000 "compliance" fee from a faceless agency. This is the senior in a mobile home she owns, watching her lot rent climb while Tallahassee offers a subsidy instead of protection.
Each story is a casualty report. The aggressor is a regulation--a rule made not by your representative. The victim is your neighbor. The cost is your sovereignty.
* * *
### **The Strategy: One Legislative Strike to Restore Your Sovereignty**
The alternative to managerial surrender is the Strike-Secure Protocol. Our governing mantra: **Strike the Root. Secure the Table.**
**THE STRIKE:** We will introduce and pass the **Regulations from the Executive in Need of Scrutiny (REINS) Act.** This is the single, structural strike at the root. It declares that any major federal rule from HUD, the EPA, or any agency--any edict that adds thousands to your home's cost or blocks you from building--must be sent back to Congress for an up-or-down vote. Your representative must be accountable to you for that vote.
No more hidden deprivation. No more regulatory taxes you never voted for. We strike the root of bureaucratic overreach with the REINS Act. We reclaim your **Economic Security** by dismantling the cost. We restore your **Political Security** by returning the constitutional chain of consent.
**This fight is about stewardship.** The American Kitchen Table is where we pass on our inheritance--a safe home, a strong community, and a healthy, living world for our children. The same bureaucratic rules that make a starter home unaffordable also strangle the clean, managed growth that protects our springs, our coasts, and our land. We do not face a choice between prosperity and preservation. That is a false dilemma sold to us by managers who have failed at both. We fight for the integrity of our home.
**THE SECURE:** While we strike in Washington, we secure the evidence here. Your proof is our ammunition.
* * *
### **Your Battle Plan: Three Steps to Strike Back**
**Join me in this endeavor --**
1. **Gather Your Evidence.** Go to your county or city website. Find the zoning map for your neighborhood. Take a screenshot of where duplexes, townhomes, or "granny flats" (Accessory Dwelling Units) are prohibited. That map is the first piece of evidence.
2. **Personalize the Cost.** On that screenshot, write what that prohibition costs you. Is it your aging parent who can't move in? Your adult child who can't afford to live nearby? The rental income that would pay your mortgage? Put the human cost on the map.
3. **Send Me the Proof.** Email that annotated screenshot to **[evidence@americankitchentable.com](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/51238c98-29e4-4577-b9c8-bd7b2bab1c41?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** with the subject line **" MY HOME."** Tell me in one sentence what that prohibition is costing your family.

As we laid out in our previous dispatch, exposure is not enough. We must act. Your map and your story will be held up on the floor of the House of Representatives. We will not cite think-tank statistics. We will cite you.
* * *
### **Forward, Always**
Daniel Webster offers managed decline. I offer a return to first principles.
He issues a subsidy for your rent. I will pass a law to restore your right to build.
He asks for your patience. I ask for your proof.
This is how we end regulation without representation. This is how we secure the table.
**Strike the root. Secure the table.**
**Forward, always --
Ivette
Champion of the American Kitchen Table**

**Boysko Bulletin: A Decade of Work Crosses the Finish Line!**
---
Dear Peter, The Reconvene Session took place yesterday - with wonderful results. The Governor amended five of my bills. After reviewing the changes with the advocates, I encouraged my colleagues to accept the changes for four of the five bills. So in addition to the 12 bills signed by the Governor over the past few weeks, four additional bills will now become law on July 1 of this year. With the passage of my paid family and medical leave legislation, [SB 2](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/130042705/616422069/-1030786773?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDI2MjQiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiYTE2YmE1MWEtNTIzZi1mMTExLThlZjItMDAwZDNhMTRiNjQwIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=sHxdadLyz8MK3rWS6P-pki6MnZbREueDqqzZMQiFa6s=&emci=a99cef97-ce3d-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&emdi=a16ba51a-523f-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&ceid=22486556), Virginians will no longer have to choose between their work and caring for themselves or their families during a serious medical illness, welcoming a new baby, or deployment. For the cost of a cup of coffee, working Virginians will have the peace of mind that they can care for their loved ones. The program works like an insurance program - with small contributions from each employee and employer, the program fund will pay out benefits leaving employers free to hire a temporary employee or save money. Independent contractors can opt into the program. As programs in other states have shown, paid family and medical leave programs make it possible for small businesses to provide this benefit to their employees. I first introduced this legislation in 2019 and have been refining it ever since, working with stakeholders and national experts who have worked with the other 13 states and DC on their programs. I’ve heard from many families who were unable to care for their loved ones or were forced to quit their jobs in times of medical crises. When families choose where to live, Virginia will now be on the list. My bill, [SB 215](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/130042706/616422072/-297057690?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDI2MjQiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiYTE2YmE1MWEtNTIzZi1mMTExLThlZjItMDAwZDNhMTRiNjQwIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=sHxdadLyz8MK3rWS6P-pki6MnZbREueDqqzZMQiFa6s=&emci=a99cef97-ce3d-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&emdi=a16ba51a-523f-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&ceid=22486556), to narrow the wage gap for women and minorities will also become law - employers will be required to include wage or salary ranges with job postings and not to use salary history in hiring. When I first introduced an equal pay bill in 2017, some of my colleagues laughed at the idea. There’s nothing funny about earning less than others doing the same work. Using salary history in hiring locks people into lower wages from academic and non profit work and from lower wages from jobs worked during periods of caregiving rather than paying people fairly based on ability and experience. We also accepted changes to my bill, [SB 344](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/130042707/616422073/-1451962932?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDI2MjQiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiYTE2YmE1MWEtNTIzZi1mMTExLThlZjItMDAwZDNhMTRiNjQwIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=sHxdadLyz8MK3rWS6P-pki6MnZbREueDqqzZMQiFa6s=&emci=a99cef97-ce3d-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&emdi=a16ba51a-523f-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&ceid=22486556), to protect animals from exploitation in unaccredited zoos. Introduced in response to the egregious incidents where captive mammals were separated from their newborns, who were then sold for thousands of dollars or fed by humans for handling in zoos, I am pleased to take this step to protect these animals. I am also pleased that we accepted the Governor’s changes to my bill, [SB 348](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/130042708/616422074/-1451962928?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDI2MjQiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiYTE2YmE1MWEtNTIzZi1mMTExLThlZjItMDAwZDNhMTRiNjQwIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=sHxdadLyz8MK3rWS6P-pki6MnZbREueDqqzZMQiFa6s=&emci=a99cef97-ce3d-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&emdi=a16ba51a-523f-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&ceid=22486556), requiring safe storage of firearms. Responsible gun ownership includes locking up firearms in homes with a minor or a person prohibited from access. I appreciate that the Governor’s team met with Delegate Watts, myself, and the advocates who have spent many years fighting for this legislation. I am hopeful that the Governor will sign the bill as it passed the General Assembly with bipartisan support. Families should be able to call for help when their loved ones are in crisis without fearing that the encounter will end with a felony. There are times when deterrence is not effective, when people with a disability cannot process what is happening and react with a fight or flight response. I am pleased that the Governor’s team made it clear that they do not want to criminalize disability. The Governor has 30 days to act on the bills with recommendations that were not accepted. In many cases, the legislation was the result of years of effort and I am hopeful that she will sign the bills where her recommendations were not accepted. If not, we have the rest of the year to work with the Governor and her team. I want to thank all of you who voted in Tuesday’s election regarding the constitutional amendment on redistricting. The amendment passed, with especially strong support in our district. There are litigation challenges to be resolved. I am grateful that we elected Attorney General Jones who will fight for us. Watching the federal administration take steps that hurt people in our country and around the world is difficult. We can choose not to look away and to do what we can to make our values known. Today we gaveled in for the special session on the budget. The budget conferees continue their work. Unfortunately the federal administration has taken actions that threaten healthcare and education and food support here in Virginia. Our budget will be balanced per our constitution. I expect we will be back in Richmond soon to finish work on the budget. The draft program is now available for public review on [DRPT’s Open Data Portal](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/130042754/616422120/-371490028?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDI2MjQiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiYTE2YmE1MWEtNTIzZi1mMTExLThlZjItMDAwZDNhMTRiNjQwIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=sHxdadLyz8MK3rWS6P-pki6MnZbREueDqqzZMQiFa6s=&emci=a99cef97-ce3d-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&emdi=a16ba51a-523f-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&ceid=22486556). The SYIP reflects DRPT’s ongoing commitment to supporting transit agencies, enhancing rail infrastructure, and improving mobility for communities throughout Virginia. The program includes investments in public transportation operations and capital projects, as well as funding to advance freight and passenger rail initiatives across the Commonwealth. As part of the statewide transportation planning process, the [Commonwealth Transportation Board (CTB)](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/130042755/616422122/-314440159?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDI2MjQiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiYTE2YmE1MWEtNTIzZi1mMTExLThlZjItMDAwZDNhMTRiNjQwIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=sHxdadLyz8MK3rWS6P-pki6MnZbREueDqqzZMQiFa6s=&emci=a99cef97-ce3d-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&emdi=a16ba51a-523f-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&ceid=22486556) is inviting public feedback on transportation projects and initiatives recommended for funding, including those included in the draft SYIP. The Draft FY 2027–2032 SYIP allocates funding across key programs such as Revenue Sharing, Transportation Alternatives, Innovation and Technology Transportation Fund, State of Good Repair, and public transportation and rail programs. DRPT encourages the public to provide feedback on the draft program by attending public meetings or submitting comments online, by email, or by mail. The CTB will host nine public meetings across Virginia, providing opportunities for community members to learn more about proposed projects and share feedback. Public input will also be accepted for new projects valued at more than $25 million. clean_body: | | | | Boysko Bulletin: A Decade of Work Crosses the Finish Line! Dear Peter, The Reconvene Session took place yesterday - with wonderful results. The Governor amended five of my bills. After reviewing the changes with the advocates, I encouraged my colleagues to accept the changes for four of the five bills. So in addition to the 12 bills signed by the Governor over the past few weeks, four additional bills will now become law on July 1 of this year. With the passage of my paid family and medical leave legislation, , Virginians will no longer have to choose between their work and caring for themselves or their families during a serious medical illness, welcoming a new baby, or deployment. For the cost of a cup of coffee, working Virginians will have the peace of mind that they can care for their loved ones. The program works like an insurance program - with small contributions from each employee and employer, the program fund will pay out benefits leaving employers free to hire a temporary employee or save money. Independent contractors can opt into the program. As programs in other states have shown, paid family and medical leave programs make it possible for small businesses to provide this benefit to their employees. I first introduced this legislation in 2019 and have been refining it ever since, working with stakeholders and national experts who have worked with the other 13 states and DC on their programs. I’ve heard from many families who were unable to care for their loved ones or were forced to quit their jobs in times of medical crises. When families choose where to live, Virginia will now be on the list. My bill, , to narrow the wage gap for women and minorities will also become law - employers will be required to include wage or salary ranges with job postings and not to use salary history in hiring. When I first introduced an equal pay bill in 2017, some of my colleagues laughed at the idea. There’s nothing funny about earning less than others doing the same work. Using salary history in hiring locks people into lower wages from academic and non profit work and from lower wages from jobs worked during periods of caregiving rather than paying people fairly based on ability and experience. We also accepted changes to my bill, , to protect animals from exploitation in unaccredited zoos. Introduced in response to the egregious incidents where captive mammals were separated from their newborns, who were then sold for thousands of dollars or fed by humans for handling in zoos, I am pleased to take this step to protect these animals. I am also pleased that we accepted the Governor’s changes to my bill, , requiring safe storage of firearms. Responsible gun ownership includes locking up firearms in homes with a minor or a person prohibited from access. Remember that Virginia offers a that covers their cost. For the fifth bill, , the changes would have left the bill ineffective. I appreciate that the Governor’s team met with Delegate Watts, myself, and the advocates who have spent many years fighting for this legislation. I am hopeful that the Governor will sign the bill as it passed the General Assembly with bipartisan support. Families should be able to call for help when their loved ones are in crisis without fearing that the encounter will end with a felony. There are times when deterrence is not effective, when people with a disability cannot process what is happening and react with a fight or flight response. I am pleased that the Governor’s team made it clear that they do not want to criminalize disability. The Governor has 30 days to act on the bills with recommendations that were not accepted. In many cases, the legislation was the result of years of effort and I am hopeful that she will sign the bills where her recommendations were not accepted. If not, we have the rest of the year to work with the Governor and her team. I want to thank all of you who voted in Tuesday’s election regarding the constitutional amendment on redistricting. The amendment passed, with especially strong support in our district. There are litigation challenges to be resolved. I am grateful that we elected Attorney General Jones who will fight for us. Watching the federal administration take steps that hurt people in our country and around the world is difficult. We can choose not to look away and to do what we can to make our values known. Today we gaveled in for the special session on the budget. The budget conferees continue their work. Unfortunately the federal administration has taken actions that threaten healthcare and education and food support here in Virginia. Our budget will be balanced per our constitution. I expect we will be back in Richmond soon to finish work on the budget. I have a fourth town hall next Monday, April 27 at the Grange in Great Falls with Delegate Sullivan - more information is included below! Kindest regards, Jennifer B. Update on the Fight Against The Tysons Casino Governor Spanberger vetoed the casino legislation,**, and yesterday the Senate sustained the veto by voting to pass the bill by for the day. In meetings with the Governor’s team, they mentioned the many emails you all sent. We have made it clear that our community does not want a casino, would not benefit from a casino financially, and in fact would be harmed by a casino. Despite the clear rejection of our community, sponsors of the legislation have vowed to introduce the bill again so we will continue the fight. I encourage everyone who opposes this proposal to stay engaged and join the growing movement to stop a Tysons casino. By organizing, educating our neighbors, and reaching out to state leaders, we have made sure that our concerns were heard loud and clear and we will continue that work. You can sign up for updates, and take action, visit the . Together, we can continue building momentum and strengthen the No Tysons Casino movement. Transportation Updates Fiscal Year 2027–2032 Six-Year Improvement Program The has released its draft Fiscal Year (FY) 2027–2032 Six-Year Improvement Program (SYIP), outlining planned investments in public transportation, and freight and passenger rail across the Commonwealth over the next six fiscal years. The draft program is now available for public review on . The SYIP reflects DRPT’s ongoing commitment to supporting transit agencies, enhancing rail infrastructure, and improving mobility for communities throughout Virginia. The program includes investments in public transportation operations and capital projects, as well as funding to advance freight and passenger rail initiatives across the Commonwealth. As part of the statewide transportation planning process, the is inviting public feedback on transportation projects and initiatives recommended for funding, including those included in the draft SYIP. The Draft FY 2027–2032 SYIP allocates funding across key programs such as Revenue Sharing, Transportation Alternatives, Innovation and Technology Transportation Fund, State of Good Repair, and public transportation and rail programs. DRPT encourages the public to provide feedback on the draft program by attending public meetings or submitting comments online, by email, or by mail. The CTB will host nine public meetings across Virginia, providing opportunities for community members to learn more about proposed projects and share feedback. Public input will also be accepted for new projects valued at more than $25 million. The Northern Virginia meeting is on May 19, 2026, at 5 pm at Hotel AKA Alexandria, 625 First St., Alexandria, VA 22314. Friends, it’s Jane.
Every year, Earth Day makes me pause to reflect on what it means to protect our planet and its people. I think about the generations who came before us and those coming next, and what kind of world we’re leaving behind.
**[That’s why this Earth Day, I’m asking every JanePAC supporter to add your name to our Earth Day Pledge to reaffirm your commitment to speaking out, standing up, and _fighting_ to elect the climate leaders who will defend our planet like our lives depend on it. _Because they do._ Join me.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/130042862/616422434/1764043573?refcode=ea.9c79a04d-523f-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&ms=ea.9c79a04d-523f-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxNi8xLzk2NzgyIiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjljNzlhMDRkLTUyM2YtZjExMS04ZWYyLTAwMGQzYTE0YjY0MCIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=06wsKjgVbRYy_DK-CdPIHfCOfRT9JnionK_Q4A0CFFE=&emci=9079a04d-523f-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&emdi=9c79a04d-523f-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&ceid=4823105)**

As I write this message, the Trump administration is pushing a budget that would leave communities across the country in real danger.
They’re colluding to slash billions in funding for the EPA, NOAA, and FEMA — including $15 billion in renewable energy infrastructure — all so corporate interests can squeeze out even more profit.
**You don’t need to be a climate scientist to understand what’s happening, because this crisis is about our values — about who we protect, and who we leave behind.**
We see it everywhere: in the air that’s harder to breathe, in the water we’re told is safe but isn’t, and in the rising cancer and disease rates in communities that have been treated as disposable for far too long.
Powerful polluters want us to feel discouraged. At 88, I tell them, I’m not giving in. I’ve lived long enough to see what’s possible when people like me and you come together and refuse to accept the status quo:
→ Since JanePAC started this work, we’ve elected **over 200 brave leaders** who will stand up to Big Oil and Big Polluters.
→ _Just this month,_ our endorsed climate champions **flipped an entire public utility board** in Arizona. The extreme right-wing organization Turning Point poured buckets of cash into this race to benefit their oily cronies, but an unprecedented number of voters showed up and delivered a clean energy majority on the Salt River Project.
→ Our movement is over **50,000 grassroots donors strong** , alongside everyday people who are protesting, volunteering, and marching to elect brave leaders at every level of government.
_I say this to remind you that hope is alive._
**You have power. I have power. And while I never said this journey would be easy, fighting for each other, for our neighbors, for our children and grandchildren, is a fight worth dedicating my final years to.**
**[So, I hope you’ll join me and take the Earth Day pledge. Every signature helps us build the grassroots movement we need to elect leaders who will be a firewall for our democracy, fight for climate justice, and stand up to Trump and Big Oil.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/130042864/616422436/1764043573?refcode=ea.9c79a04d-523f-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&ms=ea.9c79a04d-523f-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxNi8xLzk2NzgyIiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjljNzlhMDRkLTUyM2YtZjExMS04ZWYyLTAwMGQzYTE0YjY0MCIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=06wsKjgVbRYy_DK-CdPIHfCOfRT9JnionK_Q4A0CFFE=&emci=9079a04d-523f-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&emdi=9c79a04d-523f-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&ceid=4823105)**

clean_body: There's still time to sign the pledge. | Friends, Jane reached out yesterday with something close to her heart, and we want to make sure you didn't miss it. She's asking every JanePAC supporter to sign her Earth Day Pledge. | Thank you for being part of this movement. — Team JanePAC \-----Forwarded message----- Sender: Jane Fonda Date: April 22, 2026 Subject: Friends, will you take the Earth Day pledge with me? Friends, it’s Jane. Every year, Earth Day makes me pause to reflect on what it means to protect our planet and its people. I think about the generations who came before us and those coming next, and what kind of world we’re leaving behind. As I write this message, the Trump administration is pushing a budget that would leave communities across the country in real danger. They’re colluding to slash billions in funding for the EPA, NOAA, and FEMA — including $15 billion in renewable energy infrastructure — all so corporate interests can squeeze out even more profit. You don’t need to be a climate scientist to understand what’s happening, because this crisis is about our values — about who we protect, and who we leave behind. We see it everywhere: in the air that’s harder to breathe, in the water we’re told is safe but isn’t, and in the rising cancer and disease rates in communities that have been treated as disposable for far too long. Powerful polluters want us to feel discouraged. At 88, I tell them, I’m not giving in. I’ve lived long enough to see what’s possible when people like me and you come together and refuse to accept the status quo: → Since JanePAC started this work, we’ve elected over 200 brave leaders who will stand up to Big Oil and Big Polluters. → Just this month, our endorsed climate champions flipped an entire public utility board in Arizona. The extreme right-wing organization Turning Point poured buckets of cash into this race to benefit their oily cronies, but an unprecedented number of voters showed up and delivered a clean energy majority on the Salt River Project. → Our movement is over 50,000 grassroots donors strong , alongside everyday people who are protesting, volunteering, and marching to elect brave leaders at every level of government. I say this to remind you that hope is alive. You have power. I have power. And while I never said this journey would be easy, fighting for each other, for our neighbors, for our children and grandchildren, is a fight worth dedicating my final years to. xx Jane Fonda | = | = = Follow along: | | | | | ---|---|---|---|---|--- Paid for by Jane Fonda Climate PAC, not authorized by any candidate or candidate’s committee. body:
