I’ll cut the
BS and get right to it.

If you care about a Democratic Senate majority, then you need to care
about Mary Peltola. Go support her with a split contribution:
[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260423_2.immLBP&refcode=em20260423-2&t=1002&akid=6278%2E582294%2ERhFe1P ]https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_cp_20260423_2?refcode=em20260423-2

I’ve spent nearly half a century electing Democrats and winning tough
elections across the country, so please take my word for it when I say
this — we gotta get serious about Alaska’s U.S. Senate race.

The truth is: Alaska is the Democrats’ VERY BEST CHANCE to take back the
Senate majority this year.

I won’t sugarcoat it — it’s going to be one hell of a fight. But I know
what it takes to win in “red states” where people think you can’t elect a
Democrat.

So let me say this LOUD and CLEAR: Mary has what it takes. Mary knows how
to win tough races and has won statewide in Alaska before.

But she can’t pull this off without a HUGE team of people who care about
our country behind her.

Billionaires and super PACs will spend UNGODLY sums — I’m talking about
tens of millions — to defeat Mary and take Alaska off the map for
Democrats. Unless we all do everything we can, we’re handing this seat
right back to a corrupt politician, and the Senate majority to DC
Republicans.

It was a selfless move from Mary Peltola to jump into a tough race like
this! But she did it because she understands how high the stakes are for
all of us. Now I’m hoping you do too...

If everyone reading this pitched in a few bucks, we'd make sure Mary has
the resources she needs to take on this fight with room to spare.
Unfortunately, not everyone gives, so it’s that much more important that
YOU do.

Mary is fighting for all of us AND for fish, family, freedom — nothing
wrong with that! I hope you join me and fight for her too.

Thanks as always,

James Carville

body:
This week, Virginia voters approved the redistricting referendum that pushes back against a President who believes he’s “entitled” to more Republican seats in Congress.
| [](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/107757?t=6&akid=23843%2E878179%2EiLcose) We did it.

**This week, Virginia voters approved the redistricting referendum that pushes back against a President who believes he’s “entitled” to more Republican seats in Congress.**

While other states gave in to those demands without letting voters decide, Virginians refused to let that stand.

This victory matters — not just here in the Commonwealth, but across the country. Virginia will play a central role in shaping control of the House of Representatives this November, and I look forward to campaigning with candidates as they earn Virginians’ trust — and their votes.

Now, it’s time to build on that momentum — to support candidates up and down the ballot who will now get to work in the districts the voters approved last night. To do that, we need your support.

[Will you split a donation to help us elect more Democrats, keep the pressure on Republicans, and ensure Virginia stays on track for progress?](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/107757?t=7&akid=23843%2E878179%2EiLcose) If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your split donation between United for Virginia’s Future PAC and VPP will go through immediately: | [CONTRIBUTE $10 »](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/107769?t=8&akid=23843%2E878179%2EiLcose)

Derek,
America is facing a crisis. Prices are skyrocketing, voting rights are being threatened, and systemic injustices occur daily across our country.
Working people deserve better. They deserve lower prices, for their voices to be heard, and to feel safe in their communities.
But Donald Trump and the Republican Party continue to stand in the way.
After he campaigned on lowering costs and saying no to new wars, Trump has betrayed the promises he made to voters, and his failed policies have pushed American families to the brink of financial crisis.
**This is why we need Democrats to win in 2026.**
And here’s my plan for how we do that: Democrats will win when we fight like hell for working people. When we champion bold ideas, even if billionaires don’t like them. When we stand up to the extremism of Donald Trump’s administration.
And we need you to be a part of this fight. So I’ll be answering your questions about attacks from Donald Trump and MAGA Republicans, how we’re fighting back to hold them accountable, and our plans to win big and take back Congress in November. body:
# [](https://act.katieporter.com/go/21486?t=1&akid=41202%2E3422442%2EhNvJBw)
Peter, at last night’s debate, Katie showed up the way she always does—focused on the facts, grounded in reality, and fighting for working families.
Katie gets it. She knows firsthand what it means when rent eats up half a paycheck. She’s lived the struggles of juggling child care costs, rising prices, and making the tough choices of what has to give.
And instead of dodging those challenges, she broke them down the way she always does— _with a plan to actually fix them._
The rest of the stage? Same old story.
A self-funding billionaire trying to buy the seat.
A candidate bankrolled by Big Oil.
And MAGA Republicans pushing Trump’s agenda in California.
**Katie cut through all the noise.**
She’s not taking corporate cash, funneling her own money into her campaign, or bringing an extreme agenda to the table. She has a clear focus: _making California more affordable and accountable to the people who actually live here._
And if there had been a whiteboard on stage, you know she would’ve used it to show exactly who’s benefiting from the status quo. _(Spoiler: it’s not working families.)_
**With less than six weeks until the primary and only two candidates advancing to November’s ballot, we need all hands on deck to make sure Katie is one of them.**

body:
| [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/130044362/616427382/1254288483?refcode=em-header&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDM1MzYiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiN2EwMDc4MjktNTczZi1mMTExLThlZjItMDAwZDNhMTRiNjQwIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=wh0xg0CU3wwYvJAJ8Il_e4wxfqM_ByYpdgi-3TJ_TOs=) Friend, We are only 40 days out from our primary, but that doesn’t mean the work stops in Congress on behalf of Californians. I know the headlines don't always show it, but amid the Trump administration's chaos we're actually moving a lot of important new legislation to deliver progress for Californians. Here are just a few of my most recent efforts:
* I've cosponsored the **Momnibus** , a comprehensive package of bills to keep our new moms healthy and decrease health disparities between women of different incomes and races.

* I'm supporting the **GUARDRAILS Act** to undo the Trump administrations' one-size-fits-all AI regulation plan, to give states the ability to add commonsense safeguards as artificial intelligence advancements continue to shift the playing field for millions of workers and consumers.

* And I'm backing a pair of efforts, the **Transit Workforce Development Act** and the **Modal Parity in Permitting Act** , to make public transit easier to staff and less costly, reducing traffic congestion and giving commuters more options.

I am proud that we have these in the pipeline, and I will work tirelessly through December to see these efforts -- and more -- make it into law. [ ](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/130045040/616429543/693975070?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzAvMS85MTExMyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI5NzRhNTY2Yy01NzNmLWYxMTEtOGVmMi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=mUWGRe2aNek26yBWOmIP39Ed9ohU_fHljNWYnVl76TI=&emci=c84ad7bc-4a3f-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&emdi=974a566c-573f-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&ceid=15820338)

Peter,

Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. has no business being in charge of the Department of Health and Human Services. I have been protesting his appointment from the beginning, and I will never stop fighting back against his dangerous policies. That's why, when he came to Capitol Hill to defend the Trump budget proposal, I grilled him and made him answer for his disastrous agenda.

The budget Trump released, and RFK Jr. supports, would:

❌ Cut the Health Department budget by 12.5%

❌ Cut NIH funding by $5 billion

❌ Cut the CDC's budget by $2.9 billion

❌ Eliminate the Hospital Preparedness Program, which provides aid to hospitals to plan and respond to public health emergencies.

❌ Cancel Title X family planning funding.

How does any of this protect the American people from disease, disasters, or health emergencies? Here's my answer: **It doesn't.**

I ran for Congress because I believe healthcare is a human right. I believe our government should make it more accessible, and should do everything possible to protect its citizens from harm and keep them healthy. As a doctor, I took an oath to do no harm. I think about that every day, because it applies to my work in Congress, too.

Yet, when I look at this GOP budget, I see something that goes against that basic principle. It does harm. It kicks people off coverage. It makes care harder to access. It stops our doctors and scientists from finding cures or treatments for harmful diseases. It prevents our hospitals from having the resources to keep their doors open and protect their communities. And it creates more problems than it solves for people who are just trying to stay healthy and get by. I'm not going to sit back and let that happen without a fight.

clean_body: I just grilled RFK Jr. on some of the Trump administration's budget priorities. Peter, Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. has no business being in charge of the Department of Health and Human Services. I have been protesting his appointment from the beginning, and I will never stop fighting back against his dangerous policies. That's why, when he came to Capitol Hill to defend the Trump budget proposal, I grilled him and made him answer for his disastrous agenda. The budget Trump released, and RFK Jr. supports, would: ❌ Cut the Health Department budget by 12.5% ❌ Cut NIH funding by $5 billion ❌ Cut the CDC's budget by $2.9 billion ❌ Eliminate the Hospital Preparedness Program, which provides aid to hospitals to plan and respond to public health emergencies. ❌ Cancel Title X family planning funding. How does any of this protect the American people from disease, disasters, or health emergencies? Here's my answer: It doesn't. I ran for Congress because I believe healthcare is a human right. I believe our government should make it more accessible, and should do everything possible to protect its citizens from harm and keep them healthy. As a doctor, I took an oath to do no harm. I think about that every day, because it applies to my work in Congress, too. Yet, when I look at this GOP budget, I see something that goes against that basic principle. It does harm. It kicks people off coverage. It makes care harder to access. It stops our doctors and scientists from finding cures or treatments for harmful diseases. It prevents our hospitals from having the resources to keep their doors open and protect their communities. Our right to vote has never been more important. We've never truly faced threats like this before, and with the midterms coming up fast we have to do everything possible to combat voter suppression, register voters, and ensure we actually have free and fair elections to vote in.
We have to stop the opponents of voting rights before we lose our fundamental right to vote. RUSH $35 or more right now to help us fight back >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?refcode=042326_2&amount=35]
Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
“How we have to even run against these people—I won’t say cancel the election, they should cancel the election, because the fake news will say, ‘He wants the elections canceled. He’s a dictator.’ They always call me a dictator."
That was Donald Trump, Team, speaking to members of his party in the House of Representatives on the 5th anniversary of his supporters storming the Capitol to overturn an election he lost.
How many times has Trump "joked" about something he wanted to do before he did it? Too many to count, including weaponizing the government to attack his opponents, his attack on Venezuela, and his attacks on mail-in ballots.
Now, apparently, he's "joking" -- and not for the first time -- about canceling the upcoming midterm elections. It's a threat we all have to take seriously, regardless of party affiliation, because our country was founded on the idea that our voices matter, not just the voices of the powerful.

#
Peter:
There are things that cowards like Trump will never understand.
Service, for one. Sacrifice. Honor. Obligation. Trust.
Giving your life for your friends, your country, or a cause is the most sacred sacrifice you can make. When you join the Military, you accept that you might be asked to make that sacrifice. And you do it, willingly, because you believe the United States of America and our people are worth the risk.
But what about Afghans who believed so much in the United States of America that they put their lives on the line for us? Who went out with Americans every day and had their six in the worst situations you can imagine. We made promises to those people: have our back today, and we’ll have yours tomorrow.
To Trump, their service and sacrifice were worthless. The promises we made and the obligations we have to them mean nothing to him. And as of this week, Trump gave them two options: Go to the Congo, or go back to Afghanistan — where they will be killed.
But VoteVets does not cut and run, and we are not going to abandon our friends. Peter, we need your help. We’re fighting for the Afghans who stood beside us, but we can’t do it on our own.

Angel did everything by the book. He applied for his DACA renewal well in advance, as directed by USCIS. Yet, his renewal application still hasn’t been processed.

clean_body: Send a Letter: Demand USCIS End DACA Delays Now! | | | ** | | "My wife is expected to give birth on May 1 – the same day my DACA expires. " — Angel, waiting since November ** Angel should be focused on his growing family, instead, he faces the looming threat of unemployment and financial instability due to ongoing DACA delays. Will you send a letter to USCIS to demand an end to these delays? | | Peter, Angel did everything by the book. He applied for his DACA renewal well in advance, as directed by USCIS. Yet, his renewal application still hasn’t been processed. Like more and more DACA recipients across the country, Angel has been waiting months to hear back from USCIS. With his work authorization and protections from deportation set to expire in May, Angel — an expecting parent — now risks losing the ability to provide for his family. Unfortunately, this is not an isolated situation. We are facing the most dangerous moment in DACA’s history, and mass delegalization efforts are unfolding before our eyes. In the last year, we witnessed the unlawful detention of close to 340 DACA recipients and the deportation of nearly 100 of them. Now, with USCIS sitting on renewal applications and failing to process them promptly, DACA recipients are at an even greater risk of being torn for their families and communities. Will you take action today to protect Angel and all other DACA recipients facing these growing renewal delays? Together, we can demand the safety and stability that our neighbors need. Peter, these ongoing delays put our entire communities and families at risk. DACA has allowed hundreds of thousands of young people to pursue higher education, secure stable jobs, start businesses, buy homes, and contribute to our communities. From healthcare to education, DACA recipients power every aspect of our daily lives. USCIS cannot sit on renewal applications while our neighbors, teachers, parents, and nurses lose their protections and jobs.** must process renewal applications before Angel and more of our neighbors lose their ability to provide for their families. In unity, Nico and the United We Dream team P.S.: Are you a DACA recipient navigating these delays on your own? We know the emotional toll it can take to make sense of this moment. _**by Ellie Leonard, Blue Amp Media Contributing Editor**_
Since his 2015 Presidential campaign Donald Trump has made no secret about how he feels about mainstream media, otherwise known as "legacy media," outlets like CNN, NBC, CBS, the New York Times, et al. He taught us the phrase "fake news" and often refers to the "lamestream media" and the "failing New York Times." As our country rose up post-George Floyd he sic'd the police on Black Lives Matter protestors and [blamed the media](https://substack.com/redirect/fa6bf55f-87f8-4a38-81c6-a3eb5469e031?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for false coverage, leading to threats against journalists and news agencies.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/c11d0887-16da-4c04-a313-306ccea04037?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Omar Jimenez, a CNN correspondent, and his crew were arrested while giving a live television report Friday morning in Minneapolis as they were covering protests over the death of George Floyd. - Reuters
> _" Sir, I am a journalist covering this," Ms. Davidson turned to walk away, and the officer shoved her in the back, causing her to trip and hit her head against a fire hydrant, she said. She was not hurt, she added, because she was wearing a helmet she had bought while getting skateboarding equipment for a nephew._\- _The New York Times_
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/c11d0887-16da-4c04-a313-306ccea04037?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The photographer Barbara Davidson, on Saturday, while covering the protests.
In 2022, filmmakers [Heidi Ewing and Rachel Grady](https://substack.com/redirect/ca7278c9-8221-406f-9ac2-5eacaa562d2c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), along with journalist and producer [Ronan Farrow](https://substack.com/redirect/6acf5860-c14d-44c1-bedf-53a7bced4ebd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), released "Endangered," a documentary that focused on the threats of violence against journalists in the U.S. and abroad. These were the same journalists that Trump was calling the "enemy of the people" shortly after entering office in 2017.
These weren't hollow threats, and they never have been. In 2002 [Daniel Pear](https://substack.com/redirect/023a44d1-2031-4647-add0-7d70c230650c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)l, an American journalist who worked for the Wall Street Journal, was kidnapped by jihadist militants while he was on his way to what he had expected would be an interview with Pakistani religious cleric Mubarak Ali Gilani in the city of Karachi. He was beheaded.
[Jamal Ahmad Hamza Khashoggi](https://substack.com/redirect/7f410b7c-a5de-4793-bd9e-ad25969f84cf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), a Saudi journalist and dissident who worked for the Washington Post, was assassinated at the Saudi consulate in Istanbul in 2018 by agents of the Saudi government at the behest of the Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman. Donald Trump recently secured a "historic"[ $600 billion investment](https://substack.com/redirect/1769bc5a-a236-4768-9b86-ca732253647b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) commitment in Saudi Arabia. Bin Salman was never charged.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuYmx1ZWFtcC5jby9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.OhEcX7-LCPfAOY6kf_UEa6lwL_pKG6OHw5uk1ckYTgk?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=195049207)
In Russia, there is even a [Wikipedia](https://substack.com/redirect/cc8c81da-99ad-4c62-8c24-de6329bbddc6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) page dedicated to all the journalists killed in the line of duty, many under suspicious circumstances, including multiple contract killings, being beaten to death in the streets, kidnappings, and murder in their own beds.
It isn't uncommon for journalists to be threatened, for their families to be threatened, but being threatened by a Presidential administration is something new. But despite everything, we stood by our news media, who seemed to present a stalwart take on current events.
_Fast-forward to 2026._
We live in a time unrecognizable by our 1990s and early 2000s predecessors, when true and unbiased news media like PBS and NPR are the "enemy," when major journalists are losing their jobs for speaking the truth, when academic institutions like Harvard and Columbia Universities are forced to teach "only just so," and to "only just you, but certainly not you." News media like the Associated Press are [banned](https://substack.com/redirect/dc02f216-6ff7-4ea8-ad89-1bb08f332854?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) from White House press briefings, a public platform meant to be available to the American public in an informative and unbiased setting, for taking a stance on calling the Gulf of Mexico...the "Gulf of Mexico."
[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=3722532&post_id=195049207&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTk1MDQ5MjA3LCJpYXQiOjE3NzY5ODMzNjYsImV4cCI6MTc3OTU3NTM2NiwiaXNzIjoicHViLTM3MjI1MzIiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.0Gha0tXAvgBHoR3ff8yVWR7a1FJiJ2nGqqMK-9thmso)
Major news outlets like the Washington Post, owned by billionaire Trump supporter Jeff Bezos, are [pulling](https://substack.com/redirect/d3d0b5f7-e2d6-46c1-b30a-9f77f84b65cf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) their presidential endorsements (they've endorsed Democrats only since 1976) and declaring that the Opinion section will now cover only "[personal liberties and free markets](https://substack.com/redirect/444f1941-3888-41f1-baa8-4b6375ead4fb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)," leaving viewpoints that oppose these pillars to be "published by other authors." This is a clear stance that aligns with the new administration.
"I am of America and for America, and proud to be so. And a big part of America's success has been freedom in the economic realm and everywhere else." \- Jeff Bezos
Both the Washington Post Opinions Editor, David Shipley, and Associate Editor, David Maraniss resigned immediately. Maraniss had worked at the Post for more than four decades.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/c11d0887-16da-4c04-a313-306ccea04037?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
[Leave a comment](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=3722532&post_id=195049207&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&isFreemail=true&comments=true&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTk1MDQ5MjA3LCJpYXQiOjE3NzY5ODMzNjYsImV4cCI6MTc3OTU3NTM2NiwiaXNzIjoicHViLTM3MjI1MzIiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.0Gha0tXAvgBHoR3ff8yVWR7a1FJiJ2nGqqMK-9thmso&r=1hvr60&utm_campaign=email-half-magic-comments&action=post-comment)
But unfortunately for the American people, money speaks louder than truth, and we're starting to see a shift in the news media that we relied on and trusted. It's not the "fake news." It's not the "lamestream media" or "MSDNC" that Trump touts. And despite what he claims, the New York Times has [more subscribers](https://substack.com/redirect/5c24b450-2ff0-43f8-9436-f849d60ee8cd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) than ever. But in order to stay in that briefing room, in order to please an administration that threatens to pull funds and dismantle journalistic infrastructure left and right, corporate newsrooms are ceding to authority, if only to survive.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/c11d0887-16da-4c04-a313-306ccea04037?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
We saw this with Jake Tapper's recent book _[Original Sin,](https://substack.com/redirect/c69505af-eba2-47a9-b458-d5c53ed9f55f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_ a Tonya-Harding-like kneecap to an administration that let us rest and gave us our jobs and livelihoods back post-COVID. And for what? We just spent four years complaining that the Right wouldn't let the 2020 election and claims of "stop the steal" go. And now here we are, Jake.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuYmx1ZWFtcC5jby9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.OhEcX7-LCPfAOY6kf_UEa6lwL_pKG6OHw5uk1ckYTgk?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=195049207)
We're seeing major journalists of color let go from legacy news media, people like Joy-Ann Reid and Katie Phang at MSNBC, in[ greater numbers ](https://substack.com/redirect/e2c77449-2d11-4492-848e-a2cd01796a9a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)than their white counterparts, as corporations[ dismantle](https://substack.com/redirect/b8862038-7c67-4dff-acc8-ddbe73f1a49f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) their diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI) departments to bootlick Washington.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/c11d0887-16da-4c04-a313-306ccea04037?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Joy-Ann Reid's last show at MSNBC - February 23rd, 2025
Which brings me to the point of this essay, and why we're all here in the first place. In the wave of threats, and ass-kissing, and money, and CEOs guiding the headlines that land on our proverbial breakfast tables on Sunday morning: **we 've all become the journalists we want to see in the world.**
Pardon the cliche: _we became the change._
Now it's all of us, including the major anchors and journalists banished by legacy media--[Katie Phang](https://substack.com/redirect/ff0d76c8-26a9-4bc5-a07b-740664aa5851?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [Jim Acosta](https://substack.com/redirect/4adb1329-a01c-455a-8139-88cde02d9e14?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [Don Lemon](https://substack.com/redirect/3e62f029-fe63-4c7e-ae32-32ca40df8e7f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [Rick Wilson](https://substack.com/redirect/27538297-76e5-40de-aa6b-c17f7259b7fe?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and the [Lincoln Project](https://substack.com/redirect/c6532acc-cff1-4d8f-8e30-6bf765272a3e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [Aaron Parnas](https://substack.com/redirect/f63353cb-121b-414c-82b6-1183bf7a3687?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [Joy-Ann Reid](https://substack.com/redirect/08d0f1d8-7f86-42cb-836e-9834c7eb102b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [Scott MacFarlane](https://substack.com/@macfarlanenews), [Blue Amp Media](https://substack.com/@blueamp), [Wajahat Ali](https://substack.com/@thelefthook), [Zev Shalev](https://substack.com/@zevshalev)--along with authors, media personalities, comedians, politicians, and voices big and small, who are telling the stories. And we're not just telling them, we're actually a part of them, on the ground, talking to people, hitting record, and showing news as it happens.
[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=3722532&post_id=195049207&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTk1MDQ5MjA3LCJpYXQiOjE3NzY5ODMzNjYsImV4cCI6MTc3OTU3NTM2NiwiaXNzIjoicHViLTM3MjI1MzIiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.0Gha0tXAvgBHoR3ff8yVWR7a1FJiJ2nGqqMK-9thmso)
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/c11d0887-16da-4c04-a313-306ccea04037?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Barack Obama attends the 2014 Correspondents' Dinner - Associated Press
This weekend is the annual White House Correspondents' Association Dinner, a lush, black-tie affair filled with the biggest names in journalism, along with a long list of iconic hosts, though notable that only four of those were women. Donald Trump has made it a point to never attend. Though not the only one--Reagan skipped to heal from an assassination attempt--Trump's absence was met with relief, comic and otherwise. This year, however, he plans on attending for the first time, a decision met with ire and a rash of boycott-led alternative events, one of which yours truly plans on attending. The sycophants will stay, adorned in Mar-a-Lago chic, atop My Pillows, and wading through Alex Jones' tears that smell slightly of _onion._
The rest of us? We'll dance a little, eat some tiny food, probably go out for the _real_ drinks somewhere after. But in the meantime, we'll be suspect of Trump's "new media," purposely cultivated and sculpted in the halls of Project 2025. But not because they once weren't telling the truth. Not because what we saw on TV and in the newspaper didn't align with the biggest heads in Washington once upon a time. But because Trump and his cabinet got to all of them, with threats of dismantling the fourth branch of government, the free press, what makes America really great, meant to inform the public and hold those in power accountable.
And that's just what we're doing.

Peter, Dan is a fierce proponent of common-sense gun safety solutions, so this set of endorsements is particularly meaningful. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/130046778/616434882/1903510307?refcode=AU_DSG_EG_GEN_PET_AC_20260423_PM1_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzEvMS85NDA4NyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJmZmNiNmQ5ZS01YjNmLWYxMTEtOGVmMi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=wTxE2UtUb3k4Jg8OqhVKXMnaWgfmradr25NsCBU2d9U=&emci=bca460f2-593f-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&emdi=ffcb6d9e-5b3f-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&ceid=13556823) The advocates endorsing Dan include the Brady Campaign, Jackie Rowe-Adams, who founded Harlem Mothers S.A.V.E. after losing two sons to gun violence, and activist Fred Guttenberg, whose daughter Jaime was killed in the Parkland high school shooting in Parkland, Florida. Dan has been recognized for his leadership alongside community-based organizations on the front lines of the fight against gun violence in NY-10, as well as his proven record advancing gun safety laws. As Vice Chair of the House Gun Violence Prevention Task Force, he has written and introduced major legislation to push forward common-sense reforms, including:
* **Prioritizing Resources for Outreach, Safety, Violence Prevention, Youth Empowerment and Resilience (PROSPER) Act** to invest in community-based organizations that focus on gun violence intervention and prevention
* **Preventing Pretrial Gun Purchases Act** to address flaws in the background check process and keep firearms out of the hands of individuals that courts determine pose a risk of harm to others
* **Firearm Destruction Licensure Act** to ensure firearms intended to be destroyed are not sold and do not fall back into the hands of bad actors
* **Disarming Cartels Act** to curtail the trafficking of U.S.-made firearms and ammunition south-bound over the U.S.-Mexico border

Dan is fighting for strong and uniform federal legislation because our nation’s dangerous patchwork of state gun safety laws means that Americans are only as safe as the weakest state law, not the strongest. Sen. Mark Kelly here.
A few weeks ago, I watched my friend Michael Bennet tear into Trump's CIA director over the handling of Trump’s disastrous, unauthorized war in Iran.

clean_body: | | | Hi Peter, Every election, nearly half a million people trust my team and me with one of their most sacred rights - their right to vote. That’s more registered voters than the entire state of Wyoming. As the county clerk of one of Colorado’s largest counties, I’m running a nearly $20 million organization and am responsible for 114 full-time employees and up to 1,000 temporary election workers in one year. I’ve got hundreds of pages of state election law to interpret and follow, complex equipment and systems to operate, and need to make quick decisions and solve problems under pressure—every day. I’ve already got about 10% of Colorado’s entire electorate looking to me to protect their vote when outside forces try to create confusion or shake trust in our elections. I’m running for Secretary of State because this job, in this moment, is too important to hand to someone who's never done it before. This campaign runs on people like you. If you're able, helps us keep fighting through the primary on June 30. ** ** This is our democracy. We're taking it back. **Trump knows Republicans in Congress will keep enabling him. And with voters ready to hold them accountable in November, Trump and his allies are rushing to rig the rules.**

clean_body: MAGA Republicans will do anything to keep us from voting | = Peter, Instead of focusing on making our lives safer and more affordable, Donald Trump has been obsessed with making it harder for Americans to vote. He has tried to interfere with mail-in voting, empowered loyalists who intimidate election workers, and continued to push the SAVE America Act — a bill that would disenfranchise millions of women and LGBTQ+ Americans. Trump knows Republicans in Congress will keep enabling him. And with voters ready to hold them accountable in November, Trump and his allies are rushing to rig the rules. ******=**** | = The U.S. House has already passed the SAVE Act, and Trump is counting on Republican senators to keep pushing his anti-democratic agenda. At the same time, Republican-led states across the country are advancing their own voter suppression laws, with bills that mirror the SAVE Act and threaten to make it harder for millions of people to cast a ballot. But EMILYs List is working hard to elect Democratic pro-choice women who fight back. We’re supporting battle-tested leaders who are ready to protect voting rights, stand up for their communities, and make sure every voice is heard — no matter how hard Trump and his allies try to silence voters. ****=****** If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue, your donation will go through immediately: = | = ---|--- = | = = | = Thank you, the EMILYs List team P.S. These are people who are living in limbo, many of whom have committed no crime but await a decision that has serious implications for their safety and their future. I met with a gentleman who’s lived in the US for 30 years and is struggling to get the healthcare he needs. And a young gay man from Iran who came to the US, trying to exist safely and honestly as himself. Our movement to transform the Democratic Party for the better has never
been about one single race or candidate.

We may not have won my Democratic primary race for Congress in North
Carolina’s 4th district last month, but we came closer than the pundits
ever thought possible in what ended up being the most expensive primary in
state history.

When I ran against my opponent in 2022, she won by 9 points. This time,
she won by less than 1 percent, even though AI super PACs poured over $2
million into the district to support her while my campaign rejected
corporate PAC funding altogether.

Plus, we helped increase voter turnout among people under the age of 40,
Asian American and Pacific Islander voters, and Muslim voters.

That’s why I don’t see this race as a loss: it’s just one example of the
power and progress we’re building. Together, we ARE moving the needle — we
can’t let losses or despair slow down our momentum.

Right now, we still have 11 more chances to defeat the corporate-backed
establishment and elect Justice Democrats in other primaries across the
country.

Each and every one of them is ready to take on Donald Trump, AIPAC, the AI
and Crypto lobbies, and other corporate super PACs in order to deliver the
bold solutions we need to match the scale of the crises our communities
face.

The more Justice Democrats we elect in 2026, the closer we’ll be to
winning Medicare for All, an end to U.S. funding for genocide, economic

name: Beto O'Rourke
subject: What are young voters thinking?
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Powered by People, [poweredxpeople
body:
# [](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/43706?t=1&akid=240805%2E444211%2E5opdfT)
A sunny, blustery day at the University of Texas at El Paso yesterday with Amy and our amazing Powered by People organizing and volunteer team:
In just over two hours, we registered many new voters, updated and confirmed voter registrations and in every instance agreed to personally stay in touch with each student to answer questions about elections and voting and help ensure they cast their ballot in this year’s elections.
To make this work, we take our time to have open conversations about whatever is on a student’s mind and then ensure we are connecting the dots between what is happening in their lives and in the country with their power to vote.
I met Victoria, a psychology major from Fabens who wants to be a teacher and might get her master's at UTEP after she graduates. I told her she’s taking on one of the most important jobs I can think of at one of the toughest times to be a teacher. This next election could decide whether we have more resources in public schools, less standardized testing and more respect for teachers from our next governor. Amy and I wanted to make sure she knew we are proud of her and have her back.
We also talked to Nicholas who moved to Texas from Pennsylvania a few years ago to attend school here. He thought he couldn’t vote in Texas, but we helped him understand that because he’s a full time resident he’s also an eligible Texas voter. We helped him update his registration from Pennsylvania to Texas so that he can vote in this next election.
When I asked Rafael why he got registered with us today he said, ”Why not? It’s free and maybe I’ll need to use it someday.” He told me he’s pursuing a criminal justice degree and wants to go to the police academy after he graduates. He added that he wants a career where he can help people and keep them safe.
Another student told Amy that he voted for Trump in 2024 “because of crypto” but is unhappy now. He feels that Trump hasn’t followed through on his promises. Amy made sure his voter registration was up to date and promised to stay in touch with him through November. It’s important that he knows that we don’t care who he voted for last time. All that matters is that he makes the right choice this time. And by being open, respectful and taking the time to talk with him, there’s a good chance that will happen.
This is the work that sets us apart. Human to human connection, building relationships of trust that radically increase the likelihood that young people will vote.
**In 2024, we took a voter turnout rate for 18-29 year olds in our program from 37% to 79%.**
[**I’m proud to be a Powered by People volunteer and grateful for everyone who pitches in to make this work possible. Including you! Please donate today to ensure we have the resources to organize all across Texas.**](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/56109?c0=pbp-em-20260423.yBBLrH&refcode=ema20260423-240805&t=3&akid=240805%2E444211%2E5opdfT)

Thank you,
Beto

clean_body: A huge win for Philly, and a big moment for WFP power | | | Dear Peter, We did it. Today is a historic day for Working Families in Philadelphia. For the first time ever, two minority party members passed major legislation on the same day. And not just any legislation, but two of the most significant bills to pass this year. (Photo by Rachael Warriner – @raye-photo on Instagram) Working Families Councilmember Kendra Brooks, alongside Councilmember Rue Landau, helped lead the fight for ICE Out, taking on the fear and harm caused by ICE. Working Families Councilmember Nicolas O’Rourke led Safe Healthy Homes, taking on negligent landlords and unsafe housing. These were real fights. And today, they won. For decades, minority party seats in City Council did not have the power to pass major legislation. Today shows what is possible when Working Families Party leaders are in office, rooted in community and backed by real organizing. And this is exactly what we meant when we said winning the minority bloc for the WFP would change people’s lives. Because these victories didn’t happen by accident. They are the result of years of organizing by immigrant communities, tenant leaders, and grassroots groups across Philly, alongside WFP champions in City Hall who were willing to take on tough fights and stick with them. Here is what these victories mean: ICE OUT puts Philadelphia’s welcoming city values into law by limiting collaboration with federal immigration enforcement, protecting sensitive data, and making clear that city resources should not support ICE’s deportation machine. SAFE HEALTHY HOMES gives the city stronger tools to hold bad landlords accountable, protects tenants from retaliation, supports organizing, and helps stop unsafe housing conditions before they get worse. In solidarity, The Pennsylvania Working Families Party P.S. This is what it looks like when we organize, build power, and win. Let’s keep going. Become a Working Families Party Member! _You're getting this message because you’ve supported good causes and Democratic candidates. We need your support to continue fighting for our democracy. We love having you in our network, but if you only want our most important email updates,[click here.](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/108?t=2&akid=2120%2E259176%2EPod7GP) If you'd like to unsubscribe, [click here.](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/109?t=3&akid=2120%2E259176%2EPod7GP)_

I’m launching something new, and I want you to be a part of it from the jump. I grew up in the kind of small town where everybody knew everybody, everybody’s kids played together, and everybody helped when someone was in trouble. We used to gather together as neighbors to celebrate after football games and graduations. More often than not, our gatherings took place at our local public school. My public school was foundational. It was more than my education and the name on my jersey: it was the place our town came to meet. _Heck, the school was the town._ As I’ve visited small towns in other states over the years, I’ve witnessed a similar sentiment. In red districts and blue, I’ve heard about cherished local schools and how they serve as the cornerstones of their communities. But nowadays I’m seeing a disturbing new trend as those cornerstones are starting to crumble: **Local schools are closing after funding cuts, and they’re followed by other foundational pieces of the community.** The local grocery store? Gone. The local clinic? _Gone._ The job with a decent wage? _Gone._ Everyone and everything seems to be packing up and leaving town. We’re losing our neighbors. We’re losing our communities. And we aren't talking to each other anymore. This is what it looks like to defund and divide America, and it’s because of Republicans like Donald Trump and JD Vance, who are willing to sell out our communities and working families for their own political and financial gain. Why is Elon Musk closing schools in America? Why are we being told that any of the hardships our communities are facing have to do with immigration? The problem isn't your neighbor. It’s the tech bros and billionaires who pay to take turns cosplaying as your Congressman, your Senator, and your President. I think folks in small towns need to band together and stand up for our schools, our jobs, and our communities before they’re all gone. **It’s time to put the power back into the hands of our neighbors, and for Democrats to expand the map. That’s why I’m excited to launch Small Town PAC.** I’m ready to pass the baton and get out on the road to find some teachers, some nurses, some veterans, laborers, and young people in small towns across the country who can represent their communities better than Silicon Valley and corrupt Republicans. We need a new generation of elected leaders in this country – and lord knows the Democrats need some new faces. So let’s go recruit some good people with energy and ideas who actually understand small towns and are willing to fight for them. We’re on a mission to build a party that invests in small towns and delivers a message that resonates with rural America. Tim

# **Ken Griffin threatens to pull $6B NYC project after Mayor Mamdani spotlights his penthouse in pied- a-terre tax video**
Billionaire Ken Griffin signaled **[he may withdraw a $6 billion Midtown development project](https://substack.com/redirect/d1d0038a-3b71-4aec-8e04-89af6d7a78ce?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** after socialist NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani stood in front of Griffin's $238 million Central Park South penthouse in a viral April 15 video announcing a new "pied-a-terre tax" on luxury properties over $5 million whose owners don't live full-time in the city. Citadel COO Gerald Beeson blasted Mamdani in a companywide email, writing "We are about to commence the redevelopment of 350 Park Avenue, creating 6,000 highly paid construction jobs... The project - if we move forward - will entail more than $6 billion dollars of spending."

* **Context** : The directive came one day after Iranian forces fired on three commercial vessels and captured two in the strait.

Trump-aligned billionaire controlling huge parts of the media.

Think about it this way: If there’s one guy making all the decisions about
what gets made in Hollywood, our stories will all start to look the same
and they will align with the taste of that one person.

Take a show like Severance for example.

Severance would've never been made if one guy controlled all of Hollywood.

The original idea was written more than a decade ago. And creator Dan
Erickson was shopping it around, and couldn’t get anyone to bite.

But because there are multiple studios he could have pitched it to, he
kept going. And eventually Apple decided to take a chance on what ended up
becoming a fabulously successful show.

Don’t just take my word for it, here’s what Severance director Ben Stiller
had to say in response to the Warner Bros. Discovery shareholders’
decision this morning:

[ https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/3601?t=1006&akid=2872%2E4032634%2EtxEGi5 ]There are already very few buyers out there. Original ideas and non
legacy IP is extremely hard to get made by a major studio or network. The
winnowing down of choices results in less opportunity for new voices and
diverse viewpoints in what we all are given an opportunity to see. Its
already been challenging for years, and the merger will only make this
worse.

That’s what is at risk here. There will be less opportunities for great
shows, great movies, great stories, great voices, and great art to break
out. Less actors and writers and workers getting a chance to make
something different, something meaningful, something bold.

With this merger, HBO, CNN, CBS News, Showtime, TBS, Comedy Central, TNT,
Paramount+, TLC, HGTV, Nickelodeon, Cartoon Network, Animal Planet, CBS
Sports, Adult Swim, TeenNick, Boomerang, Cinemax, Cooking Channel, Food
Network, Discovery Channel, Science Channel, The CW Network, Travel
Channel, BET, MTV, and VH1 will all combine into one giant company under
David Ellison.

That's just one reason why this is a terrible decision: When it comes to
what stories are told and what news is reported, that’s dangerous for
democracy.

It’s also bad news for fair pricing. If one guy controls all of these
shows and streaming services, he can get you to pay any price he wants to
watch your favorite shows. Because where else are you going to go if you
don’t like it?

But here's the good news: this merger isn't a done deal.

State attorneys general across the country are stepping up to stop this
antitrust disaster. And I’m going to continue to pull every lever I can to
put a stop to this kind of corporate concentration.

Thanks for being part of this,

Elizabeth

How billionaires are ruining sports
# [](https://francescahong.com?refcode=em20260423-2751)
Peter,
Happy draft day. One thing you might not know about me: I'm a huge Packers fan.
[](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260423.2KOMrC&refcode=em20260423-2751&t=1&akid=2751%2E105371%2Et8immY)
When people ask me what democratic socialism looks like, I point them to Green Bay: the only community-owned, publicly-owned team in pro sports. 539,000 shareholders. A board that answers to fans, not a boss. No billionaire owner. Proof that working people can run something better than the billionaires can.
For the first time since 1986, we don't have a first-round pick. So tonight, we get to sit back without fighting about who the Packers take.
Since we've got the night off, I want to talk about what's happening to our team, because it's an allegory for what's happening to working people in this country. Same villain, too: a small class of billionaires rewriting the rules to squeeze everyone else.
Here's the story, in five parts:
* * *
1. **The hero.**

The Packers are the American worker of pro sports. We played by the rules. $579 million in savings. No debt. A foundation that has given away nearly $30 million since 1986 and now reaches 63 of Wisconsin's 72 counties. No owner embarrassing the team (cough, New York Jets, Dallas Cowboys). No holding the city hostage for a new stadium (looking at you, Chicago and Buffalo). No moving to a shinier market (ask St. Louis and Oakland). A team that did it right (and did it without a billionaire's checkbook).
And all of it is under threat.
* * *
2. **The promise.**

An old commissioner named Bert Bell said it best: what makes pro football the best sport in the world isn't the money. It's that come Sunday, any team can beat any other. A team from Green Bay — population 107,000 — can beat a team from Denver owned by the richest family in America.
It isn't magic. It's by design. The salary cap. A draft that hands the worst team the best pick. Revenue sharing that splits TV money evenly among all 32 teams. These rules were written to keep the playing field level, because a level playing field is more fun, more competitive, and better for everyone who loves the game.
Sound familiar? That's the promise of America, too.
* * *
3. **The villain.**

The other 31 owners have figured out how to break the rules. "Void years" let them push real money into fake future seasons and keep their stars locked up forever. The Philadelphia Eagles alone have $452 million stashed in void years. They and the 49ers, using the same tricks, have represented the NFC in five of the last nine Super Bowls. Last spring, Roger Goodell himself questioned the "integrity" of the cap.
And when they can't break the rules fast enough, they cheat. Two weeks ago, an NFL appeals panel ruled that the league itself "improperly" invited owners to collude on holding down guaranteed contracts. The owners beat the case on a technicality. No consequences. This is what billionaires do: they find the loopholes, cheat when the loopholes aren't enough, and then buy their way out of accountability.
* * *
4. **The cash grab.**

Four years ago the Cincinnati Bengals broke a quarter-century holdout and sold the naming rights to their stadium to pay for Joe Burrow's looming contract extension. That was the warning sign. In August 2024, NFL owners voted 31-1 to open the door to private equity, unlocking roughly $500 million in new cash per franchise. Thirty-one teams got that option. Guess which one didn't.
Last month the Miami Dolphins sold one percent of their team for $125 million in a single afternoon. That’s nearly a quarter of the entire reserve fund the Packers took twenty years to build. Our own CEO Ed Policy calls us "an extreme anomaly." But actually, that was by design: In 1960, the NFL wrote a rule into its own constitution (they literally call it the Green Bay Rule!) making sure no other town could ever own a team the way we do. They locked the door behind us. We've been the only ones inside ever since.
* * *
5. **The bill comes to us.**

So what happens to a team that can't tap Wall Street, can't sell a slice to a billionaire, and can't cash in on private equity? The bill lands on the fans.
Ticket prices are going up again — the 16th increase in 17 years. The cheapest seat at Lambeau cost $54 in 2005; today it's $143, and a family of four at one game is most of a paycheck. The Packers just sold the naming rights to Titletown's football field. Ed Policy warns we're "soon to be the only stadium without naming rights." This math ends, eventually, with a corporation's name on Lambeau Field. And we all know it.
That's the trap. A league where billionaire-owned franchises hoard stars through cash tricks. Where the cap is an accounting exercise. Where the one team actually owned by working people has to charge working people more just to stay in the conversation.
* * *
And folks, this is Wisconsin. We were told that if we worked hard and kept our heads down, a little piece of the American dream could be ours. But an unelected class of billionaires keeps rewriting the rules in ways that make our lives less stable and stack the deck for the people who already have everything.
As a fan, I hope the NFL enforces its own salary cap. But I can change the rules of the game here in Wisconsin, because that's what governors do: level the playing field for everyone who lives here. That's why I'm running. Because there shouldn't be one set of rules for the rich and powerful, and another for the rest of us.
Something to think about as you watch the draft tonight.
**[And if you're feeling generous, chip in $5.20 for our 52nd overall pick.](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260423.2KOMrC&refcode=em20260423-2751&t=2&akid=2751%2E105371%2Et8immY)**
**[Donate $5 ››](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260423.2KOMrC&amount=5&refcode=em20260423-2751&t=21&akid=2751%2E105371%2Et8immY)**
Go Pack!
\- Fran

| | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. ## Virginia Redistricting Update
---
| |
---
The American people want a representative who works hard, shares their values, works across the aisle, and gets things done for their constituents. By the grace of God, we've been able to help a lot of people. As a Navy SEAL veteran, serving in Congress is how I continue service to our great nation. When I was in the General Assembly, my team and I were able to pass bills every year where every Democrat and every Republican voted yes. At the same time, I received the highest award for conservatism. One of my favorite bills my team and I passed in the General Assembly continues to save lives by allowing school nurses in elementary, middle, and high schools to store and administer naloxone to prevent death by overdose.
Fast forward to my time in Congress, today, I received the highest award for conservatism in Congress. My team and I have been serving together for 16 months, solving problems, helping people get home from dangerous countries overseas, and getting things accomplished in the district for the people we represent. Most recently, we passed two bills in the span of three weeks. One of those bills was the Wintergreen Emergency Egress Act. This was a 25-year problem the last six congressmen tried to solve, but were unable to get across the finish line. My incredible team and I found out about this issue and by working across the aisle got this bill passed in the House in just six months.
I was elected to represent everyone in Virginia's Fifth Congressional District, and Tuesday's election does not change that.
Thank you to all the volunteers and everyone else who put in countless hours putting up signs, making phone calls, and more to help us get out the NO vote.
We expect the Virginia Supreme Court to do its constitutional duty and uphold the lower court ruling on the redistricting referendum as unconstitutional and illegal. Until then, I will continue to campaign and represent the amazing people of the current Fifth District where my incredible team and I so far have helped return over eight million dollars back in to their pockets owed to them by the IRS, Social Security, Veterans Administration, and more. It is an honor to serve you and your family. God bless America, and God bless our great Commonwealth.

name: Squad Victory HQ
subject: We refuse to accept this as the status quo
body:
[ https://act.squadvictoryfund.com/go/18910?refcode=em20260423-2192-foote&t=1001&akid=2192%2E342411%2EBSajxa ]Squad Victory Fund

Peter,

The Squad Victory Fund exists because we know real change doesn’t come
from the top down. It comes from people coming together to demand
something better.

This is a movement rooted in justice, equity, and the belief that
everyone, regardless of zip code, race, or income, deserves a fair shot at
opportunity, safety, and dignity.

But right now, communities across this country are being pushed to the
brink. Families are navigating economic instability. Public health systems
are still under strain. And systemic racism continues to shape access to
housing, education, and opportunity in ways that cannot be ignored.

At the same time, Trump and his MAGA allies are working to drag this
country backward — rolling back rights, attacking vulnerable communities,
and trying to silence the voices of those who speak truth to power and
refuse to stay quiet in the face of injustice.

We are not accepting that as the status quo.

Our progressive champions — Alexandria, Ayanna, Ilhan, and Rashida —
continue to fight for bold, progressive change every single day. They
aren’t backing down, and neither are we.

This movement is only as strong as the people who power it: organizers
organizing in their communities, volunteers showing up day after day, and
grassroots supporters who refuse to give up on a better future.

We’re building a people-powered movement rooted in collective action and
the unshakable belief that progress is possible when we stand together. If
you’re ready to be part of that fight, now is the time to step up.

[ https://act.squadvictoryfund.com/go/19213?c0=svfem-20260423-movement.lq7Q4t&refcode=em20260423-2192&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1002&akid=2192%2E342411%2EBSajxa ]Will you power this movement forward with a $3
grassroots donation to the Squad Victory Fund today? Every contribution,
no matter how big or small, makes a difference.

[ https://act.squadvictoryfund.com/go/19213?c0=svfem-20260423-movement.lq7Q4t&refcode=em20260423-2192&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1021&akid=2192%2E342411%2EBSajxa ]Contribute ››

In solidarity,

Squad Victory HQ

This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com. Email is the most important way for us to reach you about opportunities to get involved. If you need to remove yourself from our email list, click here to unsubscribe:

You can unsubscribe from this mailing list at any time:
http://act.squadvictoryfund.com/cms/unsubscribe/unsubscribe/?akid=2192%2E342411%2EBSajxa

Paid for by The Squad Victory Fund, a joint fundraising committee authorized by Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez for Congress, Ilhan for Congress, The Committee to Elect Ayanna Pressley, Rashida Tlaib for Congress, Courage to Change, Inspiring Leadership Has a Name PAC, Power of Us PAC, and Rooted in Community Leadership PAC.

In addition to what’s legally required, The Squad Victory Fund does not accept contributions from: (1) corporations, associations, or their PACs; (2) individuals registered as federal lobbyists or under FARA; (3) from the PACs, lobbyists, or SEC-named executives of fossil fuel companies; or (4) from the Fraternal Order of Police.

Contributions or gifts to The Squad Victory Fund are not tax deductible.

Contributions to The Squad Victory Fund will be allocated equally among: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez for Congress, Ilhan for Congress, The Committee to Elect Ayanna Pressley, Rashida Tlaib for Congress, Courage to Change, Inspiring Leadership Has a Name PAC, Power of Us PAC, and Rooted in Community Leadership PAC.

Any contributor may designate their contribution for a particular participant. The allocation formula above may change if any contributor makes a contribution that, when allocated, would exceed the amount that the contributor may lawfully give to any participant.

After contributing to The Squad Victory Fund, you will automatically be signed up to receive email updates from Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez for Congress, Ilhan for Congress, The Committee to Elect Ayanna Pressley, and Rashida Tlaib for Congress. You may of course opt-out by unsubscribing at any time.

To contribute via check, please address to The Squad Victory Fund c/o MBA Consulting Group, PO Box 15845, Washington D.C., 20003

Email us: info@squadvictoryfund.com

Peter ,
For years, Republicans have tried to make voting harder through voter ID laws, attacks on mail ballots, voter roll purges, and endless conspiracy theories about fraud.
Now the far right is pushing the next step... and it might be the most alarming yet.
A new report lays out how MAGA influencers, conservative activists, and Pete Hegseth’s own pastor are openly floating ideas like repealing women’s right to vote, letting the male “head of household” cast votes for his family, and limiting the vote to property owners.
These ideas sound absurd until you remember that voter suppression almost always starts as a fringe talking point before it becomes a bill, a court case, or a Republican campaign promise.
After all, this is the party that still believes the lie that Donald Trump won the 2020 election and even went as far as to stage a coup on the Capitol. Anyone who thinks this could never be a mainstream MAGA plan hasn’t been paying attention.
And this is exactly why GOTV PAC focuses on turnout.
When Republicans try to shrink the electorate, our job is to expand it. We reach the voters who are most likely to be ignored by traditional campaigns, especially low-propensity Democrats who already share our values but may not hear from anyone before Election Day.
Because the answer to a movement that wants fewer people voting is not panic. It’s more contact and turnout work. Ensuring more voters know their power and use it.
We’re going to keep doing that work everywhere we can, and with your help, we’ll make sure Democrats turn out in numbers this November that Republicans can’t deny. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/gotvpac2026?refcode=em04232026]

I won't beat around the bush: Is saving this reliably red Senate seat worth it to you? Is it worth donating just $10 or even $5 right this very moment? We've relied on Texas to help us flip the Senate, the House, and the White House countless times over the last 50 years, and my stomach is in knots seeing the Democrat U.S. Senate nominee's first quarter fundraising numbers. Inaction today spells certain doom for our glorious Texas. I 'm pleading with you to wake up and stop pretending like someone else is going to step in and make sure we don't lose the crown jewel of Republican states for the first time in 38 years. I’m no stranger to being underestimated. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/130050988/616448947/274653739?refcode=AU_MTH_FR_TAN_GEN_AC_20260423_PM1_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDYvMS84OTA0NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI4ODFiMDMzYi02YzNmLWYxMTEtOGVmMi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=2RmfjtQWWHq9atfPKkomLPYfKn68rUyw-64c059eOL4=) As a child with severe chronic asthma, I was constantly told what I wouldn’t be able to do. _And I proved them wrong._ [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/130050989/616448948/274653739?refcode=AU_MTH_FR_TAN_GEN_AC_20260423_PM1_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDYvMS84OTA0NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI4ODFiMDMzYi02YzNmLWYxMTEtOGVmMi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=2RmfjtQWWHq9atfPKkomLPYfKn68rUyw-64c059eOL4=) When I first ran for school board in 2004, I was up against a crowded field — including two incumbents — and people told me I had no chance of winning. I became the youngest person to be elected to the Minneapolis Board of Education and won the most votes. _I proved the doubters wrong._ [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/130050990/616448949/274653739?refcode=AU_MTH_FR_TAN_GEN_AC_20260423_PM1_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDYvMS84OTA0NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI4ODFiMDMzYi02YzNmLWYxMTEtOGVmMi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=2RmfjtQWWHq9atfPKkomLPYfKn68rUyw-64c059eOL4=) In 2015, I became only the second Native American woman in the Minnesota House when I won my special election and _proved the doubters wrong._ So now, when I hear folks say we can’t compete with the avalanche of GOP cash coming our way I know that we will do what we always do,_we’re going to prove the doubters wrong,_ _again_. There will always be doubters, but I’ve always chosen not to listen. I keep my head down, get the work done, and deliver for the people of Minnesota. clean_body: I’m no stranger to being underestimated. = As a child with severe chronic asthma, I was constantly told what I wouldn’t be able to do. And I proved them wrong. = When I first ran for school board in 2004, I was up against a crowded field — including two incumbents — and people told me I had no chance of winning. I became the youngest person to be elected to the Minneapolis Board of Education and won the most votes. I proved the doubters wrong. = In 2015, I became only the second Native American woman in the Minnesota House when I won my special election and proved the doubters wrong. So now, when I hear folks say we can’t compete with the avalanche of GOP cash coming our way I know that we will do what we always do,we’re going to prove the doubters wrong, again. There will always be doubters, but I’ve always chosen not to listen. clean_body: I see this every day from inside the Senate. | | | Peter, I’m going to be straight with you: This may be the most important message you read today. I’m serving in the United States Senate right now, and the truth is this: without a Republican majority, we cannot pass laws that protect our faith, our families, or our freedoms.Everythingslows.Everythinggets blocked. The 2026 Senate majority could come down to a SINGLE seat, and Mike Rogers is in the fight of his life to win it . When I ran, no woman had ever been elected to the U.S. Senate from Alabama. Plenty of people doubted I could win. They were wrong. That experience taught me something important: when the pressure is highest, real leaders don’t back down.They fight harder, Peter . That’s exactly where Mike Rogers is right now. Mike is an Army veteran and former Congressman who came within 0.3% of winning his Senate race in 2024. He’s already faced the toughest attacks the Left could throw at him, and came incredibly close before. With the right support, Make no mistake: if we lose this seat, Democrats WILL take control of the Senate. And when they do, they WILL push policies that undermine our faith, weaken families, and erode the freedoms we’re fighting to protect. I see this every day from inside the Senate. To do my job fighting for you and protecting our values, I NEED a Republican majority in the Senate. That’s why this race matters, and why we need a fighter like Mike. He’s an Army veteran who stands for our values, and he’s ready to fight like hell to keep the Senate Majority in Republican hands because America is worth fighting for. But he can’t do it alone, Peter. Democrats are pouring MILLIONS into this race. It will be one of the most expensive and closely watched races in the country. . If you’re able, please consider chipping in today: If Mike doesn’t have your vote, I understand. . Thank you for taking the time to read this and for caring about what’s at stake. U.S. Senator I didn’t run for Senate to sit quietly on the sidelines. I’m a mom, a conservative, and a proud Alabamian—and I came to fight for the values that make America strong. Faith. Family. Freedom. The Left is doing everything they can to tear it all down. But I didn’t come to Washington to play games. I came to fight for the people who feel forgotten, overlooked, and ignored. From securing the border to protecting our kids and defending our way of life—I’m in this for the long haul. This fight isn’t easy, but it’s worth it. And I’m not going anywhere.
